News.title: Fresh CCTV released in frantic search for girl, 16, who vanished nearly a month ago
News.content:
FIND HER Fresh CCTV released in frantic search for girl, 16, who vanished nearly a month ago

FRESH CCTV images have been released in a desperate search for a girl who went missing nearly a month ago.

Jessica, 16, from Tameside, was last seen 17 days ago after travelling to Piccadilly Gardens in Manchester.



Cops previously thought Jessica had been seen at Granada Park, in Denton, at 7.15pm that evening.

But in a major update officers have now know Jessica was travelling to Manchester’s city centre as she was spotted getting off a bus at Piccadilly Gardens at 8.25pm.



She had boarded the bus from the Windsor Road area of Denton, GMP said.

The new CCTV images show Jessica on a bus and carrying two bags, wearing a black zip-up top and sandals.

Police previously disclosed that Jessica had no access to a phone or money.

She has been classed as a “high-risk” missing person, with multiple appeals to find her issued in recent days.

Anyone with information that could help police find Jessica is urged to come forward as soon as possible.

A Greater Manchester Police spokesperson said: “We are desperately doing everything we can to locate Jessica who has been missing from Tameside since Thursday, July 16 2026.



“She was last seen getting off a bus at Piccadilly Gardens at around 8.25pm, having travelled from the Windsor Road area of Denton.

“We and her family are incredibly concerned about her and want to make sure she is safe and well.”

Cops have urged the public to keep their eyes peeled for Jessica and to share any information they may have on her whereabouts.

You can contact the police on 0161 856 9325 quoting reference number MSP/06GG/0001262/26.

The force added: “We have also launched a public portal for anyone with any information including CCTV, mobile phone or Dashcam footage, to submit in the hope that anything we can gather as much information as we can which will help us locate Jessica and bring her home safely.”

News.title: ‘People smugglers’ arrested as Moroccan migrants caught trying to enter Spain on jet ski after 60k breached Ceuta border
News.content:
A SUSPECTED trafficker has been arrested after trying to smuggle migrants from North Africa into Spain on jet skis.

Another alleged criminal was captured while piloting a speedboat with 11 Moroccan nationals.



The migrants aboard the jet skis and speedboat reportedly entered the Spanish enclave of Ceuta from Morocco.

Now, the suspected people smugglers had been trying to sneak migrants across the 11-mile stretch from Ceuta into Spain.



Making the journey between Ceuta and Spain on a jet ski takes between 30 and 45 minutes in good weather conditions.

Cops have previously broken up gangs using jet skis to smuggle people and discovered that they charge nearly £3,500 per migrant.



They are also used to run cannabis across borders.

Typical jet skis can reach around 65mph, making it possible for traffickers to cross several times in a single day.

The Spanish Civil Guard intercepted the journey and seized the speedboat, towing it back to port in Ceuta.

The captain of the motorboat is under the age of 18, according to local residents.



The nationalities of the two suspects have not been made public and it is not clear if they are in jail or have been released on bail.

It comes after a wave of 60,000 migrants flooded the Spanish enclave on Thursday night.

At least 72 people were killed in the surge.

Most swam around the border from Morocco after seeing social media posts claiming they would be offered Spanish citzenship if they made it to Ceuta.

The sudden surge to the Spanish enclave has sparked warnings of increased illegal migration into the UK.



Shadow Foreign Secretary Priti Patel has claimed some of those who made it into Ceuta would “inevitable try to make their way to the UK.”

Reform leader Nigel Farage reacted to the border crisis by warning: “Thousands of young men, lots of them dangerous, will be heading towards Calais and our country. It’s time to wake up. This is a battle for our civilization.”

As of Friday evening, more than 48,000 people had returned to Morocco, said Spanish officials.

News.title: Mum of Henry Nowak’s killer put in ‘female Monster Mansion’ holding Lucy Letby, Constance Marten & Sara Sharif’s stepmum
News.content:
THE vile mum of Henry Nowak’s killer Vicrum Digwa has been moved onto a “cushy” jail unit at the “female Monster Mansion” housing Lucy Letby and Constance Marten.

Kiran Kaur – jailed for hiding the knife Digwa used to stab student Henry, 18 – has been switched to notorious Unit 4 at HMP Bronzefield for her own safety.



The prison wing houses killers including ex-nurse Letby, 36, baby death aristocrat Constance Marten, 38, and Sara Sharif‘s killer stepmum Beinash Batool, 31.

Kaur, 53, was previously held on a separate block at Bronzefield, Surrey, but was switched to Unit 4 after being sentenced for assisting an offender.



The wing is “enhanced” where lags get extra privileges – meaning there is less violence as cons fear being moved if they attack anyone.

But a source said: “It stinks that Kaur has been moved there. It is one of the most comfortable wings on the prison estate and they’ve done it so she is safe.”



Unit 4 holds long-term, life-sentenced and enhanced-level prisoners and is known for having better conditions compared to other prison wings.

Inmates are said to have access to a hair and beauty salon while cells have their own showers, TVs and DVD players, reports the Daily Star.

A source told the outlet that the unit was “cushty” and claimed Kaur was sent there after she “pretended” she couldn’t speak English.

It comes as The Sun can reveal killer Digwa – who murdered Henry in Southampton and claimed he had been the victim of a racist attack – is still in a segregation unit at Frankland Prison, Durham as he fears mixing with other lags on a wing.

He is said to be “literally shaking with fear” behind bars after becoming a target for some of Britain’s most dangerous inmates.



Digwa, 23, knifed 18-year-old Henry Nowak five times in a random street attack as the teen made his way home from a night out.

The killer then filmed Henry as he tried to flee over a fence while leaving a trail of blood and shouting “I’m going to die”.

When cops arrived, Digwa accused the teen of making racist remarks – causing officers to place Henry in handcuffs as he lay dying.

Shocking video footage revealed the moment Digwa told his mother to take the knife he used to kill Henry away from the crime scene.

Taken on Digwa’s phone, which is pointed at the ground, he can be heard speaking to Kaur in Punjabi, asking her to remove the knife.



Kaur was jailed last month for three years for assisting an offender.

Digwa himself was jailed for life with a minimum term of 21 years on June 1 for the murder of Henry.

Sentencing Kaur, Judge William Mousley KC said the mum’s actions “added to your son’s pretence that he had done nothing wrong and that he was the victim”.



He continued: “A responsible parent would have challenged their son over their actions and encourage them to do the right thing.

“Instead you took the knife home and put it with a larger collection of ceremonial and other weapons in your son’s bedroom.

“That would have helped to conceal what it had been used for.”

The Sun has previously reported on how Lucy Letby and murdered Sara Sharif’s stepmother Beinash Batool had struck up a friendship in the female “Monster Mansion”.

We reported how both inmates – who have “enhanced” privileges – spend hours trying to out-manoeuvre each other into checkmate on the jail unit.



At Christmas, inmates were invited to an opera workshop with festive goodies laid on behind bars.

Letby was sentenced for the murders of seven babies and the attempted murders of seven more while a neonatal nurse at the Countess of Chester Hosptial in 2015 and 2016.

She was senteneced to 15 whole-life orders – but her case is at the centre of a high-profile miscarriage of justice campaign.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Batool was jailed in December 2024 for the horrific murder of her tortured stepdaughter.

Others on the unit included aristocrat Constance Marten, 39 – jailed over the on-the-run death of her baby daughter – and killer mum Sian Hedges, 29.

News.title: One in 10 Brits haven’t taken a bath in more than a decade, new study finds
News.content:
NOSE YOUR LIMITS One in 10 Brits haven’t taken a bath in more than a decade, new study finds

ONE in 10 Brits haven’t taken a bath in more than a decade, according to research.

A poll of 2,000 adults found 51 per cent agreed bathing has fallen out of fashion, with 20 per cent of those who don’t indulge regularly blaming a lack of time to relax.



While 33 per cent are too impatient for the time they take to run.

Other reasons for the decline in popularity included not wanting to use too much water for either cost-saving (24 per cent) or environmental (22 per cent) reasons.



But 48 per cent are just “shower people” who don’t like the idea of hanging around in a warm puddle.

The phenomenon goes beyond preference though, as 18 per cent of people don’t even have a bath in their homes.



Recent studies, such as the Shower Market Report have seen an uptick in renovations being done to remove unused baths, even if they were included in the first place – in favour of walk-in showers, wet rooms, or additional floor space.

This data is backed up by the 21 per cent who have had a tub removed from their homes in a quest to create a larger shower space (43 per cent), modernise their bathroom (42 per cent), or convert to a walk-in shower (31 per cent).

Others (14 per cent) made this renovation specifically to help reduce their water usage.

A spokesperson from leading smart Pay-As-You-Go energy supplier Utilita, which commissioned the research to support its award winning High5 tips series , including to keep showers to four minutes maximum, said: “Once a staple of the home, baths seem to have fallen out of favour for many across the UK.



“From homes getting smaller to costs getting higher, there are numerous reasons why this might be.

“But however you choose to clean and refresh, the most important thing is being conscious about your water usage, for the sake of both your pocket and the planet.”

While bathing is clearly on the outs, 30 per cent went so far as to say it will become completely extinct within the next 10 years.

Reasons for baths falling out of fashion range from busier lifestyles (55 per cent) and smaller homes (53 per cent) to rising costs of both energy (55 per cent) and water (70 per cent).

Higher prices likely also form part of the reason 77 per cent describe themselves as conscious of the amount of water they use.



Nine in 10 (90 per cent) also take active steps to reduce their consumption, such as only filling the kettle with the water they need (55 per cent), collecting rain to water plants (29 per cent), limiting hosepipe use (29 per cent), and re-using grey water (13 per cent).

More than a third (35 per cent) have also swapped baths for showers for this precise reason, according to the OnePoll.com data.

Three quarters (76 per cent) also believe this makes a difference to reducing their water bills, with 77 per cent saying the same about taking shorter showers.

The average shower now lasts for nine minutes, but when asked what could be done to reduce this even further, costs were the key motivator.

Three in 10 (32 per cent) said knowing exactly how much money they could save or seeing real-time costs per minute (30 per cent) would convince them to cut down.



Utilita’s spokesperson added: “Swapping baths for showers or reducing the time spent doing either can be a small, easy change that can have a lasting impact.

“It’s great to see so many people are already doing this and have faith in the money they could save on their bills from this simple act.

“And no matter whether you prefer baths or showers, everyone can be a water-savvy person.”

News.title: Five dead and 41 missing after ferry catches fire sparking huge search and rescue mission for 250 stranded passengers
News.content:
FIVE people are dead and another 41 remain missing after a ferry carrying hundreds went up in flames off the coast of Indonesia.

A frantic search and rescue operation is underway with crews deployed on emergency vessels to evacuate the boat.



Chaos struck just hours after Mutiara Sentosa 2 departed a port in Surabaya heading for Makassar.

The ferry was carrying around 250 passengers and crew when the blaze erupted close to Madura island.



Shocking footage shows huge plumes of thick black smoke billowing from the top decks.

Terrified passengers jumped overboard, plunging into the sea to escape the flames.

Nanang Sigit, head of the Surabaya Search and Rescue Office, said: “TB Hasnur 26 and the British Mentor are assisting in evacuating passengers who jumped from KMP Mutiara Sentosa 2.

“Four vessels are now alongside the ferry.”



Most of the ferry was engulfed by the inferno, reports said, forcing passengers onto the bridge and the bow to await evacuation.

Authorities said around 200 passengers had been transferred to rescue vessels.

But 40 people remained onboard at around 11.20am as the fire raged inside.

Images show dozens of survivors wearing life jackets packed into boats as they were driven to shore.

The Surabaya Search and Rescue Office was alerted to the fire at 8.24am.



According to Nanang, the ferry was located about 19 nautical miles from Buruan Sapudi Island.

The captain reported the fire between 6am and 7am before communication was lost.

Nanang said the first ship to reach the stricken ship was forced to turn back because it was carrying flammable cargo.



The cause of the fire remains unclear.

It comes after a pregnant woman was among five dead after a ferry erupted in flames off the Indonesian coast last year.

Chaos erupted as terrified passengers strapped on life jackets and leapt off the burning KM Barcelona VA.

Authorities said 284 of the passengers and crew were rescued, and no injuries were reported.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A brave survivor filmed himself clinging to a baby in the sea after leaping off the burning ferry.



Commander of the Indonesian Fleet Command Denih Hendrata said three navy ships had been deployed.

News.title: Zelensky’s ‘WW3’ masterstroke? How drawing Iran into Ukraine war could spell doom for Putin’s invasion…with Trump’s help
News.content:
UKRAINE has given Vladimir Putin a major headache by dragging Iran towards the Ukraine war and giving Donald Trump a reason to tighten the screws on Moscow.

Kyiv’s daring drone strike on an Iranian military cargo ship in the Caspian Sea sparked threats from Tehran that may see two conflicts collide.



As opposing allies become drawn into the conflict, experts say Volodymyr Zelensky could seal a World War Three-style showdown to defeat Putin.

Ukraine’s attack on Iran targeted a supply line that the Kremlin has used to import lethal Shahed suicide drones and missiles from the pariah state since 2022.



It marked the first direct clash between the two nations since Russia‘s invasion.

Iran claimed that the vessel was purely commercial and vowed to respond – declaring that the “hostile and criminal” strike “cannot go unanswered”.

But the move could position Ukraine as an ally to Trump in a shadow war against the anti-Western axis.

Foreign policy experts say it could be a high-risk strategy from Zelensky to convince the US president to tighten the screws on Putin.



Dr Richard Arnold, an Eastern European security expert, told The Sun: “Ukraine wants to be in Trump’s good books.

“Trump has shown a lot of frustration with Nato allies who have not come to his aid and it appears Zelensky’s almost trying to say, ‘look, we’re the better partner than your Nato partners.'”

Dr Arnold suggested that Ukraine may be positioning itself as an anti-Iran shield.

Zelensky is “trying to build up the image of Ukraine as the Israel of Eastern Europe,” he said.

Since the outbreak of the Iran war, Kyiv has provided the US with technical expertise to counter the Iranian Shahed drones – weapons that Russia has used extensively to attack Ukrainian cities.



Professor Mikhail Alexseev, a political science expert at San Diego University, said it is a calculated move to drum up support in Washington.

He told The Sun: “For Ukraine, it’s very important to have the United States on its side. Ukraine needs to show Trump that it has the cards.

“This is one of the cards – that it can help the United States prevail in achieving objectives in Iran, with having its nuclear program suppressed and ensuring security in the Strait of Hormuz.”



After attacking the Iranian ship, Zelensky revealed that Russia has been feeding Tehran satellite intelligence to strike American military bases in the Gulf.

He said: “There is a clear correlation between Russia’s satellite imagery of these sites and Iranian strikes – both before the attacks, in preparation for them, and afterward, to assess the damage inflicted.”

The Ukrainian leader promised to share the intel with Washington – but made a point of aligning the US and Ukraine’s ambitions.

He said: “None of us in the world should turn a blind eye to one very simple fact: evil always seeks ways to make things worse and spread further.

“Russia must be stopped. This war must be stopped. Pressure on the aggressor must work.”



Zelensky’s bid to win over the White House appears to have been paying dividends.

At the Nato summit in Ankara, Trump said he would grant Ukraine the game-changing licence to build state-of-the-art Patriot missile interceptors.

It may prove decisive in dismantling Putin’s last major advantage – Russia’s missile capabilities – with Zelensky claiming the “battle in the sky” will be key to winning the war.



Ukraine has been desperate to bolster its rapidly-depleting stockpile of interceptors amid a slew of deadly ballistic missile attacks on Kyiv.

But the growing alignment between Washington and Kyiv could prompt Putin to pile more support behind Iran and deepen the conflict.

Arnold said: “It gives Russia a powerful incentive not to let Iran fail. That’s how this war becomes almost unstoppable.”

He warned that “escalation of the conflict is far more likely than resolution”.

It comes after Nato scrambled fighter jets after a Russian Kh-101 missile smashed into Poland this week.



Washington previously warned that Putin could be plotting an armed attack on Poland to test the international alliance – as it faces calls to fight back.

Alexseev said that the conflict has been moving in the direction of an all-out global war for some time.

He explained: “Russia’s war against Ukraine has been not just a small regional war, but a much broader international conflict from the get-go.



“We have seen the way that Russia aligned its forces, counting on economic support from India and China, on military support with Shahed drones and ballistic missile technology from Iran, with troops and artillery ammunition from North Korea.

“Wars, particularly involving great powers, rarely can be contained on a regional scale.”

As the Ukraine and the Iran wars collide, experts fear allies on both sides could be dragged into World War Three.

Alekseev said: “We’re moving into the kind of environment where conflict is normalised, everybody retaliates, nobody takes a step back, and we’re approaching the kind of conditions that led to larger wars in the past.”

Arnold warned: “There are a lot of voices, unfortunately, saying we are in what is called the pre-war period.



“Scholars have been noting for some time how similar the world of today looks to the world before World War One.”

Meanwhile, the strain on Putin’s weakening war machine has backed the dictator into a corner.

Kremlin Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said the country is enduring a “very difficult period”, and Putin recently made the rare admission that the country is “struggling” with an energy crisis.



Dwindling manpower has seen Moscow deploy 30,000 North Korean troops and parliament allow even the most hardened criminals to be drafted.

Arnold said: “Russia is facing a manpower problem, simply because it hasn’t got enough people to power its industries and fight the war in Ukraine.”

Russia has suffered 1.4 million casualties since invading Ukraine in 2022, including an estimated 500,000 deaths.

A report last month showed that the average life expectancy for Russian troops on the frontline was just 20 minutes.

Zelensky warned that Putin may declare another full-scale mobilisation after September’s elections and Moscow struggles to sustain the war effort.



The move may be a response to the recent endgame blitz that Ukraine has targeted at key Russian infrastructure over the summer.

Zelensky said Putin will only end the fighting once he is beaten.

The Ukrainian president told Sky News: “What we tried to do to make this challenge also for Russians; otherwise, they will not feel that the war is everywhere…

“That’s why we started to do everything to respond and to bring this war back to Russia, where it came to us… and that’s why we started our mid-strikes and deep-strike operations, just to respond.”

Alexseev stressed that while cracks are appearing on the Russian front, Ukraine’s Western allies must do far more to force Putin to backtrack.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

He said: “Putin is very stubborn and Russia is a big, resourceful, rich country. The pressure signals moves in the right direction, but it’s not yet enough.

“A lot more has to be done, both in terms of supporting Ukraine with greater capabilities and in terms of repositioning globally against Russia.”

News.title: I spent years finding long-lost mum & made shock discovery that cracked 50-year cold case… truth was right under my nose
News.content:
DESPERATE for answers about his biological mother, Richard Hanchett had no idea his quest would solve one of the greatest murder mysteries that had baffled cops for nearly 50 years.

During efforts to find the woman who gave him up for adoption, Richard, unravelled the shocking truth that his mum had been right under his nose the whole time.



It turned out she was at the centre of the decades-long cold case.

“I had no idea in the world where it was going to go or anything,” Richard Hanchett told Oxygen.com.



In 1974, an auburn haired woman’s mutilated woman was discovered abandoned in the windswept dunes of Cape Cod.

Lying on a beach towel was the naked body of the woman whose skull had been savagely crushed.



Her hands had been severed in what investigators believed was a calculated attempt to prevent identification through fingerprints.

A young girl was out walking the family dog with her parents when she stumbled upon the woman’s lifeless body sprawled among the sand dunes.

Her pale, motionless form lay exposed on the beach, her pink-painted toenails still eerily neat against the sand. Beside her head sat a pair of jeans and a blue bandana.

Despite years of detective work, forensic examinations and countless public appeals, the victim’s identity remained maddeningly elusive.



The case was dubbed “The Lady of the Dunes” in every newspaper in the city that Richard, from the Detroit suburbs, had walked past and gazed at – never knowing that the woman was his biological mother.

The mystery snowballed into one of America’s defining cold cases, generating a maze of theories and suspected links to notorious killers.

But nothing was ever linked back to the nameless woman whose story remained a mystery for nearly five decades.



The mystery body was exhumed on three occasions, 1980, 2000 and 2013.

Clay composites were made of her head – hoping someone in the world might recognise her.

Then, a potential breakthrough came from an unlikely source – Joe Hill, the son of literary giant Stephen King.

He had followed the case closely and become fascinated by the mystery surrounding the woman’s identity.

In 2015, Joe was watching a 40th anniversary screening of Jaws, filmed in Massachusetts during the summer of 1974 – around the same time the Lady of the Dunes was believed to have been in Provincetown, roughly 100 miles from the production.



Just over halfway through the film, something on the screen stopped him cold.

Among the crowds was a young woman who looked remarkably like the composite image of the unidentified victim Joe knew so well.

She appeared to be around 30, with her hair pulled back in a bandanna and blue jeans on – details that immediately caught his attention.

Joe wondered whether he had stumbled across the woman’s last known sighting, captured entirely by chance on film.

Jaws screenwriter Carl Gottlieb later heard about Hill’s discovery and dug out the production records.



The timing appeared to fit, with the woman visible in Scene 130, around 54 minutes into the film, as crowds boarded a ferry.

There was, however, no record of her being a hired extra for the scene.

She may simply have been a tourist caught in the background as she boarded the ferry.

Still, the footage offered investigators an extraordinary possibility – that the woman on screen was the Lady of the Dunes, travelling towards Cape Cod in the final days before she was killed.

In 2018, Richard’s submitted his DNA to Ancestry.com and matched with his living cousin, revealing the name of his mother to be Ruth Marie Terry.



But neither Richard nor the cops knew that Ruth was dead, or, crucially, that she was “The Lady of the Dunes”.

Years on, as technology advanced, investigators used the bone samples collected after exhumation used them for DNA testing in 2022.

Her profile immediately flagged genetic ties to living relatives in Tennessee and Michigan – where her son Richard Hanchett’s DNA was registered.



Genealogists used these distant and close cousin matches to build out her family tree, confirming her identity as 37-year-old Ruth Marie Terry within a few months.

Weeks before the FBI called Richard to confirm the Lady of the Dunes was in fact his real mum, he recalled having dreams about her murder.

“I was having nightmares for about three weeks… and I didn’t know what it meant; I couldn’t figure it out,” Hanchett claimed.

After hearing from the cops, he said the meaning behind his dreams became “very apparent.”

He even described to agents that he kept “seeing this guy hit a woman in the back of the head and crush her skull,” details that piqued the agency’s curiosity.



The discovery transformed Richard from an ordinary adoptee searching for his roots into the son of one of America’s most recognisable unidentified murder victims.

Back in 1958, Ruth had given birth to a son while living in Michigan.

Unable to raise the baby herself, she arranged for him to be adopted by her workplace superintendent, Richard Hanchett Sr., and his wife.

Richard said he had “such a happy life” with the couple that adopted him but could not shake off his curiosity about his real mum.

Once Ruth’s identity had finally been restored, detectives rapidly reconstructed the final chapter of her life.



Their investigation led them to her husband, Guy Rockwell Muldavin, an antiques dealer and convicted fraudster who also used several aliases, including Raoul Guy Rockwell.

The couple had married only months before Ruth vanished in 1974.

Cape and Islands District Attorney Robert Galibois announced investigators had concluded that Muldavin was responsible for Ruth’s murder.



Because Muldavin died in 2002, he will never face trial.

Family members recalled that Muldavin exhibited possessive behavior around Ruth.

When Muldavin returned alone after their summer 1974 trip driving her car, he told her family that he and Ruth had gotten into a fight during their travel and that she had gone missing.

He also told other witnesses that she had died.

Her family never saw or heard from her again.



Police also established that he disposed of her possessions, emptied her accounts and liquidated her belongings shortly after her disappearance.

The findings echoed disturbing events from years earlier.

In 1960, Muldavin had been the prime suspect in the disappearance of his second wife, Manzanita Rockwell, and his teenage stepdaughter, Dolores Mearns, in Seattle.

Human remains were later discovered in a septic tank at his property, although he was never convicted over those deaths.

Investigators have said Muldavin repeatedly preyed upon women, exploiting relationships for financial gain before disappearing from their lives.



With Ruth’s identification and the conclusions of the investigation, one of Massachusetts’ oldest unidentified homicide victims has finally reclaimed her name.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

For Richard, the search that began with a longing to know his mother ended by exposing the devastating truth behind one of America’s darkest unsolved killings.

The mystery that haunted generations has at last been given an answer.

News.title: Top cop accused of having sex with two junior colleagues was paid £55k after he quit the force
News.content:
SEX PROBE Top cop accused of having sex with two junior colleagues was paid £55k after he quit the force

A FORMER chief constable accused of having sex while on duty was paid more than £55,000 after quitting the force, it has been revealed.

Scott Chilton resigned with immediate effect following 33 years of service after the police watchdog announced he was under investigation for gross misconduct over alleged sexual relationships with two junior colleagues.



Now, figures have revealed that Mr Chilton received £55,154 as “compensation for loss of employment” following his sudden departure from Hampshire Police.

The sum is understood to relate to a payment in lieu of working his three-month contractual notice period.



The former top cop is accused of having a sexual relationship with a more junior officer while serving as chief constable.

He is further alleged to have had sex with another junior officer while on duty earlier in his policing career.



Details of the allegations emerged after the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) launched a gross misconduct investigation into his behaviour.

The misconduct notice alleges that Mr Chilton abused “his position for a sexual purpose having a sexual relationship with an officer while chief constable and failed to declare this relationship”.

He is also accused of failing to “disclose a previous sexual relationship with another officer during the application process to become chief constable”.

Investigators allege that he “repeatedly and dishonestly” denied the allegations when questioned by senior figures in the Office of the Police and Crime Commissioner.



Hampshire Police and Crime Commissioner Donna Jones met Mr Chilton at her home in November 2024 to discuss his future.

The pair met again at police headquarters on February 12, 2025, before Ms Jones made a formal referral to the IOPC on February 26, 2025.

Mr Chilton is due to face a formal misconduct hearing in October, where the allegations against him will be formally considered.

Explaining why the former officer received the substantial sum after resigning, a police spokesperson confirmed the payment details.

“On Mr Chilton’s resignation, he received £55,154 as Pay in Lieu of Notice (as opposed to him working the three month period in his contract),” the spokesperson said.



A former detective, Mr Chilton spent around 33 years in policing after joining the service at the age of 18.

He landed the top job in Hampshire in February 2023, transferring back to the force after serving as chief constable in Dorset from August 2021.

Following his sudden resignation, Alexis Boon has replaced Mr Chilton as Chief Constable of Hampshire and Isle of Wight Constabulary.

The Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) are investigating the claims.

Director Derrick Campbell, previously said: “Any allegations involving officers abusing their position for a sexual purpose are taken extremely seriously.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“At the end of our investigation, we found evidence to indicate that the former chief constable’s conduct may have breached the police standards of professional behaviour.

“We have decided that Mr Chilton should face a disciplinary hearing. It will now be for the PCC to arrange these proceedings in due course, where a disciplinary panel will then determine, based on the evidence, whether the gross misconduct allegations are proven.”

News.title: Great white shark weighing 100 STONE spotted off Florida tourist beach showing unusual behaviour
News.content:
Great white shark weighing 100 STONE spotted off Florida tourist beach showing unusual behaviour

A huge great white shark was spotted off the coast of a popular Florida beach but scientists revealed this predator has gone against the grain, surprising them with his behaviour

View 2 Images A 1,400lbs great white shark nicknamed Breton was near a popular Florida beach (Image: Ocearch / SWNS)

A massive 13ft long great white shark weighing a whopping 100st was unexpectedly spotted off the coast of Florida, near a popular beach, as the predator surprised scientists with its behaviour.

‌



The 1,400lbs (100st) creature, nicknamed Breton, has been heading south this summer despite other sharks swimming north for cooler waters and more food. Each summer, great whites usually follow the same pattern and travel from the Gulf of Mexico and along Florida's coast to migrate up the Atlantic towards Canada - but Breton's movements have been a complete break from the rest of the pack.

‌



On July 25 the apex predator was tracked "paving his own path down south" and his tracker "pinged" near the popular tourist spot of Daytona Beach.

‌



Pregnant woman saved from shark attack by hero fiancée as he is rushed to hospital READ MORE :

View 2 Images Breton being examined by scientists (Image: Ocearch / SWNS)

The shark's tracker, which was being monitored by OCEARCH, transmitted a locating "ping" signal when his dorsal fins is exposed above the water's surface for long enough. John Tyminki, a data scientist at the non-profit, revealed that seasonal food sources and cooler water temperatures are part of why sharks migrate north during the summer.

He added that this was not the first time this particular shark has shocked scientists. Tyminki said: "Breton always surprises us. He was tagged September 11, 2020, so it is going on nearly six years.

‌



"Our estimate is that he has travelled more than 52,000 miles. He has gone in shore and off shore and because he is a mature male he is showing us useful patterns. Right now he is off the East coast of Florida as of July 25 in the Gulf stream.

"Usually our understanding is that great white sharks at this time are in Canada or Cape Cod because of the seals and the water temperature. Yet Breton has gone somewhere different.

"We wondered, isn't the water temperature too warm for him to be there? His tag also sends us temperature data and where he is, it is on the warm side for white sharks, at 80 degrees Fahrenheit."

Article continues below

Scientists revealed they do not know why Breton has chosen to go against the grain. Tyminki added: "He is probably spending his time a lot deeper down where the water is colder. Our guess is that Breton is following seasonal schools of fish. He continues to surprise us and is amazing."

This comes after a huge shark, thought to possibly be a great white, was spotted circling a boat in Portugal on July 25. The predator was seen around two nautical miles off the coast of Nazaré - an area famous for surfing.

A video of the terrifying moment was uploaded by a boat-tour company with the caption: "This morning, between São Martinho do Porto and Nazaré, about 2MN from land, we spotted a large shark during a walk."

News.title: 'I died 3 times in Army bomb blast but I'd still let my son join up'
News.content:
Lying in the dust of Helmand Province, Lance Corporal Martyn Compton thought he was taking his last breath. His armoured vehicle had been ripped apart by a roadside IED, then rocket-propelled grenades turned it into an inferno. Engulfed in flames, as he crawled for cover, he was shot in the right leg twice, shattering his femur.

This weekend, it’s the 20th anniversary of the devastating ambush that left the Household Cavalry soldier with burns to 75 per cent of his body. Yet, as his son, Archie, approaches his 16th birthday in November - Martyn’s age when he joined-up - he says he’ll support him if he wants to become a soldier.

Martyn says: "People expect me to say I'd do everything I could to stop Archie joining the Army. That's honestly not how I feel. Of course I’d be terrified. I know exactly what can happen. I've lived through the worst. I’ve seen the true horror of war. I also know what the Army gave me. It gave me confidence, discipline, lifelong friends and opportunities I'd never have had anywhere else."

Maverick Daily Mirror hero who risked her life to entertain WWII frontline soldiers READ MORE :

Forgotten icon who changed London's Tube forever but critics wiped her name READ MORE :

View 6 Images Martyn Compton with his wife Michelle, son Archie and daughter Coral, 20 years after he was horrifically injured in Afghanistan (Image: Philip Coburn/Daily Mirror)

‌



He continues: “It gave me an inner self belief and resilience that gave me the fight to stay alive. For that reason, if Archie came to me tomorrow and said, 'Dad, I want to join the Army,' I'd tell him I support him. Of course I'd worry. But I'd also be incredibly proud of him."

Martyn believes too many young people are growing up without direction. He says: "We've got a generation who feel a bit lost. The defence of our nation and patriotism are dwindling, which is tough to watch when you’ve served your country. One million young people who’re not in employment, education or training.

“I worry about this generation and what the future holds for them. It’s created a nation that feels divided. There seems to be less care and respect for one another and less direction. I hope this new Government will take more steps for them. Because of this, I support National Service, including for my own children. Many countries around the world do it. Why can’t we? Some form of National Service would give you purpose. It teaches teamwork, respect and responsibility. Those lessons stay with you long after you've taken the uniform off."

‌



View 6 Images Martyn and Michelle Compton before he was injured (Image: © Press People)

On August 1, 2006, Martyn's regiment was travelling in convoy in small tanks, heading to support Danish forces in Helmand Province. The lead vehicle crossed a narrow bridge safely. As Martyn's vehicle followed, gunfire erupted. He says: "The bullets started smashing into the vehicle. As I reversed, an IED exploded and ripped our Spartan vehicle apart. Every man travelling with me lost their life. I was the sole survivor.”

Leaving him no time to think, insurgents fired rocket-propelled grenades. Martyn says: "One hit the deck. One hit the engine. Suddenly, I was completely engulfed in flames. My adrenaline kicked in. Pure instinct to survive took over. I could smell burning, but didn’t even register it was my own flesh. The pain hadn’t kicked in. My one thought was ‘I must get out of here.’”

Dragging himself from the burning vehicle, he rolled across the sand to extinguish the flames. He says: "The heat was unbelievable. I just knew I had to put the flames out." Still under heavy enemy fire, he crawled towards cover, saying: "As I reached a wall I was shot twice in my right leg.

‌



"My strongest memory isn't the pain, it was thinking, 'that's it. I'm not going home.' Then everything stopped hurting. I genuinely believed I was slipping away." He survived because fellow soldiers Andrew Radford and Mick Flynn repeatedly exposed themselves to enemy fire to reach him. Martyn, 42, of Hastings, East Sussex, says: “They did the bravest thing I've ever seen. They fought through enemy fire to get to me. They risked their own lives to save mine. "

View 6 Images Martyn and Michelle Compton on their wedding day (Image: © Press People)

In the ensuing 20 years Martyn’s had more than 500 painful skin grafts, reconstructive surgery and rehabilitation. In his most recent operation last year, surgeons operated on one of his eyes. Scars cover most of his body, but he says: "I've got used to living with them. People still stare at me sometimes in the street, or when they first meet me. I can still feel awkward and self-conscious. But my scars don't define me - my amazing family does."

Finally when home, looking unrecognisable, Martyn had a frank conversation with his then girlfriend, Michelle. He says: "I told her I'd understand if she wanted to leave.” Instead, they’ve just celebrated their 18th wedding anniversary with their children, Archie, 15, and Coral, 14, and their dog Lola, four. He says: "Michelle has been beside me through every operation, every setback and every bad day. Even in the darkest moments, there is light.This experience taught me what real love is. She's walked every step of this journey with me."

‌



Another source of support has been Prince William, who he met while he was in hospital recovering in 2007. His champion ever since, Martyn says: “Prince William was serving in my regiment when I returned injured from Afghanistan. I was still in a wheelchair when he came to see me, privately. He stopped by one day and simply said, 'If you ever need anything, let me know’. He’s been true to his word ever since.”

View 6 Images Michelle and Martyn with their dog, Lola (Image: Philip Coburn/Daily Mirror)

Military duties meant William couldn't attend Martyn and Michelle's wedding in July 2008, but he sent a personal message wishing them every happiness. Years later, they were invited to William's wedding to Catherine at London’s Westminster Abbey on April 29, 2011. Martyn says: "He spotted me in the Abbey straight away. Michelle and me were sat in front of the Beckhams and opposite Elton John. As Prince William walked down to take his place at the altar, we were the first ones he spoke to. He grinned and said ‘hello Compo, how are you doing?’ It was a surreal moment, to sit with all these famous people around me. That's the sort of man he is.”

Despite the decades of pain and endless operations Martyn has enjoyed some amazing experiences - including being photographed by rockstar Bryan Adams. He says: “I remember being asked to pose for Bryan, he had a converted warehouse on the Thames. Archie was just a baby and ,as we walked in ,there was a guy making a cup of tea. I didn’t think much of it and I said, ‘can I just pop in here and change Archie’s nappy? He said ‘yes of course’. Then Michelle said, ‘that’s Bryan Adams.’ His photoshoot with me ended up in the National Portrait Gallery.”

‌



Still living with PTSD, Martyn admits: "I still get nightmares. But I've learned how to cope. "Veterans' charities, especially Pilgrim Bandits, have been a lifeline. They are a small amazing charity who helped me massively and they are making a difference to the lives of injured veterans. They understand what we've all been through."

View 6 Images Martyn Compton is now fundraising to help struggling veterans (Image: © PRESS PEOPLE)

And he’s about to take on a challenge for Pilgrim Bandits, to raise money for struggling veterans. He says: “I am going to travel through the jungle of Vietnam with other injured veterans. For me, to share some camaraderie with others who have faced hell, is cathartic.” Every August 1, Martyn raises a glass to the men who never made it home. He says: "You never forget them. For most people Afghanistan is something from the past. For some of us it's still part of everyday life."

Reflecting on what an Army career would mean, should Archie choose one, he says: "The scars remind me every day what the Army took from me. But they also remind me what it gave me. So, if Archie chose that life, I'd stand beside him. Not because it would be easy. But because I’d be proud of him. Every time I look in the mirror I’m reminded of that day - but also I’m reminded of how precious life is.”

‌



To donate to Martyn’s venture for other servicemen see: www.justgiving.com/page/martyn-compton

News.title: Telling clue about Meghan and Harry's changing relationship after 'great escape'
News.content:
Telling clue about Meghan and Harry's changing relationship after 'great escape'

Prince Harry and Meghan Markle appear to be eyeing up a return to the royal fold, in some capacity. But it remains to be seen how realistic a reversal of Megxit really is

View 7 Images Harry and Meghan's star in the US is fading, experts have warned (Image: Aaron Chown/PA Wire)

Prince Harry and Meghan Markle have a new goal. With their popularity dwindling in the US, the couple are said to be determined to mend their broken relationship with the royal family - beginning with their recent meeting with King Charles.

‌



It was the first time that the monarch had seen his grandchildren Archie and Lilibet since 2022, and Meghan's first return to Britain since the late Queen's funeral.

‌



But what is the motivation behind their renewed efforts to fix those burned bridges? Reports suggest that the couple are still pushing for a 'half-in, half-out' position within the family - something the late Queen expressly forbade.

‌



It's believed that the couple want to carry on making money to fund their lifestyle in Montecito, but also to be treated as 'working royals' when in the UK while doing charity and public speaking events.

View 7 Images The Sussexes are said to be looking for a return to the royal fold, in some capacity (Image: Netflix)

Some critics believe Harry is making his move now while he has the ear of the King - and before his older brother Prince William takes power. Certainly, there is no love lost between the siblings, and there will surely be no place for the Sussexes within the royal fold when he becomes king.

‌



Others argue the couple need their connection to the royal family in order to stay relevant. "There is definitely a feeling in his camp that he has started to feel a bit unwelcome in America," a source close to Harry told the Mail. "That has been an increasing and significant shift in sentiment, a feeling that the American dream might not be all that it was cracked up to be."

The couple's axed or reduced deals with Spotify and Netflix hint, some royal experts say, at their star fading in the States. But it's not only their American dream that has transitioned - so, too, has their relationship, according to another source.

"I don't think he's ever wanted to be estranged from his family. I think when he was madly in love with Meghan he could be blind enough to choose her," they told the publication. "Now things are different, and the veil is lifting."

‌



7 View 7 Images Sources close to the couple say their relationship has shifted into a new stage (Image: meghan/Instagram) 7 View 7 Images The couple are all loved-up on Instagram (Image: meghan /Instagram)

At the start of their romance, Harry positioned himself as Meghan's protector and defender. Most notably, he condemned the racism being directed towards her on social media in a public statement - which has since been removed from the royal family's website.

‌



He then went one step further. During the couple's now-infamous interview with Oprah Winfrey post-Megxit, they claimed that an unnamed member of the royal family expressed "concerns" about how dark their son Archie's skin might be before he was born. It caused an unprecedented crisis within the family.

Harry later denied accusing the royal family of racism during an interview with British journalist Tom Bradby ahead of the publication of his memoir Spare. But the hits kept on coming, with Harry going on to allege physical fights with William, describing a falling out between Meghan and Princess Kate, and calling Queen Camilla "the villain" and "dangerous".

View 7 Images The Sussexes reunited with King Charles earlier this month (Image: GETTY)

‌



After quitting royal life, the Sussexes were just as inseperable - embarking on joint work ventures and events to fund their new life in Montecito. Most of these projects proved to be lucrative because of their links to the royal family. But when that well dried up, they seemed to professionally separate.

Meghan launched American Riviera Orchard - now As Ever, and threw herself into her lifestyle series, With Love, Meghan, which has since been cancelled. Harry, meanwhile, focused on his charity work, though that too has proved difficult with a bitter boardroom battle at Sentebale - the charity he co-founded in honour of his late mother Princess Diana - leading to his resignation and huge heartache.

Now the couple are said to be struggling to bring any of their projects to fruition, with experts having long suggested that their connection to the royal family is what gave them real relevance.

‌



Some royal watchers have mused over whether this may have put strain on their marriage. Meghan has long been seen as the instigator - and the orchestrator - of Megxit. But sources close to Harry now say that Meghan is 'fully behind' his plans to return to the royal fold, in some capacity.

View 7 Images Meghan is reportedly 'fully behind' Harry's plans (Image: ANP/AFP via Getty Images)

The Sussexes have been married for eight years - and they have certainly gone through some major changes in that time. From being feted as a breath of fresh air for the royal family, to quitting royal life, moving to California, and becoming hugely polarising figures, they have had a rollercoaster ride. Not to mention the fact that they have become parents in that time, to Archie and Lilibet in 2019 and 2021 respectively.

‌



There's no sign of trouble in paradise from the outside, with Meghan regularly posting loved-up snaps with Harry and their children. Just last week, the Duchess shared sweet photos of the couple giggling together while on their summer holiday in Portugal.

But just like any relationship, things look different nearly a decade into marriage. Relationship expert and dating coach Hayley Quinn, tells the Mirror: "In the first flurry of love, people can often end up putting their partners on a pedestal. They can idealise their partners, and want to do anything for them. They may even attempt to show their love through overcoming adversity. In the case of Harry and Megan, Harry showed his loyalty to Megan during Megxit when the couple left their royal duties for a life in the USA.

View 7 Images The Sussexes with their children, Archie and Lilibet (Image: @meghan/Instagram)

‌



"Since then, their plans have had to survive contact with reality. This includes disappointing ratings for their podcasts and TV shows. Additionally, the couple are parents to two young children, which as every parent knows brings its own set of stresses and strains.

"It's believable that their once great escape no longer feels so gilded and the couple may be experiencing strain on their relationship. Recently there seems to be more attempts from Harry to reconnect with his family, which may suggest he's had a change of heart about the importance of his wider social relationships outside of his marriage."

Hayley continued: "Ultimately, all relationships can't survive on adrenaline and desire alone. Many formerly passionate relationships have to contend with maintaining desire after the honeymoon period has ended.

Article continues below

"Part of this work is a mental readjustment that your 'roommate years', where you are focused on coparenting, are a natural progression not a problem in your relationship. It's also totally normal to discover that your partner has some flaws, that perhaps you didn't notice in the beginning, nobody is perfect.

"The other part of the work is to find healthy outlets to keep the novelty alive and to spend quality one-to-one time together. For famous couples with demanding schedules, this may be easier said than done."

News.title: Josh Kerr jokes 'pressure is for tyres' as he celebrates Commonwealth Games gold medal in Glasgow
News.content:
Josh Kerr jokes 'pressure is for tyres' as he celebrates Commonwealth Games gold medal in Glasgow

The world record holder relaxed after he won the One Mile race in three minutes 54.12 seconds, ahead of rising Australian star Cameron Myers, who took silver, while Kenya’s Timothy Cheruiyot won bronze

View 3 Images Josh Kerr with his Commonwealth Gold one mile medal (Image: Owen Humphreys/PA Wire)

Josh Kerr joked that 'pressure is for tyres' today as he celebrated a turbo-charged Commonwealth gold in front of his home crowd in Glasgow.

‌



The world record holder won the One Mile race in three minutes 54.12 seconds, ahead of rising Australian star Cameron Myers, who took silver, while Kenya’s Timothy Cheruiyot won bronze. The field also included fellow Scot Jake Wightman, who finished fifth.

‌



Kerr, 28, explained that he trained in the stadium as a teenager, learning how to 'win and lose'. Kerr joked that he did not feel the pressure after his world record mile two weeks ago adding: "Pressure is for tyres."

‌



View 3 Images Josh Kerr wins Commonwealth Gold in front of his home crowd (Image: Getty Images)

Gianni Infantino planned to bank £22million salary PLUS bonuses before FIFA ploy collapsed READ MORE :

On being named as 'King of Scotland,' he added: "Stop it. It was incredible, the fans packed the stadium and I knew that I had to seize the moment. I learned my craft there in Scotstoun stadium, it is where I learned how to win and lose. Winning in front of the home crowd was just incredibly special."

He thanked his childhood coach and said: "I am very, very proud to be an Eric Fisher athlete." Kerr said that he hoped to set an example for young athletes. Eric, who is still coaching in Glasgow, said he was very proud to guide both Kerr and Wightman when they were teenagers.

‌



A raucous home crowd roared with delight as Kerr took the lead in the final lap and crossed the finish line comfortably ahead of his rivals. The First Minister presented the athletes with their medals at a ceremony later in the evening.

View 3 Images Josh Kerr after his Commonwealth Gold (Image: Martin Rickett/PA Wire)

Mr Swinney described Scotland’s performance in the Games as “truly historic and inspiring”. He said: “We’ve enjoyed some truly historic performances from Team Scotland at the Commonwealth Games – in swimming, bowls, athletics to name a few.

‌



“I hope that the Glasgow Games will encourage future generations to continue and build on this legacy of sporting greatness.”

The 11-day sporting extravaganza will end with tonight's closing ceremony at the Ovo Hydro. The slimmed down version of the Commonwealth Games has saved the British taxpayer around £600m - and may have secured the future of the event.

The total public funding allocated to stage the Birmingham 2022 Commonwealth Games was £778 million. Birmingham City Council and local partners contributed £184m (25%) of that total.

Article continues below

The remaining 75% (£594m) was covered by the UK central government. Organisers of Glasgow 2026 say that using hotels instead of a village, along with smaller arenas and fewer events, cut costs to around £160m. Victoria in Australia was due to host the event and paid £199m to pull out which has funded Glasgow 2026 without taxpayers paying a penny.

Phil Batty, the chief executive of Glasgow 2026, said: “This definitely isn’t the last hurrah for the Commonwealth Games. What we’ve seen is a wholesale shift in what the Commonwealth Games needs to do to sustain itself, not just through 2030, but through 2034, 2038 and beyond."

News.title: New housing development completed with help of 'Walter the robot' as UK aims to build 1.5million more homes
News.content:
New housing development completed with help of 'Walter the robot' as UK aims to build 1.5million more homes

A development built with the the help of a cutting-edge robot has just been completed. Housing chiefs say it is a ‘defining moment for the future of the construction industry’.

Andy Burnham discusses plans for new technical subjects

The race to build 1.5m new homes across the UK could be won with the help of a robot called 'Walter'.

‌



A pioneering housing development built with the help of the cutting-edge technology has just been completed. Housing chiefs say it is a ‘defining moment for the future of the construction industry’.

‌



The government aims to build 1.5m new homes in England over a five-year period, translating to an average target of about 370,00-a-year. JT Lifestyle Homes has now officially finished the development in Thornley, County Durham. It was the first in the UK to use a wall-laying terra-based robot - nicknamed WLTR or ‘Walter’ - to place bricks with speed and ultimate precision.

‌



View 3 Images A pioneering housing development has just been completed with the the help of a Robot called Walter

Miracle dog found alive after spending 29 days trapped under earthquake rubble READ MORE :

Dr Jan Telensky, founder and CEO of JT Lifestyle Homes, hopes the technology will help address the labour shortage in the construction industry. Dr Telensky said: “There is currently a severe shortage of bricklayers in the UK, along with a wider skills shortage across much of the construction industry.

"With ambitious housing targets we need to get to grips with new technology to help us meet the demand for new homes - and fast. We have been incredibly impressed with how Walter has helped us speed up build time.

‌



View 3 Images The cutting-edge Robot called Walter at work

"Using a robot which works in all weathers also meant we knew what the output would be, come rain or shine. Walter picks up and lays the bricks with precision, enhancing the overall build and literally taking the heavy lifting out of the job. It is operated by experienced trades professionals who can monitor the build and deal with the more intricate aspects of the job.”

Now finished, the Maple Close scheme boasts both cutting-edge exteriors and modern interiors. All homes are equipped with solar panels on their roofs and the homes are built with specialist clay blocks that are lower in carbon than other materials and have enhanced thermal performance.

‌



View 3 Images The Robot Walter has just completed a housing project in Co Durham (Image: JT Lifestyle Homes)

They also use less water, are lightweight and generate no mortar waste. Any damaged blocks can be crushed and reused as hardcore on site.

The UK is in the grip of a "housing crisis" and new PM Andy Burnham wants to deliver "the biggest council house building programme since the post-war period" - but has not as yet revealed any detailed plans. Keir Starmer pledged £39bn to fund the construction of 300,000 new "social and affordable houses" over the course of 10 years during the 2025 Spending Review, and said this money would "reinvigorate" council housebuilding.

Article continues below

That would equate to around 30,000 new homes a year, but the majority of those were expected to be social housing constructed by not-for-profit housing associations using government grants. Council house construction has collapsed across England since the 1980s and much of the stock of local authority homes has been sold off with the right to buy scheme of the Thatcher government.

News.title: Inside King Charles' tough challenge as pivotal royal aide to leave Palace after two decades
News.content:
Inside King Charles' tough challenge as pivotal royal aide to leave Palace after two decades

EXCLUSIVE: The King and Queen's principal private secretary Sir Clive Alderton is to leave his post after two decades working for the Royal Family - and thoughts have turned to his replacement

View 4 Images King Charles with his private secretary Sir Clive Alderton (Image: PA)

He has quietly been one of the most influential figures in the Royal Household for more than two decades - b ut now the King’s right-hand man, Sir Clive Alderton, is set to step down from his role next year.

‌



This means Charles and Queen Camilla are now left with the tough task of finding a new principal private secretary. The royal aide played a pivotal role in steering the couple through Charles’ accession to the throne and has been on hand to support the King through the likes of state visits and more personal matters, earning him the nickname from Prince Harry as 'the wasp'.

‌



King Charles pestered by troublesome fly as he and Camilla begin to wind down for summer break READ MORE :

View 4 Images The King and his right-hand man at Royal Ascot earlier this summer (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Whoever replaces him, when he leaves around the time of his 60th birthday next May, will become the King’s most senior courtier and the person whom he can call on for advice and act as a bridge between Crown and government. Royal expert Jennie Bond spent 14 years as the BBC’s royal correspondent, closely following the then Prince Charles and getting a glimpse into the inner workings of Buckingham Palace.

And she told the Mirror exactly what Sir Clive’s successor will need to tackle one of the demanding jobs working for the King. She explained: “I think most long-serving private secretaries become part adviser and part friend. He is someone the King will speak to almost every day of his life, someone whose principal role is to have his boss’s back, to foresee trouble and head it off before it happens.

“Like most previous private secretaries, Sir Clive is an experienced diplomat, and he played a vital role in engineering the huge success of the King’s visit to the United States earlier this year.

‌



View 4 Images The King and Queen must now find a new private secretary (Image: Getty Images)

“Part of the job is to work closely with the Cabinet secretary and the Prime Minister’s principal private secretary and the three of them would have overseen the programme and carefully honed the witty speeches the King made.

“To Prince Harry, he was ‘the wasp’ who blocked his way and ignored his wishes. But to the King and Queen he has proved himself a safe pair of hands, and it may be that they will continue to call on his advice.

‌



“Sir Clive is someone the King has been able to turn to, complain to, laugh with and rely on as his chief gatekeeper. His successor will indeed have big shoes to fill. Thus far they have always been men, so it would be refreshing to see a woman succeed him.”

During Sir Clive’s time as the King’s principal private secretary, he has led the monarch through his cancer diagnosis and many incoming and outgoing state visits, including his trip to Washington DC to meet US president Donald Trump, where Charles delivered an historic address to Congress.

View 4 Images Sir Clive with the King at St Paul's Cathedral (Image: Getty Images)

‌



He has kept pace with Charles, described as a “complete workaholic” by his wife, and over the years helped turn his ideas into action. And Jennie says his replacement will need to hit the ground running. She explained: “The world is still in turmoil, the King and Queen are now elderly, with the King still undergoing treatment for cancer.

“The King‘s brother is still under police investigation, his sons are still estranged and the UK is getting to know yet another Prime Minister. The King will need someone with proven diplomatic skills, sensitivity about family matters and enough experience to deal with the shifting world of politics.”

Earlier this week, royal sources said the courtier elected to share the news that he was to step aside so that an open and rigorous recruitment process for his successor can begin, with the aim of identifying the highest calibre external and internal candidates.

‌



The timeframe additionally allows for an appropriate period of handover to his eventual successor in spring/summer of 2027, once an appointment is made.

And Jennie added: “The Palace are going to be looking at both internal and external candidates and they have plenty of time to cast the net wide as Sir Clive will remain in post until next year.

Article continues below

“He has been at Charles’s side through some of the most critical times: the death of Queen Elizabeth, the succession and the Coronation.

“He’s reported to have come up with a very apt phrase to describe the tone of the new King’s reign: ‘informal formality’. And it does rather sum up the way Charles goes about his business – sometimes giving and receiving hugs in the way his mother never did.”

News.title: Dad blasts 'unfair' £200 airport parking fines despite paying at drop-off zone
News.content:
Dad blasts 'unfair' £200 airport parking fines despite paying at drop-off zone

Kevin Smith, 68, was handed two fines totalling £200 for using the drop-off zone at East Midlands Airport despite paying the £5 charge on each occasion while visiting

View 2 Images A dad has been fined despite paying for a parking ticket at the drop-off zone (Image: EMA)

A dad who was hit with £200 parking fines at East Midlands Airport despite paying when he visited has blasted the system as "unfair".

‌



Kevin Smith, 68, used the airport's rapid drop-off zone to take his son to drop off and then collect him from the airport, paying the £5 charge for both trips.

‌



And so he was left "confused" when he was sent penalties totalling £200 due to a regulation which means you must pay after you leave and not while you are in the drop off zone.

‌



A barrier-free ANPR camera system operates at the airport which allowing motorists to leave their vehicle directly outside the airport's terminal building.

View 2 Images A barrier-free ANPR camera system operates at the airport (Image: Joseph Raynor/ Reach PLC)

Drivers are charged £5 for up to 15 minutes, with an additional £1 for every minute beyond that - up to a maximum of half an hour. Payments cannot be made using cash or at any on-site payment barriers, with drivers instead required to pay online or by phone before midnight on the day following their airport visit.

‌



Mr Smith and his son used the app to make payment on both the drop-off and pick-up occasions, with the former occurring on June 30.

The Clifton resident states he spent nine minutes in the drop-off zone during the outward visit and six minutes during the return trip, with £5 being deducted from his account on both occasions.

Despite this, Mr Smith still received fines of £100 for each visit, with both reduced to £60 if settled within 14 days. Mr Smith told the Nottingham Post: "They took the money on both occasions for the rapid drop-off. We paid on the app, we followed the rules, the money left the account and then they had the cheek to give me £60 fines.

‌



"This isn't just about me, but about people who might not have a phone or who are just stuck in a bit of a bubble. I think it's so unfair. It was my first time going to East Midlands Airport and it was very confusing. I think they need to make it a lot simpler for people."

It is understood the penalties were issued because Mr Smith made the payment while still within the rapid drop-off area. A notification on the app advises customers they should ensure they've departed the forecourt before processing payment.

An East Midlands Airport spokesperson commented: "We introduced an improved layout and clear signage last year which we're satisfied provides a better customer experience."

Article continues below

A spokesperson for parking operator APCOA stated: "Customers are advised on the payment screen that vehicles must have left the drop off area before a payment is made. Customers then have until midnight the following day to pay for their visit."

Mr Smith's first penalty has already been cancelled and he's awaiting a response from APCOA regarding the second, but he added: "I will not pay and I will fight it in court if I have to."

News.title: Brainteaser used in Google job interviews that would 'stop candidates being hired'
News.content:
Brainteaser used in Google job interviews that would 'stop candidates being hired'

A woman has shared a brainteaser that Google would reportedly use in job interviews to test candidates - would you have passed their test and secured a role at the company?

View Image Would you want to work for Google? (stock) (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

If you've ever wondered what it takes to land a job at Google, it appears problem-solving abilities and 'thinking outside of the box' are crucial to acing an interview. According to TikTok creator Tanya Zakowich, who goes by @pinkpencilmath on social media, Google used to pose a brainteaser to job candidates during interviews - and wouldn't hire anyone who got it wrong.

‌



However, in 2013 Google is believed to have dialled back these questions, with the former chief of Google human resources telling the New York Times they couldn't "predict anything" and were primarily there to "make the interviewer feel smart". In a video, she said: "If you don't know the prisoner hat riddle, you're going to love this one.

‌



"It's a super classic brainteaser that was commonly asked in job interviews at Google."

‌



Explaining the riddle, she says: "There were four prisoners on a staircase all facing the same direction. A brick wall separates prisoner 4 from the rest."

She says prisoner 1 can see prisoners 2 and 3, while prisoner 2 can only see prisoner 3 and prisoners 3 and 4 cannot see anyone.

"All four prisoners are wearing hats. They are told there are only two black hats and white white hats. However, they do not know the colour of the hats they are personally wearing.

‌



"The prisoners were told to shout out the colour of the hat they're wearing as soon as they know what colour it is."

Knowing this, she says the question is: "Who is the first person to shout out correctly - and why?" The rules state that prisoners cannot turn around to look at one another, move out of formation, or remove their own hats.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



Your thoughts

Weighing in on the brainteaser, one user said: "Prisoner two. If both prisoner two and three were wearing the same hat, one would have known that he was wearing the other hat. But since he didn't, two knows that."

Another user added: "Two as he can use one's silence to infer that two and three have different colour hats. Since two can see three then two must be the opposite colour of three."

A third user said: "Four because he knew no one was looking at him so he took his hat off to look."

‌



One more user added: "I used to give this riddle to my math students all the time. It's two because one didn't say anything so they know they're different from three."

Answer

According to Puzzles and Riddles, the correct answer is prisoner two - referred to as B in their explanation.

A statement reads: "If prisoners B and C had the same colour hat on, prisoner A would have know immediately that his hat was the other colour (there are only two hats of each colour).

‌



"Since prisoner A was silent, prisoners B and C must have different coloured hats. Prisoner B realised this and knew that his hat was not the same colour as prisoner C, therefore his hat must be black!".

On another occasion, an optical illusion sparked a furious debate over the numbers hidden inside. This mesmerising image features a circle filled with swirling black patterns, but what's really set tongues wagging is the mystery of what's actually contained within that circle.
