In what was their first league match since being pipped to the title by Celtic in May, the 1,600-strong travelling support could be regularly heard singing anti-Scottish Football Association songs in protest at the contentious calls from officials in the closing matches of last season that they felt cost them dear in their quest for glory.

Following a summer of transition and a 6-0 aggregate defeat by Sturm Graz that had done little to improve the mood of the fans since that agonising end to the past campaign, there was a sense of trepidation in some quarters about the prospect of kicking off the new season at Pittodrie, where they had not won in their previous 14 visits.

Hearts’ makeshift defence – with the midfielder McEntee playing at centre-half following an injury to Malachi Fagan-Walcott – looked to have allowed the Aberdeen captain Nisbet to get clean through in the third minute but McEntee recovered well to scramble the ball behind for a corner.

Nisbet then glanced a header just wide from Connor Ronan’s corner in the 27th minute, although clear chances were generally at a premium.

Hearts made the breakthrough in the 35th minute after some pinball in the penalty area. Ba-Sy’s cutback from the left broke to Blair Spittal, whose shot was blocked by Nesta Guinness-Walker on the edge of the six-yard box and the fellow defender Dan Happe’s attempt to clear ran into the path of McEntee, who shot low into the net from seven yards.

The visitors generally looked comfortable for most of the second period, with Cláudio Braga spurning a good chance to double their lead.

Aberdeen had offered little as an attacking force but they levelled in the 90th minute when Mayo bundled in from close range after Happe headed Ronan’s free-kick back into the danger area.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The dramatic turnaround was completed in stoppage time when Toyosi Olusanya was hauled down by Findlay, who saw red, and Nisbet despatched the spot-kick.

The St Mirren manager, Craig McLeish, believes his team’s 2-0 win at Falkirk augurs well for a successful campaign.

McLeish is convinced his squad will improve on last season’s struggles before he steered Saints to safety when the interim head coach.

He has set a high bar of the top six and a European qualification bid this term, and a double from Killian Phillips helped St Mirren get off to a fine start at Falkirk Stadium.

“I thought the performance was excellent and if we can build on that we can go and achieve something as a group,” McLeish said. “I’m delighted for the group. We got the result our performance deserved. I thought we were excellent.”

Sports.title: Faster, faster: Iraola in a rush to plug Liverpool gaps before Premier League starts
Sports.content:
“Faster, faster,” bellowed Andoni Iraola throughout the open training session Liverpool held in Chicago on Friday. His first pre-season tour as Liverpool head coach ends at the city’s famous Soldier Field Stadium on Sunday, with a friendly against Leeds, and “faster, faster” could apply to all aspects of the club’s preparations for a new Premier League campaign that begins in three weeks’ time.

Iraola was in his element as he immersed himself at the centre of every training drill that Liverpool performed at Chicago Fire’s Endeavor Health Performance Center, their base for the past two weeks in the US. “Faster, faster” was the new head coach’s instruction to his players as three teams of seven worked on their pressing games. He also shouted it when they walked over to a different pitch, recently vacated by Robert Lewandowski and his new Chicago Fire teammates, to work on offensive and defensive set-piece routines. Sprints were demanded following every rondo.

There is an urgency to Iraola’s situation at Liverpool as he works towards his first season in charge, not only to his style of football. Post World-Cup holidays have deprived him of eight first-team players so far, injuries of a further six.

It was telling that, after Liverpool’s open training session had ended, many of the fans invited headed to the gym for a look through its glass windows. Jérémy Jacquet, Liverpool’s £60m recruit from Rennes, was inside working on his recovery from a shoulder problem.

He was joined by Giovanni Leoni, who is rehabilitating from an anterior cruciate ligament rupture and appears to have doubled in chest size since sustaining the injury on his Liverpool debut last September. Nearby was Joe Gomez, who pulled up with a muscle injury eight minutes into the first friendly of the tour. All central defenders, all out.

The concentration of problems in one particular area was a recurring theme under Arne Slot last season and has not eased yet. Two 18-year-olds, Mor Talla Ndiaye and Ifeanyi Ndukwe, have impressed in their absence but Liverpool are looking to loan out the latter next season having been unable to secure a work permit.

Among the observers on Friday was Mike Gordon, the president of Liverpool’s owners, Fenway Sports Group, who has returned to a more hands-on role at the club after the departure of Michael Edwards as FSG’s chief executive of football.

View image in fullscreen Teenage defender Ifeanyi Ndukwe is likely to be loaned out by Liverppool. Photograph: Icon Sportswire/Getty Images

Gordon is expected to be in attendance at Soldier Field on Sunday when Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak should feature for the first time in pre-season. FSG will not be the only ones at Liverpool looking for a return on their combined £241m investment in the pair.

“We need a very good version of Florian,” Iraola said this week, when confirming he intends to play the Germany international “in that position behind the striker” rather than on the left, where he operated without reward at the World Cup, or in the variety of roles that Slot tried without success.

Wirtz supplying Isak and/or Hugo Ekitiké was always the intended plan of attack for Liverpool last season. The trio ultimately played only 119 minutes together as injuries struck. That stat was never lost on Slot as he was ushered to the exit after a turbulent and toxic campaign.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Liverpool need a very good version of Isak, too. The excuse of playing catch-up having missed pre-season, or almost four months of the season due to a fractured ankle and fibula, no longer washes for a striker who featured in all four games of Sweden’s World Cup. Isak has looked sharp in pre-season training. He not only has to sustain that sharpness next season but convince he is a suitable fit for this Liverpool team.

View image in fullscreen Florian Wirtz will be used behind the striker this season under Andoni Iraola for Liverpool. Photograph: Becky Oliver/LFC/Liverpool FC/Getty Images

Iraola’s options and vision for Liverpool will improve as senior names return but he undoubtedly requires more help through the transfer market. Work is under way on a move for Bradley Barcola, who is open to leaving Paris Saint-Germain for Anfield, but a deal for a winger who the European champions value at £145m is yet to be struck.

A lack of defensive cover cost Liverpool last season and remains a glaring issue, and there are doubts over the futures of Curtis Jones, Federico Chiesa and Harvey Elliott, among others.

Liverpool’s head coach has admitted he “hates this month of August” because of the uncertainty that surrounds players while the season starts. “It’s difficult to build a proper team with a lot of question marks,” he added. Between Soldier Field on Sunday and St James’ Park on 23 August, the building work must accelerate.

Sports.title: Transfer news: Welbeck joins Chelsea, Brentford complete record Sangaré deal
Sports.content:
Chelsea have signed Brighton’s veteran striker Danny Welbeck in a deal worth a reported £5m. Welbeck has agreed a two-year contract and will link up with Xabi Alonso’s squad on their pre-season tour.

The 35-year-old’s move to Stamford Bridge is a break from Chelsea’s policy of signing younger players with the potential to be developed. It is the first time they have paid a transfer fee for a player over the age of 26 since they signed Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang from Barcelona in 2022 when the striker was 33.

“When you hear of interest from Chelsea, it’s something that fills you with such immense pride. Knowing the history of Chelsea, it’s a club that wants to win trophies and is pushing to do that every single season,” Welbeck said.

“I’m really honoured to come to a club of this stature at what feels like a really exciting time. I know a few of the boys already and I’ve had fantastic conversations with the manager and already feel that connection. I’ve got that fire in my belly and I’m ready to give it everything for this club to make everyone at Chelsea, and the supporters, proud.”

Alonso was keen to add experience to his squad after last season’s disappointing 10th-place finish in the Premier League. He opted for Welbeck after the former Manchester United and Arsenal forward enjoyed a memorable campaign with Brighton.

Welbeck, who has 42 caps for England, scored 13 goals in 37 Premier League games last term after netting 10 times in 2024-25.

Welbeck’s arrival in west London will raise questions about the future of Chelsea striker Liam Delap, who signed from Ipswich last season, as well as fellow forwards Nicolas Jackson and Marc Guiu.

Welbeck is the latest player to move from Brighton to Chelsea in recent years after João Pedro, Moisés Caicedo, Robert Sánchez and Marc Cucurella, who joined Real Madrid earlier this summer.

Chelsea spent a British record £117m to sign the England forward Morgan Rogers, 24, from Aston Villa in July. They also secured the France defender Maxence Lacroix, 26, from Crystal Palace for £52m earlier this week and signed Atalanta defender Marco Palestra, 21, for £43m.

Brentford seal record Sangaré deal

Brentford have signed the Mali international Mamadou Sangaré from ⁠Lens for a club-record fee, reported to be £39m. Sangaré, 24, joins Brentford on a five-year contract, with ⁠the option to extend for another year.

“Mamadou ​is someone ‌that we’ve tracked ‌for quite some time. He’s been on ‌our radar and was a player we were really keen to bring in,” the Brentford head coach Keith Andrews said. “He’s a humble young man, but he’s equally as ⁠determined to succeed in his career. He ​fits ​everything we want from ​a Brentford player, on and ​off the ‌pitch.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Sangaré left Austria’s Rapid Vienna to ‌join Lens last year, and featured prominently as they won the ​French Cup for the first time and finished second in Ligue 1.

View image in fullscreen Mamadou Sangaré has swapped RC Lens for Brentford in a £39m move. Photograph: Stéphanie Lecocq/Reuters

Bournemouth have announced the signing of António Silva from Benfica for a fee believed to be in the region of £25m. The 22-year-old defender becomes new manager Marco Rose’s second signing of the summer after the arrival of Álvaro Rodríguez earlier this week.

Silva made 235 senior appearances for Benfica and collected six major honours during his time in Portugal. He told the club website: “I am very happy to be here. It’s a pleasure to play for Bournemouth and in the Premier League.

“The mentality is always to win. I will try my best, and I will play for the fans. We have everything here that helps us perform on the pitch, and I can’t wait to get started.”

Sports.title: De Zerbi wants ‘lovely guy’ Richarlison to stay at Tottenham after winner sinks Chelsea
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi wants Richarlison to stay at Tottenham, but says the striker, who has been linked with a move away, is still unsure about his future.

The Brazilian scored a last-gasp winner as 10-man Tottenham defeated Chelsea 2-1 in a pre-season friendly in Sydney, with Kevin Danso sent off just minutes after coming on as a half-time substitute.

Speaking after the game, De Zerbi said Richarlison had not clarified if he was going to depart this summer. “I don’t know, I didn’t understand well, because sometimes he said to stay, sometimes he leaves, we have to speak. Anyway, there is not any problem, he’s a lovely guy. All of us love him, the teammates, the club, the staff, because he works hard every day.”

Richarlison has less than a year left on his contract after joining Tottenham from Everton in 2022. He has struggled to find consistent form during his time in north London but De Zerbi said it would be difficult to replace his goals.

“For me he’s still an important player because it’s not so easy to find another striker as Richarlison, because Richarlison scored goals and he knows the way. The new striker, we don’t know, the other striker, we don’t know. He [Richarlison] scored 12 goals last season, not for luck, because he feels the way to score.”

Richarlison bagged a 92nd-minute winner for Tottenham against Chelsea in front of more than 80,000 fans at Sydney’s Accor Stadium. The Brazilian was the first player to react after Jamie Donley’s shot came back off a post, prodding the ball into an empty net to avert the need for a penalty shootout.

It was the first time that the two sides have met outside the UK and the match started in the spirit of a true London derby. Conor Gallagher flew into a challenge on Dário Essugo after 10 minutes, picking up a yellow card and a fair few heckles from the largely Chelsea-supporting crowd. Jan Paul van Hecke clattered into João Pedro, while Dominic Solanke and Levi Colwill tussled off the ball.

This fixture has had its fair share of red cards over the years and there was another one to add to the list, after Danso was sent off three minutes after coming off the bench. A poor surface got the better of the Spurs defender as he failed to control a backpass, allowing João Pedro to run on to the ball and through on goal. Danso lunged headfirst into the Chelsea forward, with the referee reaching straight for his pocket.

View image in fullscreen Kevin Danso is shown a red card three minutes after coming on as a substitute. Photograph: David Neilson/EPA

De Zerbi said the sending off made the game harder for both sides. “It was worse for us and for Chelsea, because if you consider the condition of the pitch, very bad. And if you consider we are starting from two weeks, maybe less than three weeks, the second half you start the fatigue and playing, attacking against 10 players behind the line of the ball is tough for every team.”

De Zerbi’s side were on top in the early stages and took a deserved lead on 17 minutes when the new signing Sandro Tonali scored his first goal for Tottenham. The midfielder’s side-footed effort from outside the area took a deflection, wrong-footing the Chelsea goalkeeper Teddy Sharman-Lowe before nestling into the bottom corner.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Spurs were only ahead for four minutes, as Estêvão Willian got the better of Andy Robertson to head home at the back post after some good work from Jamie Gittens down the left.

The game lost its competitive edge in the second half with both sides making a flurry of substitutions, before Richarlison settled it at the death.

Chelsea will now head to Hong Kong where they will be joined by Mykhailo Mudryk, who has been cleared to play again after the Football Association and the World Anti-Doping Agency resolved his appeal against a ban for failing a doping test. The Ukrainian winger was suspended for four years after failing a drug test in 2024. De Zerbi, who managed Mudryk at Shakhtar Donetsk, said he viewed the player as one of his “sons”.

“I’m very happy – he deserves to play, he’s a good guy, top player. Hopefully he can show what he suffered in the last two years, in the next season, maybe not against Tottenham, but he’s a lovely guy and he’s a very, very good player.”

Sports.title: Amanda Staveley consortium set to buy Gold family’s 25.1% stake in West Ham
Sports.content:
A consortium led by Amanda Staveley has reached an agreement to buy a ‌25.1% stake in West ⁠Ham after Vanessa Gold, daughter of the former chair David Gold, ⁠agreed to sell ⁠her ​family’s shares in the Championship club.

The move by the businesswoman who helped lead the Saudi consortium takeover of Newcastle comes after a previously agreed sale to fellow shareholder and Czech businessman ⁠Daniel Kretinsky fell through.

The Gold family ​trust owns the 25.1% stake in West Ham, ‌who were relegated from the Premier League last season just two seasons after winning the Europa Conference League in 2023. However, current shareholders will also be presented with the chance to buy out the Gold family under an ongoing process.

Gold said in a statement: “As the daughter of David Gold, it was a great honour to step into a joint chair and director role at the club following his passing in 2023. Whether as a youth team player, a lifelong fan or an owner, my father’s priority was always to champion and protect this great club. Over the past three years I have taken huge personal pride in continuing that legacy and will always be hugely grateful to the staff, players and fans who allowed me to do so.

“On June 12, Daniel Kretínsky and I agreed a sale that would have made EP Group the single largest shareholder in West Ham. Unfortunately, since that time, the original deal and other alternatives that we have discussed could not be brought to fruition.

View image in fullscreen West Ham were relegated from the Premier League last season. Photograph: Eddie Keogh/Reuters

“In light of this, I have now reached an agreement to sell my family’s shareholding to a consortium led by Amanda Staveley, Mehrdad Ghodoussi and PCP Capital Partners. This sale remains subject to a pre-emption process, under which existing shareholders have the option to buy the shares instead.

“While the process has not yet concluded, I wanted to be open with our fans about where things stand and my intentions. My ambition throughout this process has been to ensure the club has the right leadership and ownership to enable West Ham to achieve its potential and return to its rightful place in the Premier League.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“Amanda Staveley, Mehrdad Ghodoussi and PCP Capital Partners will bring deep experience and understanding of what it takes to lead a successful football club, and I have every confidence in what she and her partners can bring to West Ham. While the sale process proceeds, I will continue to act in the club’s best interests, as my father did and would expect of me.”



Staveley brokered the deal which allowed a Saudi-backed consortium to buy-out then Newcastle owner Mike Ashley in October 2021, and she and Ghodoussi oversaw the club’s rise from Premier League relegation candidates to Champions League participants and, after their departure during the summer of 2024, Carabao Cup winners.

The Hammers dropped out of the top flight at the end of last season and will begin the process of attempting to secure a swift return at Burnley on 16 August.

Sports.title: Man United consider surprise move for Premier League star as Lewis Hall alternative
Sports.content:
Man United consider surprise move for Premier League star as Lewis Hall alternative

Manchester United could make a move for Arsenal's Myles Lewis-Skelly.

talkSPORT understands that while Newcastle's Lewis Hall remains Man United's preferred left-back target, Lewis-Skelly is being considered.

2 Lewis-Skelly was part of Arsenal's 2025/26 Premier League-winning squad but didn't feature as much as he'd have liked Credit: Getty

Man United are looking to bolster their options on the left-hand side of defence, with Luke Shaw currently the only senior player in that role.

talkSPORT initially reported in March that Man United had identified Lewis-Skelly as a possible signing.

The 19-year-old saw minutes hard to come by at Arsenal last season, and his cause won't be helped by the permanent signing of the versatile Piero Hincapie – who thrived on loan at left-back to help the Gunners end their 22-year Premier League title drought.

With Riccardo Calafiori also ahead of Lewis-Skelly in the pecking order, a move away from the Emirates Stadium might be the England international's best option as he looks to kick on his career.

Having risen through Arsenal's youth ranks and broken into the first team in 2024/25, Lewis-Skelly made just five Premier League starts last term amid stiff competition for places.

While he's already been capped six times by England, he'll need to be playing more regular club football if he's to truly establish himself at international level.

Lewis-Skelly still has four years remaining on his Gunners contract and is valued by Transfermarkt at just under £38.5m.

However, Man United have been told to pull out all the stops to bring Hall to Old Trafford.

With Eddie Howe stepping down as Newcastle boss on Friday, more player exits from St. James' Park might well follow – and Hall could be among them.

talkSPORT pundit Flex has told Man United to put in a substantial opening bid for the 21-year-old.

2 Four-cap England international Hall has made over 100 appearances for Newcastle since joining from Chelsea three years ago Credit: Getty

"We’re not in charge of the purse, but I’m saying you slap £50million down – opening bid – and just ruffle some feathers in there," he said on Inside Devils.

Man United have been busy adding to their squad during Michael Carrick's first full transfer window as head coach.

Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos are the headline arrivals so far, joining from Aston Villa and Chelsea respectively.

The Red Devils have also added Wales goalkeeper Karl Darlow on a free transfer following his departure from Leeds.

Having continued their pre-season with a 2-1 friendly win over Atletico Madrid in Sweden on Saturday – with wonderkid JJ Gabriel playing his first senior minutes – Carrick's men get the 2026/27 campaign underway with a trip to newly promoted Hull on August 22.

They then take on another promoted side, Ipswich, in their home opener eight days later.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta’s response to Vinicius Jr question sends Arsenal fans into a frenzy
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta again outlined Arsenal's transfer ambitions, amid continued talk of a move for Vinicius Jr.

The Brazil superstar remains linked with a switch to the Gunners, with his Real Madrid future yet to be resolved.

2 Could we see Vinicius Jr lighting up the Premier League this coming season? Credit: Getty

Vinicius is out of contract at the Bernabeu next summer, and talkSPORT reported last month that Arsenal were considering a surprise swoop for the 26-year-old forward.

And now comments from Arteta have heightened Gunners fans' excitement around the possibility of what would be surely the most momentous transfer of the summer.

Arsenal 'won't sit still'

Asked 'when's Vini joining?' after Arsenal's 4-1 pre-season friendly win over Girona, Arteta smiled.

And he went on to tell reporters about the prospect of more signings as the Gunners prepare for their Premier League title defence: "Well, we are already active trying to improve and evolve the team – that's clear.

"We expect to have movements in the next few weeks, obviously, because we want to get better like anybody else, and you just can see the transfer market and our opponents what we are doing.

"We won't sit still and we are very ambitious what we want to do."

Could that ambition extend to bringing Vinicius to the Emirates Stadium?

Gunners fans have been getting carried away with themselves following that interview.

One said: "Remember same reaction from Wenger when Ozil signed."

Another added: "That smile says it all."

2 Vinicius has scored 128 goals in 376 appearances for Real Madrid Credit: Getty

Well, Arsenal fans have been warned that the situation might be a misdirection, as Transfer Insiders host Rickie Haywood-Williams suggested.

"I think this is the biggest red herring in history in terms of live transfers," he said on talkSPORT.

"Because I feel like Vinicius Jr has been trying to get a new contract at Real Madrid for the last couple of years.

"In that time, they’ve signed [Kylian] Mbappe – Mbappe is on incredible money and he [Vinicius] obviously is going to want parity with that or somewhere close, and I think he’s using the Premier League as a bit of a bargaining chip to try and up the ante on his money, to try and get a bigger contract."

Gunners' squad takes shape

Arsenal have made two new additions to their squad during the current transfer window.

Goalkeeper Illan Meslier has come in on a free transfer after leaving Leeds, while winger Christos Tzolis has arrived from Club Brugge in a deal worth £34m.

Title-winning full-back Piero Hincapie has also made his loan move from Bayer Leverkusen permanent.

And the Gunners are closing in on Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes.

Arsenal are back in pre-season action against Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday.

Their first competitive game of the new campaign sees them face FA Cup winners Manchester City in the Community Shield at Wembley on August 16 – before the Premier League curtain-raiser at home to newly promoted Coventry five days later.

Sports.title: Trent Alexander-Arnold told to explore controversial Premier League return at specific club
Sports.content:
Liverpool should be open to re-signing Trent Alexander-Arnold.

That's the strong belief of talkSPORT's Angelina Kelly, who called on supporters to embrace the possibility of the right-back returning to Anfield.

3 Alexander-Arnold won two Premier League titles with Liverpool after coming through the Reds' academy Credit: Getty



The relationship between Alexander-Arnold and Reds fans became strained after he opted against signing a new contract with his boyhood club and joined Real Madrid last summer, with some going as far as to boo their former hero.

But the 27-year-old's move to Spain has proved far from successful so far, after he started just 14 LaLiga games last season and failed to score in any competition for the first time since his maiden senior campaign of 2016/17.

And Kelly believes Liverpool should at least think about bringing Alexander-Arnold back to Merseyside amid question marks over their own right-back position.

Joining Nick Bright on talkSPORT's Transfer Insiders, she said: "I know what it’s like for a player to, in your opinion, betray the club – especially one of your own, especially being a Liverpudlian. I get it.



"When Real Madrid come calling, it is hard to say no – we have to be honest with that – and he’s made the move and it hasn’t really worked out.

"And you look at Liverpool and you think do they need a new right-back?



"I mean, [Jeremie] Frimpong didn’t look great last season – I think he’s probably better playing further forward – [Conor] Bradley injured…

"I think maybe they should cut their losses and just explore the Trent situation.



"I’m not saying you’ve got to sign him immediately – let’s just explore this. Because Real Madrid have signed another right-back in Denzel Dumfries – that is not good news for Trent [who has been warned to expect to lose his place].

"So, why can’t everyone just take some ownership…take a bit of accountability and we can all come back together and be happy?

3 Alexander-Arnold faces right-back competition from new arrival Denzel Dumfries Credit: Getty

"You know, Marcus Rashford and Manchester United, they're having not exactly the same but a similar situation of having to come back.



"I think that there is a way back, and surely there’s one Liverpool fan listening that would have him back – I can’t be on my own here.

"I just think that…you may as well try it because…he was so good at Liverpool…

"Back at Liverpool where a few games, a few goals maybe, a few assists or something – he does something. If he ends up helping Liverpool, like, win the Premier League or get to a Champions League final – if he does something really, really good for Liverpool, I know the fans are loyal, but surely that’s his way of saying sorry and making up for it [his departure]?

"If he can make up for it, why not?"

Reminded by Bright that she'd said fans should accept Alexander-Arnold back in a Liverpool shirt, Kelly affirmed: "They should have him back because on paper, things have gone wrong, yes – but there's always a road back.



3 Alexander-Arnold has played 354 games for Liverpool... so far

"People sometimes deserve second chances and I think Trent does.

"So, the way things are going – right-back situation, you've got a gap there – get him back in."

Liverpool have completed two first-team signings so far this summer, bringing in France U21 defender Jeremie Jacquet and World Cup-winning Spain forward Victor Munoz from Rennes and Osasuna respectively.

Sports.title: West Ham’s ‘next Declan Rice’ set for permanent transfer to Champions League club
Sports.content:
West Ham have agreed to sell academy graduate Freddie Potts to Club Brugge in a deal worth around £10million, talkSPORT understands.

The 22-year-old was expected to be a key member of the Hammers' squad in their upcoming Championship season, as they seek an immediate return to the top flight.

5 Freddie Potts looks set to depart West Ham after making 32 senior appearances Credit: Getty

But Potts - the son of club icon Steve - now looks set to end his 17-year association with the club he first joined as a six-year-old.

talkSPORT understands the midfielder has been permitted to travel to Belgium for a medical with top-flight side Club Brugge.

Despite a move appearing close, Potts was named on West Ham's bench for their final pre-season friendly against German second division side FC Magdeburg.

The young Englishman did not feature in the clash, though, as the Irons rounded off their season's preparations with a 1-1 draw.

And the east London outfit now look to have been dealt a late blow ahead of their campaign, with Potts seemingly destined to leave.

If his move to Brugge goes through, the midfielder will be swapping the Championship for Champions League football, after the Belgian giants qualified by clinching league glory last term.

Potts, who has drawn comparisons to former West Ham captain Declan Rice, is being lined up as a replacement for Raphael Onyedika.

The Nigeria international is closing in on a move to Bundesliga outfit Eintracht Frankfurt for a rumoured £7.6m fee.

Pott twist

Potts' anticipated West Ham exit comes just as he looked set to play a greater role for the club in the Championship.

The local lad made 22 Premier League appearances last season, starting 12 times as the Hammers were relegated on the final day.

5 Potts captained West Ham in a 1-1 draw with Rangers in pre-season Credit: Getty

5 Potts' dad, Steve, made over 500 appearances for West Ham in 17 years at the club Credit: Getty

But having spent the 2024/25 season on loan at Portsmouth in the second tier, he was expected to feature more in the upcoming campaign.

The departure of key man Mateus Fernandes to Tottenham in a £85m deal appeared to pave the way for this.

Potts wore the captain's armband during West Ham's pre-season friendly draw with Rangers in July, suggesting he would be among Nuno Espirito Santo's starting midfielders.

It appears Potts himself even expected this, having recently shared his plans to become an established player at the London Stadium.

In an interview with BBC Radio London, he said: "I want to play as much as I can for West Ham this season.

"I want to show that I've got the experience in the Championship from before with previous clubs. I'm excited for the challenge that comes ahead."

5 Potts has never played outside of English football in his fledgling career Credit: Getty

Potts also spoke of the desire throughout the club to bounce back to the Premier League at the first attempt following relegation.

He added: "I think it's going to be a very good season for us."

"We can see the love for the club from the fans, and we want to replicate that on the pitch.

"We're very confident going into this season that we can achieve the goal that everyone wants to achieve and no doubt the fans will back us."

End of the road?

Should he finalise his departure, Potts will leave West Ham having made 32 first-team appearances.

He made his senior debut in a 1–0 loss against Dinamo Zagreb in the Conference League in 2021, with his Premier League bow coming last August, coming on as a half-time substitute in a 5-1 loss to Chelsea.

5 Nuno Espirito Santo is looking to win promotion from the Championship for the second time in his career with West Ham Credit: Getty

West Ham will play their first competitive game of the season next week, as they host league rivals Portsmouth in the Carabao Cup first round.

They will then get their league campaign underway a week later with an away trip to fellow relegated side Burnley on August 16.

Sports.title: Liverpool have a responsibility to give forgotten man ‘second chance’ after PFA failure
Sports.content:
Harvey Elliott has revealed he is ready for a 'second chance' at Liverpool - and it's the club's duty to make sure he's given one.

The 23-year-old has unexpectedly found himself back with his boyhood club after his tumultuous season on loan with Aston Villa.



6 Elliott started as the attacking midfielder in Iraola's 4-2-3-1 formation for Liverpool's win over Wrexham Credit: Getty

The England Under-21 international wouldn't have expected to have played for Liverpool again when he left the club last summer.

Elliott had the pick of several clubs across Europe as a reward for his standout role in the Young Lions' defence of their U21 Euro title.

The attacker was named the player of the tournament in Slovakia after scoring five goals for Lee Carsley's back-to-back champions.



His solo success came off the back of Liverpool's title-winning 2024/25 season in which he made just six starts under Arne Slot.

Elliott joined Aston Villa on deadline day on an initial loan that carried a £35million obligation to buy once he made 10 league appearances.



However, Villa decided early in the season that they did not want to trigger that option, while Unai Emery stated multiple times that his side had no interest in signing Elliott from Liverpool permanently.

That stance meant the former Fulham starlet managed just 277 minutes of football in all competitions - only 13 of which came in the Premier League from the end of September.



Having started last season playing for Liverpool, FIFA rules also prevented Elliott from cutting short his Villa loan to join a third European club - effectively confining him to the football wilderness.

'The PFA should have spoken out'

Former Liverpool Forward Stan Collymore told Hawksbee & Jacobs in May: "I think it's a disgrace, to be honest.

"I think that, firstly, the PFA, where are you - in Delia [Smith] speak - looking after a player that basically won't have played for a season is exactly the kind of territory I'd expect the PFA chief to come out and say, 'This is unacceptable.'

6 Elliott effectively lost a year of his career after being exiled at Villa Credit: Getty



"This is a season gone in a career that only comes around once and is very short," Ex-Villa star Collymore continued on talkSPORT.

"Neither Villa nor Liverpool come out of this very well. Why? Liverpool had their rules and regulations that they wanted Villa to stick by in terms of purchases or not, but Villa either did want the player or didn't.

"You can't take a player on loan and then, effectively, within a couple of weeks say not for us.

"So Aston Villa's recruitment department is partly to blame. And I think there's a very simple workaround.



"We often talk in the game of player power, which doesn't really exist.

"They sign contracts, and they only sign contracts that clubs are willing to give them. So when people say, what are you talking about, Collymore? This player's signed a hundred grand a week contract or 300 grand a week. There isn't a club that is forced to give any player a contract.

6 Elliott scored England's first goal in the 3-2 win over Germany in the Under-21s Euro final Credit: AFP

"So in terms of Harvey Elliott, I'd like to see players via the PFA wrestle back a little bit more power.



"And that would be Harvey Elliott signs for Villa on loan or whoever. And if he's not involved in 90 per cent of the club's first 10 games, then the player turns around and says, well, you've not discharged your part of the bargain. I'm going to trigger a release clause to go back to the parent club.

"And then I'm going to go back on loan to somewhere that will have me. And I think that that would stop this overnight.

"It would give players a little bit more reassurance that they've got some control over their own career, which Harvey Elliott has not had this season."

That control is something Liverpool can - and should - give back to their No.19 this summer or else risk being directly responsible for curtailing a promising career they helped build.



According to Jurgen Klopp, Elliott could have 'gone pretty much anywhere' before he decided to sign for Liverpool at 16-years-old.

After he signed professional terms at Anfield, Klopp added: "What is great is that he has the perfect culture here and we will protect him."

Yet that culture had changed so drastically under his successor Slot, who seemingly washed his hands of Elliott's situation in January.

6 Elliott returned early to pre-season and began preparatory work with Liverpool's U21 squad Credit: Getty



Slot said: “He’s an Aston Villa player. So if you want to ask things about an Aston Villa player, you should ask Unai Emery.”

In reality, Elliott was technically still a Liverpool player as he was still only on loan, hence his being back at the club now for pre-season.

Far from being bitter at his cold shoulder, the player himself has been relishing enjoying his football again after starting both of Iraola's pre-season games in charge this summer.

Elliott ready to take 'second chance' at Liverpool

“Everyone knows how much I love the club so the feeling never goes of putting the shirt back on, representing the club, and fulfilling your childhood dream,” Elliott told reporters after Liverpool’s 1-0 friendly win over Wrexham in New York.



“But truthfully, yes [I felt it would never happen again], because I wanted a new challenge. I wanted to explore something, come out of my comfort zone, and I thought that would take me on as a player. Unfortunately, it didn’t work out, but the way I see it is it’s kind of a second chance, especially with the gaffer and new coaching staff coming in.

“It’s another chance to impress and hopefully get in their good books. But whatever happened last season, I wish Villa nothing but the very best.

“I had a lot of love for them, and they treated me very well. I’m here now, and I’m trying to cement my spot in the team or within the squad.”

6 Elliott insists he harbours 'no hard feelings' towards Villa Credit: Getty



Elliott would have been eyeing a wildcard entry into Thomas Tuchel’s World Cup squad before his career stalled in the Midlands.

While he has denied that 'it was a lost year', which is the correct mentality to have, the truth of the matter is that it was.

Liverpool don't have to suddenly offer him a new contract as compensation for that, but the least they can do is give him a genuine lifeline to remain a part of Iraola's first-team squad.

If Elliott pushes to leave, that's his decision, but with only one more month before the window shuts, he runs the risk of repeating his ill-fated Villa loan.



A third straight season playing little-to-no football would be a death knell for his career, and it's hard to see what club would actually prove the right fit if they've waited this long to make a serious approach.

“I’m not sure yet what’s going to happen (regarding his future),” Elliott continued. “That’s a conversation for me to have more in detail with the gaffer. When the time is right, I’ll go and ask.

“I’m just giving my all and trying to impress. Going forward, I need to be more kind of cautious with my decisions. I have to do what’s right for me, whether that’s staying here and fighting for my place, or whether that’s potentially going elsewhere.

“But I’m really happy to be back. Since the first day I walked through the door at the AXA, I’ve had a big beaming smile on my face. Putting the shirt on, I don’t want to take these moments for granted because last season I thought I’d done it for the last time. Playing at Liverpool, there’s no better feeling.”



6 Elliott provided an assist in his 45-minute showing against Sunderland Credit: Getty

They say there is no room for sentiment in football, but this is just as practical a decision as it is an emotional one.

Elliott adds depth in two areas Liverpool are light in (No.10 and right-wing), and flourished most in Klopp's high-intensity system that is much more akin to Iraola's style of play than Slot's.

Under the Spaniard, he 'has the perfect culture here', as Klopp once said, to rediscover his potential - it's down to the hierarchy now to protect him from being shoved straight out of the exit door.

Sports.title: Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal close to Guimaraes deal north of £75m, Welbeck announced, Brentford sign Sangare for club record fee
Sports.content:
UEFA welcomes FIFA’s decision to withdraw its plan to sell a stake in its competitions – including the World Cup – into private hands.

The proposal was unanimously rejected by UEFA’s national associations and by many other federations and confederations of all sizes around the world, whose job it is to protect football.

UEFA thanks all the fans, leagues, clubs, players, individuals, associations and confederations that opposed the scheme, alongside the many Prime Ministers, Heads of State and commentators who have demonstrated to the FIFA President that football is not for sale.

We cannot keep going on like this with secret schemes on fast track timescales, cooked up by faceless individuals and of dubious benefit to the game. We must identify those responsible and hold them to account.

It is right that, in the coming days and weeks, UEFA will work with its associations and in close cooperation with other confederations to reflect on how this happened and devise a plan to make sure that it cannot occur again. That review should be thorough and fundamental. No option should be off the table. The current FIFA leadership has not only lost UEFA’s confidence but also that of many other members of the football family.

When Gianni Infantino asked for the trust and the votes of FIFA’s Member Associations to elect him as their President in 2016, he said, “Of course we have to be transparent. I have been this in the last 15 years of my life in UEFA. You will have to play a part every day in the life of FIFA,” before telling the assembled stakeholders, “The money of FIFA is your money. It’s not the money of the FIFA President. It’s your money. You are the national associations and the money of FIFA has to serve for the development of football and not for anything else.”

On both these promises, he has failed to deliver. The shabby, back room, opaque deal he hatched and tried to force through was anything but transparent.

And with reserves standing at over $5bn, he has also failed to use associations’ money for the benefit of the game.

UEFA will begin work immediately with partners and stakeholders all over the world and right across the game to propose a new way of distributing resources through the existing FIFA Forward programme.

We must start to use some of that money that is sat idle in FIFA’s bank account to deliver the kick start that the grassroots and the wider game need in each of the 211 countries of FIFA. But we don’t need to sell off the family silver to pay for it.

This is a victory for the whole game. But it must not be the end of the story. The proposal has gone. The task of rebuilding trust in FIFA has only just begun.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick handed major JJ Gabriel warning as 15-year-old wonderkid makes Manchester United debut
Sports.content:
Manchester United must not introduce JJ Gabriel to first team action too early despite his impressive development.

That's the plea made by talkSPORT host Angelina Kelly after the 15-year-old played his first minutes for the senior side in pre-season.



3 Gabriel was handed his United debut in their friendly win against Atletico Credit: Getty

Gabriel came off the bench for Bryan Mbeumo on Saturday as United beat Atletico Madrid 2-1 at the Strawberry Arena in Stockholm.

Although he was brought on with less than ten minutes to go, it saw one of the club's brightest prospects make his debut.

The teenager joined their pre-season tour after a stunning year in which he was named as the U18 Premier League Player of the Season.



It appears that he has the backing of head coach Michael Carrick, and could earn some competitive experience in the upcoming season.

Gift of the Gab

Kelly lauded Gabriel for his impact in the United academy as, on talkSPORT's Transfer Insiders, she said: "He's been absolutely brilliant so far.



"It was 23 goals in 23 games for United's U18s (last season), he's good with the assists as well, he's just a really exciting talent.

"Because he's so young, and we're seeing other players like Max Dowman (Arsenal) getting opportunities, he's United's version of that.



"He helped United to the FA Youth Cup final, they did lose it to Manchester City but he scored three goals in that competition."

Kelly then insisted that United should be careful not to rush him, and used Chido Obi-Martin as an example.

The forward is another promising starlet and has made eight senior appearances for United, but is yet to have scored or assisted.

3 United have been warned against bringing Gabriel into the first team too early Credit: Getty



Easy does it

"Just a really exciting goalscorer and I think for Manchester United, the youth side of things, we've seen a couple of players come through," Kelly said.

"A few former players' children like Darren Fletcher's sons (Jack and Tyler), but to actually have an exciting goalscorer from Man United's academy, we've not really seen anybody for a while.

"Somebody to really be impressing in the way that he is, so I think they've got to be very careful as to how they bring him in.

"United brought Chido Obi-Martin from Arsenal and everyone was expecting that to be absolute fireworks.



"It hasn't quite clicked just yet, and we probably introduced him a little bit too early.

"So, I think with this player, you've got to be really careful with how you handle it but so far, he keeps hitting every height so, very exciting."

3 Carrick may be willing to give Gabriel more minutes in pre-season Credit: Getty

United's pre-season so far

After a 1-0 defeat to Wrexham, United have bounced back with two consecutive wins this summer.



A 5-0 thrashing of Rosenborg BK preceded the victory over Atletico, but three tough fixtures are up next on their schedule.

Champions League winners Paris Saint-Germain meet them on August 8, with rivals Leeds United their opponents four days later.

AC Milan will be their final test on August 15, a week before United travel to Hull City for their Premier League opener, live on talkSPORT.

Sports.title: Manchester City warned summer transfer will cost them the Premier League title
Sports.content:
Manchester City would rule themselves out of the Premier League title race this season by letting Rodri leave.

That's according to talkSPORT host Adam Catterall, as Ashley Williams labelled the midfielder as the world's best player.

3 Rodri could be on his way to Madrid this summer Credit: Getty

talkSPORT understands that Real Madrid have opened talks with City to sign Rodri this summer.

City want to keep the midfielder for the upcoming season, even if he doesn't sign a new deal at the Etihad Stadium.

However, with one year left on his current contract in Manchester, it's understood that Rodri wants to move to Madrid.

If Lille star Ayyoub Bouaddi was to sign for City, then they could well be more inclined to sanction an exit for the 2024 Ballon d'Or winner.

Rodri would still be a massive miss, so much so that Catterall believes his absence will damage City's hopes of winning the title.

Hot Rod

"There's a lot of chat about Rodri, at the moment, off the back of his fantastic World Cup (with Spain)," he said on Saturday Session.

"I know that off the back of his injury last year, he wasn't at his scintillating best, but the World Cup kind of pointed in the direction that the Ballon d'Or winner is back to his very, very best.

"I genuinely believe that if he does go to Real Madrid in this window, that will scupper any chances that Manchester City have of winning the Premier League.

"I think he's that influential. He has to be at City, if City are going to make a Premier League challenge this year."

Catterall then asked: "Am I going too far with that? Can one player be that influential in a team?"

3 City have been warned that without Rodri, they will not win the title Credit: Getty

Former Premier League defender Williams answered yes to the latter question, and said: "If it's him... the best player in the world right now, Rodri.

"My concern is that they've brought in Elliot Anderson and think, 'We can probably live without Rodri', they can't, I think they need both of them. I love Elliot Anderson, I think he's brilliant, he'll be the future.

"But wouldn't it be great for him to have all that he's got already and learn off Rodri with the way he plays? And have both of them at least overlapping for a couple of seasons.

"At no point would you ever, ever get rid of Rodri, for no amount of money. They could offer me whatever and I wouldn't sell Rodri."

What has been said on Rodri?

Ahead of his first season as City manager, Enzo Maresca has had to deal with an uncertain future over one of his key players.

However, when asked about the latest information he could give on the 30-year-old, he said It's just speculation at this moment.

3 Maresca faces a wait to see if he will have to do without Rodri this season Credit: Getty

"Rodri had the (minor back) surgery last Monday, everything was fine," Maresca said.

"Now some days off, and then back with us when he finishes his holiday."

Sports.title: Ex-Manchester United star Casemiro scores an OWN GOAL on his Inter Miami home debut - as Lionel Messi returns to club action after Argentina's World Cup final defeat by Spain
Sports.content:
Ex-Manchester United star Casemiro scores an OWN GOAL on his Inter Miami home debut - as Lionel Messi returns to club action after Argentina's World Cup final defeat by Spain

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Casemiro endured an Inter Miami home debut to forget as he scored an own goal during their 2-2 MLS draw with Columbus Crew on Saturday.

The 34-year-old joined the American outfit on a free transfer after leaving Manchester United - where he earned £375,000-per-week - at the end of the 2025-26 Premier League campaign.

He made his debut on July 26 - playing the full duration in a 1-0 win at Montreal.

And less than a week later he started in front of his new home supporters but with a different outcome.

Leading 1-0 thanks to Luis Suarez's long-range strike, Inter Miami were pegged back on 34 minutes when Casemiro finished past his own goalkeeper.

The Brazilian was at fault for the build-up to the own goal too when he gave away possession inside his own half.

A goal is a goal 🤩 pic.twitter.com/0DZyLQwtIp — The Crew (@ColumbusCrew) August 2, 2026

Casemiro (centre left) scored an own goal on his Inter Miami home debut as they drew 2-2

The 34-year-old was later booked for a foul on Columbus Crew's Sekou Bangoura (centre)

His pass was intercepted by Hugo Picard who passed to Daniel Gazdag. Gazdag played the ball out wide to Taha Habroune and as his low delivery went across the box, a desperate Casemiro could only stretch to divert it past team-mate Rocco Rios Novo.

The Brazil international cut a sheepish figure as the Nu Stadium was stunned into silence. He was later booked too for a foul on Sekou Bangoura.

Noah Allen's goal deep into first-half stoppage time restored the noise inside the ground as Inter Miami took the lead and that volume increased early in the second half when Lionel Messi came on.

Miami talisman Messi came on in the 53rd minute to a rapturous applause in what was his first outing since captaining Argentina to their abject World Cup final defeat by Spain on July 19.

The 39-year-old immediately took the armband from Suarez but he was unable to steer his team to three points as Brais Mendez scored a late equaliser.

Mendez curled a free-kick from the right side that went untouched off the post and into the net in the 84th minute.

Messi is back after leading Argentina to its second-straight World Cup Final appearance. 👏 pic.twitter.com/F91Bo3BC4v — Major League Soccer (@MLS) August 2, 2026

Lionel Messi (right) made a return to Inter Miami action after losing the World Cup final in July

Much like events that occurred in the World Cup, the encounter was delayed by 40 minutes due to inclement weather.

The draw ended Inter Miami's six-game winning streak but they are now unbeaten in seven matches.

Sports.title: Athletes who hate their sports: From a Premier League winner who doesn't watch football to an Ally Pally world champion that isn't a fan of darts
Sports.content:
Athletes who hate their sports: From a Premier League winner who doesn't watch football to an Ally Pally world champion that isn't a fan of darts

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

There are a number of pulls when it comes to a career in sport.

The chance to spend every day doing what you love, earning your living along the way. Or maybe the pursuit of glory, the drive to be the best at what you have dedicated your life to. How about the sometimes staggering prize money on offer, which can lead to the chance of fame and a lifestyle most can only dream of?

Few consider that, for some, it's not really a choice. It's what athletes know – what they have always done, so they will continue to do.

That seems to be the case for three-time darts world champion Michael van Gerwen, who this week spoke about how he's not a fan of darts and doesn't actually follow his sport.

And he's not alone. Some of the top names in tennis, football and more have expressed their dislike and distaste for the games that have given them so much.

Here, Daily Mail Sport takes a look at some of the world's top athletes who aren't actually too fond of the sport they have found success in.

Three-time darts world champion Michael van Gerwen revealed this week that he does not enjoy watching darts

Michael van Gerwen – Darts

Three-time world champion Michael van Gerwen has dropped down to world No 7 after the Matchplay, and his stocks have fallen significantly since his last world title in 2019.

The Dutchman has been speaking about his relationship with darts – the sport in which, perhaps for the first time in a decade, he is no longer the biggest star.

'I never did in my life,' he told Winmau of watching games. 'I don't even like watching darts.'

Luke v Luke (Littler and Humphries) has been the talk of the town for the last couple of years, while Littler has taken his game to a new dimension in recent months in becoming the first darts player to pick up £3million worth of earnings in two years.

Van Gerwen does make an effort to keep tabs on his rivals, but don't expect to see him in the crowd of any events he's not involved in any time soon, or listening to the likes of Wayne Mardle or Dan Dawson analysing the game on the tele.

But he doesn't totally hate the game. Just prefers to play it – which is fair enough, all things considered.

'Sometimes if a friend like Vincent (Van der Voort) used to play or things like that, or if Luke against Luke are playing maybe a final,' Van Gerwen continued on his viewing habits. 'I put on some live scores, but I'm not going to watch it at all.

'I'd rather play than watch. Simple as that. I always say the same, so it would be really weird to change my opinion.'

Ben White – Football

Arsenal defender Ben White has proven to be a bit of a diverse character in football in recent years. It all came to a head in November 2022, when he fell out with England assistant manager Steve Holland – supposedly over his attitude towards the game.

White is not a fan of watching football unless it's to analyse his own performances. Reports also emerged three years ago that White was not watching other analytical videos while with England.

'I watch myself for analytical reasons,' White recently claimed to The Overlap. 'I watch England, maybe, but I'm always busy doing something. I wouldn't just sit down and watch a game.

'I didn't ever watch football when I was younger. I still don't now.'

But, as is the case with Van Gerwen, it's not all hate with White. He just wants to be out there playing.

'I just loved the game,' he continued. 'I was always playing it, never watching.

'So I don't know too much about the older generations, but I know (Patrick) Vieira was a very good player. But I don't know the details.'

Ben White (right) has become known for his dislike of watching football

Serena Williams – Tennis

Serena Williams is perhaps the most famous name in women's tennis history, and one of the most dominant too.

'I don't love tennis today, but I'm here, and I can't live without it,' she told TennisNow in 2012. 'So I'm still here and I don't want to go anywhere any time soon.'

That's despite winning seven Australian Opens, seven Wimbledon titles, six US Opens and three French Opens. But it's not just tennis – it's sport on the whole.

'It's not that I've fallen out of love, I've actually never liked sports, and I never understood how I became an athlete,' she continued. 'I don't like working out, I don't like anything that has to do with working physically.'

Not too much of an issue, though, it seems...

Serena Williams revealed in 2012 that she doesn't love tennis - or sport on the whole

Nick Kyrgios – Tennis

Tennis bad boy Nick Kyrgios has had a bit of a love-hate relationship with his sport.

The Australian, who is planning retirement at the age of 31, reached his first Grand Slam final in 2022 at Wimbledon. He would lose to Novak Djokovic, but has also regularly made headlines for his actions away from the actual tennis, such as his shouting during matches.

One wonders if his relationship with tennis is related to that. He said in 2015: 'I don't really like the sport of tennis that much. I don't love it.'

He does, though, have love for a different sport.

'It was crazy when I was 14,' he continued. 'I was all for basketball and I made the decision to play tennis. I got pushed by my parents and to this day I can still say I don't love the sport. It is just crazy how things go.

'It's good when you're out there on a tennis court. There's nowhere to hide. It's all you, tactically, physically, mentally. But I just love basketball, I love the sport. I always have. I try when I'm on the road with tennis not to watch too many basketball videos and stuff like that, to keep me focused, but it's tough.'

What could have been.

Nick Kygrios has a love-hate relationship with the sport - and would rather have been a basketball player

Mark Williams – Snooker

Things seem to be going a little better for Mark Williams since his comments in 2019, when he became one of the few athletes to actively say they 'hate' their sport.

Currently World No 8 and a 2025 World Championship finalist, the Welshman was going through a tough patch back in 2019 when he had just beaten Fraser Patrick 6-2 in the first round of the UK Snooker Championship.

Despite actually being ranked No 3 in the world, Williams had failed to win a ranking event all year. He lashed out at snooker, and, like Kyrgios, his mind was elsewhere.

'I really struggled but somehow he struggled more than me and made it easy for me on a couple of frames,' Williams said. 'It's going all right, I'm enjoying myself when I'm on the golf course.'

When questioned on snooker, he added: 'Hate it. I'm just enjoying playing golf more.'

He had also talked about retirement in 2017, before going on to become world champion for a third time a year later.

Maybe he feels differently now.

Mark Williams admitted to 'hating' snooker in 2019 after teasing retirement a few years earlier

Tyson Fury – Boxing

Potentially the biggest name in modern boxing doesn't actually like boxing.

Tyson Fury has retired and un-retired countless times, but attributes his many returns to an addiction that helps him deal with his mental health struggles.

'I've tried to walk away many times and been unsuccessful,' he told DAZN in 2024. 'I meant it when I retired after Dillian Whyte back in 2022, I really meant that wholeheartedly. I could have put my hand on the Bible and meant it, but it was difficult to let it go.

'I've been in love with boxing from a little boy. It's been a love-hate relationship. When it's good, it's very good and when it's bad, it's very toxic. Now I am a fully grown adult with a family of my own.

'I wanted to walk away a lot of times but it always drags me back. Boxing is an addiction. It abuses my body, my mind, my soul. But I feel like it takes me to ecstasy. The rush is unbelievable. It gives me the biggest highs ever, but it also gives me the lowest lows. Boxing is more addictive than any drug ever. Ever. You can't let it go.'

It only takes a quick viewing of his reality show to see how much his family have begged him to pack it in. It seems, though, their words aren't enough.

Fury is set to take on Anthony Joshua in an all-British mega-fight later this year, having eased past Mariusz Wach last weekend. After that, he may well retire again – but will seemingly always keep on coming back.

Tyson Fury has tried to retire from boxing a number of times but finds himself returning

Benoit Assou-Ekotto – Football

A pattern emerges in the list of players who don't like their sport. They engage with it in some form all the time – every decision is based on their career, they have to analyse everything about it, and they spend most of their time performing it.

'I play it enough, don't I?' former Tottenham full back Benoit Assou-Ekotto once argued in an interview with Sky Sports.

'I don't watch football. I don't talk about football away from the game either. I suppose that is unusual. My interests are my friends and music, especially hip-hop. I like Ice Cube and 50 Cent.'

Assou-Ekotto played more than 200 times for Spurs, and didn't do too much wrong. Perhaps his argument proves you don't have to be totally obsessed with what you are doing to reach the top level – or maybe it suggests he could have gone higher if he was.

Former Tottenham defender Benoit Assou-Ekotto (right) is another sports star who does not enjoy watching their sport

Andre Agassi wrote in his autobiography that he 'hates' tennis despite his widespread success

Andre Agassi – Tennis

We have saved the most brutal for last – eight-time Grand Slam tennis champion Andre Agassi hates tennis.

'I play tennis for a living even though I hate tennis,' he wrote in his autobiography. 'I hate it with a dark and secret passion and always have.'

Tell us what you really think, Andre.

It's unclear exactly why the American feels that way, but it could be something to do with top players being on tour for more than 30 weeks a year, having tennis dominate their lives, and the stress involved.

Agassi won all there was to win. Others on this list have too. Still – it is not always enough. Showing that, sometimes, being a sports star may not be all it can seem to be.

Sports.title: Inside the chaotic four days that have left Gianni Infantino fighting to stay in power, how arrogant FIFA president's gamble spectacularly backfired and the contenders looking to overthrow him after World Cup own goal
Sports.content:
It's only two weeks since Gianni Infantino joined President Donald Trump in handing over the Jules Rimet trophy to Spain in New Jersey, wearing a dark suit, blindingly white trainers and the self-satisfied grin of a man celebrating a World Cup triumph of his own.

The FIFA president declared the tournament - and its new 48-team format - a huge success after spending the previous six weeks flitting around North America in a private jet to see his vision become reality.

Anybody else might have been inclined to spend some time reflecting on a World Cup that produced more than its fair share of talking points, or even have some time off.

Not Infantino. He was already moving onto his next project; one that backfired spectacularly this week and has left the 56-year-old Swiss fighting to stay in power.

It took less than four days for his grand plan to sell off football’s crown jewel to private investors for £3.1billion to go up in smoke, from the bombshell news breaking at lunchtime on Tuesday to Infantino’s humiliating statement in the early hours of Saturday confirming it has been scrapped in the face of widespread opposition.

At the end of a seismic week for world football, it is hard to see how he can survive after leading confederations and even senior executives at FIFA turned on the embattled president, and UEFA made the first move towards removing him from office with a vote of no confidence on Saturday morning.

Just days after lauding the 2026 World Cup as a huge, almost personal, success Gianni Infantino saw his iron grip on FIFA's presidency unravel

Why did it unravel so quickly? How did Infantino, a skilled political figure, get it so horribly wrong?

It was clear this wasn’t going to end well from the immediate sense of shock and outrage when The Times revealed that Infantino wanted to create a subsidiary company called FIFA Forward Enterprise to run its flagship events, primarily the World Cup, in a deal that could be worth up to £15bn.

Private investors would have been able to buy stakes in FFE through a group led by Thrive Eternal, a US venture capital company founded by Joshua Kushner, the brother of Trump’s son-in-law Jared.

The 211 member associations were offered a £30m cut if they agreed with the proposals by September 19.

UEFA were the first to voice their opposition with a strongly worded statement agreed unanimously and co-signed by the English FA and Europe’s other 54 associations. They criticised Infantino for ‘a profound failure of leadership’ and presiding over ‘governance by intimidation’, adding: ‘None of us are the owners of football. It is not FIFA’s to sell.’

UEFA followed that up with a threat to boycott the World Cup if Infantino refused to back down and abandon his plans.

Two other Confederations then came out against Infantino on Thursday and Friday. CONCACAF, which represents 41 countries across North America, Central America and the Caribbean, rejected the proposal and expressed ‘deep concerns about the lack of due process surrounding the proposal and the artificially short deadline imposed’.

The Asian Football Confederation followed, saying: ‘Football should never have been placed in such a position. It has exposed fundamental weaknesses in FIFA’s consultation and decision-making processes that must now be addressed.’

Infantino needed a majority of the 211 member nations to vote through his proposals, but already 136 of them were opposed to him.

He doubled down on Friday morning when FIFA issued a statement insisting that ‘nobody is selling football’ - but opposition was growing at an alarming rate.

New Prime Minister Andy Burnham weighed into the controversy, questioning whether Infantino is the right man to lead FIFA anymore.

‘This was an outrageous suggestion,’ said Burnham. ‘The idea that it could even be brought forward, in my view, shows that the FIFA president is the wrong man to lead the organisation.’

More damagingly for Infantino, two of his senior aides turned against him in the space of a few hours.

President of the US Soccer Federation Carlos Cordeiro was a key Infantino ally before he fell on his sword

CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani has emerged as an early contender to stand against Infantino in March

Carlos Cordeiro, who was FIFA’s representative on the White House taskforce for the World Cup and at Infantino’s side throughout, said: ‘As a senior adviser to the FIFA president, a former banker, and a lifelong football fan, I cannot stand by while FIFA considers selling a stake in the World Cup.

‘I had no involvement in this proposal, and I oppose it unequivocally. It is a bad deal for FIFA’s member associations, a bad deal for football, and a bad deal for the long-term future of the game.

‘Selling a permanent stake in football’s most valuable asset to raise $4.2bn makes little sense. It is mortgaging football’s future without any compelling justification.’

If that wasn’t bad enough for Infantino, FIFA’s chief operating officer Kevin Lamour then quit, claiming that Infantino had ‘deceived’ his own administration and accusing him of a ‘lie by omission’. He blasted the plans as a ‘the project of one person’.

‘This (lie) and unilateral exercise of power are not trivial,’ added Lamour. ‘They are indicative of a lack of trust, a lack of transparency, a lack of discernment, a lack of good governance. And a serious lack of respect.

‘Not only must this project not go ahead, but the time has now come for football political leaders to ask themselves the right questions and make the right decisions.

‘My colleagues - some of whom have dedicated their lives to football - deserve better than contempt and intimidation.

‘The ball is now in the court of those who have the power to change things. I know I have a duty of loyalty to my employer. But I also, and above all, have a duty of loyalty to certain values and to the upbringing I have received, and a duty to support my colleagues. And if that means I lose my job, then so be it. I will understand and respect that decision. At least I’ll sleep well tonight.’

Shortly after midnight, Infantino inevitably bowed to the pressure and announced he was scrapping the proposals because ‘it has become clear that the project has created divisions of a nature that, regardless of the level of support, are no longer in the interest of the objective set out in the first place’.

If he thought that would be the end of the matter, however, it quickly became clear on Saturday that the implications could be far greater when UEFA declared a vote of no confidence in him.

Europe’s governing body hit out at Infantino for the ‘shabby, back-room, opaque deal he hatched’ and promised to work with the other confederations in world football to ‘identify those responsible and hold them to account’.

It added: ‘This is a victory for the whole game. But it must not be the end of the story. The proposal has gone. The task of rebuilding trust in FIFA has only just begun.’

So what next for Infantino? He has been in power for 10 years and was expected to win re-election for a fourth term unopposed at the next FIFA congress in Morocco in March.

But with support dwindling fast and UEFA on the warpath, it looks increasingly likely that a rival candidate will stand against him.

CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani has emerged as an early contender, along with current FIFA general secretary Mattias Granstrom and Dariusz Mioduski, a vice-president of the European Football Clubs body.

Two weeks after he had the whole world in his hands, it feels as though Gianni Infantino’s time is almost up.

Sports.title: The tactical shift that proves Enzo Maresca will not be a Pep Guardiola copycat, how new Man City boss may have discovered Antoine Semenyo's best position and the academy star ready to step up after dazzling display against Inter Milan
Sports.content:
The Enzo Maresca era at Manchester City is officially underway after his side lost 3-1 on penalties to lose the Asahi Super Dry Trophy to Inter Milan.

Inside the 50,000-seat Kai Tak Stadium in Hong Kong, Divin Mubama scored the first goal of the Maresca era after brilliant wing play by Antoine Semenyo, only for Inter Milan to respond through Benjamin Pavard.

While City were the better side in the second half, striking the post through youngster Ryan McAidoo, it ultimately went to penalties and despite a delightful Panenka penalty from Claudio Echeverri, misses from Rayan Ait-Nouri, Abdukodir Khusanov and Nico Gonzalez meant City came out as the runners-up.

Many of their World Cup stars are still to come back in and so this was a mixed-up group for Maresca to cut his teeth with.

Daily Mail Sport takes a look at the key things we learned from Maresca's first game in charge in Hong Kong.

The Enzo Maresca era at Manchester City is officially underway after facing Inter Milan in Asia

THE FODEN PUZZLE

There is so much for Enzo Maresca to get stuck into this pre-season but finding a formula to get the best out of Phil Foden should be top of the pile.

Foden has had seven weeks off to refresh, both physically and mentally, after a tough season where criticism was sharp and top performances felt few and far between, given what had come before.

Here was Foden wearing the captain's armband, playing as the No 10 in a side that had been built around him.

Maresca knows exactly what Foden can do, one of the Premier League's absolute best players when he's at the peak of his powers, and finding a way to consistently maximise that could be the difference between winning and losing the biggest prizes.

'He's very important, like the rest,' Maresca said in the lead-up. 'Knowing Phil from years ago, I know how good he is so it's my duty to try to help him to be the Phil that we all want.

'First of all, to be happy, to play football, for him is the most important thing. And as I said, Phil in a good condition and mood can help us to win games and titles - and that's what we want…'

First half here it felt like the game was passing Foden by; a couple of erroneous losses of possession and limited opportunities to build attacks were the headlines.

Second half, with Semenyo operating through the middle ahead of him, Foden looked sharper but still shy of the levels many are urging him to get back to.

Just under 70 minutes of action here for Foden was a reminder that while he is eager to be given a fresh start - and Maresca is ready to give him one - much more will be expected. Both player and manager need to find the formula for success.

Phil Foden showed flashes of what he can do but he needs to deliver much more this season

SHAPE WORK

This is one of the more interesting aspects of any opening pre-season game, particularly when a team is entering a new era following unprecedented success under its greatest ever manager.

So, no, this wasn't copy-and-paste of the Pep Guardiola era by Maresca.

What we saw instead was an aggressive 4-2-4 high press out of possession, with Foden pushed up high alongside striker Divin Mubama, while it was a 3-4-2-1 with the ball with Josko Gvardiol anchoring a back three.

It was not flawless, mind you, with any cheap turnovers of possession allowing Inter Milan to counter quickly, exploiting the space out wide with City's full-backs advanced up the pitch.

In the first half City's midfield was overcrowded and too much space was being afforded out wide. Tijjani Reijnders in particular struggled to influence the game alongside Mateo Kovacic.

There were times too when Maresca was barking at his players to press zonally, albeit the hope will be intensity can add into this when fitness builds up and more first team players add back in.

Inter Milan had chances and many were presented to them by City which will be cause for concern, particularly with space in the forward areas.

But City will be one of pre-season's most interesting watches to see how Maresca's methodology beds in in Manchester.

LEFT IS BEST FOR ANTOINE

When the teamsheet dropped to show Antoine Semenyo as the left winger, rather than the right, where Pep Guardiola liked to play him, there was a collective rejoicing in the City fanbase.

Semenyo is incredibly versatile and while he started out on the right in the early days at Bournemouth, he really kicked into gear as one of the Premier League's best players off the left for the Cherries.

And here in Hong Kong was a great deal of evidence as to why the left side is the best side for the Ghanaian.

One of the criticisms of Semenyo on the right is that there is a predictability to his movements in the final third.

Here against Inter Milan it was wholly unpredictable and therefore a nightmare assignment for Inter Milan's defenders, as Semenyo toyed with them, turning inside and out.

It was Semenyo's burst, really noticeable in the first half before he was moved centrally in the second, that teed up the first goal of the Maresca era when he glided past Andy Diouf and rolled it across for Divin Mubama to slot in.

Jeremy Doku will come back in to the fold but on this evidence, relocating Semenyo should not be top of Maresca's to-do list.

Antoine Semenyo was immense off the left, but saw his game shackled when moved inside

Ryan McAidoo turned Inter Milan's players inside-out in a really promising second half cameo

RYAN IS READY

For those who watch academy football regularly, the sight of Ryan McAidoo turning full-backs inside-out is one that you see on a weekly basis.

The question has been whether it will translate to the senior level. On this evidence, the answer is absolutely yes.

The 18-year-old's cameo in Hong Kong was bursting with quality as he had Inter Milan players bouncing off him, so strong is his low centre of gravity, and he even struck the post after a brilliant solo run.

One of the criticisms of City's wide players at times during the Guardiola era was that they appeared over-coached and had flair in their game limited in favour of ball security.

Well, McAidoo was a breath of fresh air here, running directly at players, relishing any and all one-versus-one match-ups and a bag of tricks that would have made Foden and Semenyo proud.

'He played as well as Semenyo for me,' former City winger Shaun Wright-Phillips said. 'He did more than impress... I loved it.'

Maresca can't help but have been impressed, too. McAidoo is ready.
