Sports.title: Where in Europe should F1 race if the final two rounds cannot go ahead? | Debates and Polls
Sports.content:
Formula 1 CEO Stefano Domenicali has said Europe will be the series’ back-up plan if it cannot hold its final rounds in 2026.

The Qatar and Abu Dhabi grands prix on November 29th and December 6th respectively are in doubt as the war between the US and Iran continues and shows signs of spreading to other neighbouring countries.

Europe has several permanent tracks which haven’t hosted F1 races in 2026 and have the necessary FIA grade one licence. But there is an obvious problem: weather conditions are generally much cooler in Europe in the winter than they are in the Middle East.

So if F1 has to find two alternative venues at short notice, which would be best?

Algarve, Portugal

Previous F1 races: 2

Last F1 race: 2021 Portuguese Grand Prix

Formula 1 is already due to return to Portugal’s undulating Algarve circuit next year, so why not get a head start? Average temperatures in December are around 17C which is much warmer than many other venues in the region.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Hockenheimring, Germany

Previous F1 races: 37

Last F1 race: 2019 German Grand Prix

The thought of Formula 1’s energy-starved 2026 cars attempting to lap the original high-speed Hockenheimring is comical. They would suit the butchered, post-2001 version better, but likely ambient temperatures in the low single digits would present a different challenge.

Imola, Italy

Previous F1 races: 32

Last F1 race: 2025 Emilia Romagna Grand Prix

Domenicali has indicated Imola is a likely venue and there are obvious reasons why: its infrastructure is bang up to date as F1 raced there last year and championship leader Andrea Kimi Antonelli hails from the area (as does the F1 boss). The temperatures will be on the cool side, however – potentially not much warmer than Hockenheim.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Jerez, Spain

Previous F1 races: 7

Last F1 race: 1997 European Grand Prix

Southern Spain offers the best chance of a reasonably warm race, with December temperatures in the 20C region. The tight, slow Jerez circuit would also help disguise the power deficit of the current cars.

Magny-Cours, France

Previous F1 races: 19

Last F1 race: 2008 French Grand Prix

Another track Formula 1 hasn’t visited in a long time which still has the necessary FIA grade to hold a grand prix. Central France would be rather chilly, though.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Motorland Aragon, Spain

Previous F1 races: None

The only FIA grade one track in Europe which F1 hasn’t raced at, which will inevitably count against it. Motorland Aragon is a rather typical modern autodrome-style circuit. Weather conditions in December would be a good chunk cooler than Jerez if F1 sprang a surprise by choosing this circuit as a venue for a third race in Spain this year.

Mugello, Italy

Previous F1 races: 1

Last F1 race: 2020 Tuscan Grand Prix

Mugello joined the F1 calendar as a one-off during the Covid-hit 2020 season and produced one of the year’s most memorable races, not least because a series of shunts meant several restarts were required. It would be very cool in December, though all those long, fast corners should help keep heat in the tyres.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Nurburgring, Germany

Previous F1 races: 19 (new circuit), 41 (total)

Last F1 race: 2020 Eifel Grand Prix

Another track F1 last visited during the pandemic, and one with an abundance of heritage. But like many other venues on this list, cold conditions would be a factor.

Paul Ricard, France

Previous F1 races: 18

Last F1 race: 2022 French Grand Prix

Paul Ricard was not F1’s most inspiring circuit to begin with: then it was shortened, then revived as a test track. F1 later returned to the longer track, albeit with a slow chicane before one of its best corners.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

I say

When F1’s calendar was disrupted six years ago by Covid-19, it was deeply unfortunate, but at least it was understood that the cause was mere misfortune. Advert | Become a Supporter & go ad-free It is deeply saddening to see a similar situation now playing out due to those who have decided to inflict pain, suffering and death on others. Compared to that, the rescheduling of a couple of motor races matters not one iota. However the fact remains that the outside world does affect life in F1’s ‘bubble’ and will continue to. I cannot think of many circuits you could drop Losail and Yas Marina for which would not constitute an improvement. Of course what I’d most like to see is F1 take in the most spectacular and demanding tracks available – Imola is a decent choice, but Mugello would be even better. Then reality kicks in. When F1 went to Mugello six years ago the cars were monstrously fast, not the feeble new generation which coast into the quick corners to save their batteries. Around a super-quick track like Mugello they would be badly starved of energy. Given that, arguably one of the slower tracks would suit the current cars better. But I’m not going to pretend I actually want to see F1 hunting out the tightest, slowest circuits so its drivers have plenty of opportunities to charge their batteries. I’ve more than had my fill of ‘clipping’ and ‘yo-yo racing’. Forget replacing Losail and Yas Marina, I’d rather the season ended two weeks early.

Sports.title: Former F1 boss Boullier becomes promoter of World Rally Championship | Brief
Sports.content:
Former Formula 1 team principal Eric Boullier will has a new role as the promoter of the World Rally Championship. He will also be responsible for running the European Rally Championship in a new deal announced by the FIA.

“I take on this challenge with enthusiasm and determination, but also with humility and a strong sense of responsibility, to make these exceptional championships even more compelling,” said Boullier. “Alongside the FIA and our partners, we want to make every round a spectacular event, designed to thrill fans around the world.”

Sports.title: On This Day: Lauda survives fiery, near-fatal crash at Nurburgring | Brief
Sports.content:
On this day in 1976 Niki Lauda was fortunate to survive a shocking crash during the German Grand Prix at the Nurburgring. His Ferrari exploded into flames after striking a barrier.

Lauda survived thanks to the efforts of rivals Arturo Merzario, Guy Edwards, Brett Lunger and Harald Ertl, who stopped their cars and helped to pull the world champion from the burning wreckage.

Nonetheless Lauda sustained serious burns and lung injuries. He was leading the world championship at the time of his crash and made an early return in a bid to stop McLaren’s James Hunt beating him to the title. But confronted with dire conditions at the season finale in Fuji, Lauda opted not to race, and Hunt won the title. The story of the season was dramatised in Ron Howard’s 2013 film Rush.

Sports.title: Featured Comment: Expect changes to IndyCar’s dramatic new 2028 car design | Brief
Sports.content:
IndyCar has produced some attractive designs for its new car but expect to see some significant changes when the real thing hits the track in 2028, says Greasemonkey:

The first change to a real race car will be the wings.

Swept wings in renders have often been a thing, but are usually worse than straight wings, and often turn straight in production. Generic swept wings have to do with compressible air flow and/or structural twist. Not a thing at Indy speeds. So sweep makes no sense at least until ground through many many many iterations of CFD and tunnel runs, which might mutate some sweep in for other reasons.

And even then, more often than not, they’ll be more straight than not.

Sports.title: Fans who attended 2023 Las Vegas Grand Prix offered partial refund | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Formula 1 fans who attended the first day of track action at the inaugural Las Vegas Grand Prix have been offered partial refunds.

The first practice session at the Las Vegas Strip Circuit was halted after 10 minutes when a loose drain cover caused serious damage to Carlos Sainz Jnr’s Ferrari.

The session did not resume and the second practice session was postponed by two hours in order for track workers to make repairs. The late start meant the session took place after the security personnel’s shifts ended, which meant the spectators who remained had to be evicted from the grandstands.

A group of disappointed fans therefore brought a lawsuit against Formula 1 commercial rights holder Liberty Media, which promotes the Las Vegas race. Liberty Media has offered a settlement of $3,047,986 (£2.26m) to be shared between them, which the offer notes is “not an admission of wrongdoing”.

In its statement on the case, Jack Diep, et. al. v. Liberty Media Corporation, et. al., the United States District Court for the District of Nevada confirmed: “A settlement has been reached in a class action lawsuit between defendants Liberty Media Corporation and Las Vegas Grand Prix, Inc and persons or entities who alleged that they, and the settlement class, are entitled to partial refunds of the ticket price for the 2023 Las Vegas Grand Prix because [the] defendants had to delay the FP2 free practice session and subsequently revoked the settlement class’s admission without cause before the FP2 free practice session began.”

“The proposed settlement is not an admission of wrongdoing by [the] defendants,” it added. “[The] defendants deny all allegations of wrongdoing and disclaim all liability regarding all claims in the lawsuit.”

Key F1 figures rejected criticism of the disruption at the time. Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff angrily claimed it was “completely ridiculous” to claim the incident reflected badly on F1.

“You’re speaking about a fucking drain cover that’s been undone, that has happened before,” Wolff told a journalist during an official FIA press conference. “That’s nothing – it’s FP1. Give credit to the people that have set up this grand prix, that have made this sport much bigger than it ever was.” The FIA later formally warned Wolff over his choice of language.

Sports.title: Why Mercedes believe Antonelli was especially unlucky with his grid penalty | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Mercedes believe Andrea Kimi Antonelli was unfortunate to receive a grid penalty for his yellow flag infringement in qualifying last weekend.

The world champion received a three-place grid drop for failing to slow sufficiently for yellow flags. The stewards pointed out Antonelli’s time through the relevant mini-sector rose by just 0.03 seconds compared to “his best time for that mini-sector.”

However Mercedes’ deputy technical director Simone Resta said Antonelli had lost time in that mini-sector compared to other laps.

“The benchmark lap being used for comparison wasn’t actually an ideal lap,” said Resta in a video released by the team. “In that particular sector, the reference wasn’t representative of Kimi’s true pace.

“That made the situation more difficult because even after lifting, he was effectively being compared against a slower-than-optimal sector.”

The stewards accepted Antonelli had lifted the throttle 16 metres earlier and reduced his speed by 14kph in response to the single yellow flag. They ruled this was “insufficient”.

A similar situation occured earlier in the season in Austria where both Mercedes drivers passed single yellow flags on their final qualifying laps. Antonelli slowed down significantly and abandoned his lap, while George Russell lifted the throttle then resumed his lap and took pole position.

Resta said Antonelli had tried to back off but keep going in Hungary. “Kimi pointed out afterwards that if you compared the sector to FP3, when the car was heavier on fuel and therefore naturally slower, he was still quicker despite lifting,” he said.

“In some ways it was a perfect storm. He did react, but because of the reference lap being used, the reduction wasn’t enough to satisfy the requirement.”

Sports.title: Thomas Hearns Destroys Pipino Cuevas To Win First World Title
Sports.content:
Hearns (28-0, 26 KOs) held the USBA welterweight title under the guidance of Emanuel Steward at Kronk Gym. Cuevas (27-6, 24 KOs) received the larger purse at a reported $1.5 million compared to $500,000 for the challenger, but roughly 12,000 fans inside Joe Louis Arena backed the hometown favorite.

Hearns refused to let Cuevas establish his trademark pressure from the opening bell. His snapping jab repeatedly found the target while straight right hands pierced the champion’s defense. Cuevas struggled to work his way inside as Hearns controlled the range with speed, timing and accuracy. A sharp left hook briefly staggered the Mexican champion before another series of right hands left him badly shaken at the bell.

A crushing right hand ended matters in the second round, sending Cuevas face first onto the canvas for the first knockdown of his professional career. He beat the count, but his legs betrayed him. Trainer Lupe Sanchez climbed into the ring before the action resumed, prompting referee Stanley Christodoulou to stop the fight at 2:39 of the second round.

The knockout launched Hearns toward superstardom. He defended the WBA championship, met Sugar Ray Leonard in one of boxing’s biggest fights the following year, and eventually captured world titles in six weight divisions. Many historians regard the destruction of Cuevas as the night Thomas Hearns established himself among boxing’s elite.

Sports.title: Adrien Broner: Tank Would Knock William Zepeda Out Cold
Sports.content:
“Now, he’s a champ. Tank would knock him out cold. I’m talking about an ugly one,” Broner said on social media.

Whether fans ever see that fight is another question.

Davis has not fought since 2025, and nothing suggests Zepeda sits at the top of his list when he returns to the ring. One of boxing’s biggest attractions still has several major opportunities available.

A meeting with Shakur Stevenson carries championship implications and years of history. Ryan Garcia and Devin Haney remain among boxing’s biggest commercial draws, while Conor Benn’s popularity in the United Kingdom offers another sizable event.

Zepeda also has unfinished business at lightweight. Interim WBC champion Jadier Herrera was bypassed when the sanctioning body ordered Zepeda and Roach to fight for the vacant title. Herrera now has a strong case for the next shot at the belt.

Stylistically, Zepeda presents a difficult matchup. His nonstop punch volume, body attack and conditioning would force Davis to fight at a pace unlike many of his recent opponents. Davis also went the distance with both Roach and Isaac Cruz, making Broner’s prediction of a knockout far from certain.

Broner’s opinion reflects one view of a matchup many fans would like to see. Whether Davis ever decides to pursue Zepeda remains a separate question.

Sports.title: William Zepeda Says Lamont Roach Expected The Wrong Fighter
Sports.content:
After winning the vacant WBC lightweight title with a unanimous decision Saturday night at The Theater at Virgin Hotels in Las Vegas, Zepeda explained that he spent the year following his loss to Shakur Stevenson reshaping parts of his style. The adjustments paid off against Roach, who struggled to establish the counterpunching rhythm that had carried him through previous title fights.

“I think he expected me to come straight forward the whole fight,” Zepeda said. “Instead I boxed smarter, managed my pace, went in and out. I showed I can do more than just throw punches.”

The Mexican southpaw still applied the relentless pressure that has defined his career, but he varied his attack with sharper footwork and better distance control. Rather than giving Roach the same looks throughout the fight, Zepeda repeatedly stepped in to work the body before moving back outside, limiting Roach’s opportunities to land his right hand cleanly.

Sports.title: Lamont ‘The Reaper’ Roach Loses To William ‘Camarón’ Zepeda
Sports.content:
Lamont “The Reaper” Roach Jr. (25-2-3, 10 KOs) of Washington, D.C., dropped a unanimous decision to former interim WBC lightweight champion William “Camarón” Zepeda (34-1, 27 KOs) of San Mateo Atenco, Mexico, in a bout for the vacant WBC lightweight championship.

Roach started well, using his timing and right hand to edge the opening round against the southpaw. Zepeda responded in the second, controlling most of the round before Roach landed a hard right hand late that briefly knocked him off balance.

Zepeda gradually took command from the third through the fifth rounds, outworking Roach with steady pressure and backing him up with combinations. He finished the fifth strongly and continued dictating the action in the sixth, although Roach closed the round with a better final minute.

The seventh through ninth rounds belonged to Zepeda as he maintained a relentless pace. Roach enjoyed one of his better rounds in the tenth despite suffering a bloody nose, then finished the eleventh with renewed urgency knowing he needed something dramatic to change the fight.

Roach boxed aggressively in the twelfth, but it wasn’t enough to erase the deficit. The judges scored the bout 117-111, 117-111, and 118-110 for Zepeda.

Referee: Harvey Dock

Co-Main Event

IBF lightweight champion Raymond “Danger” Muratalla (25-0, 17 KOs) of Fontana, California, retained his title with a unanimous decision over former Olympic gold medalist and former WBC super featherweight champion Robson “Nino O Brabo” Conceição (21-4-1, 10 KOs).

Muratalla controlled the opening two rounds before repeatedly catching Conceição with right hands in the third. He continued investing in body shots through the middle rounds, while Conceição enjoyed his best success in the sixth with a left uppercut that earned him one of his few clear rounds.

Muratalla regained control from the seventh through the tenth, consistently beating Conceição to the punch and limiting his offense. The final two rounds were competitive, but Muratalla did enough to preserve his comfortable lead.

The judges scored the fight 118-110, 119-109, and 119-109.

Referee: Thomas Taylor

Raul Curiel Majority Decisions Quinton Randall

2016 Olympian and NABF welterweight champion Raul “Cugar” Curiel (18-0-1, 14 KOs) won a majority decision over former WBC USA Silver champion Quinton “Sugar Man” Randall (17-4-1, 4 KOs) over 10 rounds.

Curiel started slowly but did enough to edge the opening round. Randall used his reach effectively in the second and third rounds, keeping Curiel on the outside while scoring with counters.

Curiel regained control in the fourth and fifth rounds before finishing the sixth with a sharp three-punch combination. He continued pressing the action in the seventh and enjoyed his strongest round in the eighth, hurting Randall with a right hand to the chin during the closing seconds.

A right to the body had Randall backing up in the ninth, and Curiel closed the fight with another solid round to secure the decision.

Scores: 95-95, 97-93 and 100-90.

Referee: Tony Weeks.

Charles Conwell Stops Paul Kroll

Charles “Bad News” Conwell (22-1, 17 KOs) stopped Paul “The Punisher” Kroll (12-1-2, 8 KOs) at 2:38 of the ninth round.

Conwell controlled the opening two rounds, backing Kroll to the ropes with steady pressure. Kroll enjoyed a good third round until Conwell landed a left hand that sent him into the ropes for a knockdown. Kroll also suffered a cut during the fight.

Conwell continued dictating the pace through the middle rounds, although Kroll rallied with competitive efforts in the sixth, seventh and eighth. Referee Robert Hoyle warned Kroll for holding in the seventh.

Early in the ninth, Conwell landed a crushing left to the liver that badly hurt Kroll. As Kroll stopped returning punches, Hoyle stepped in to wave off the bout.

Both fighters were returning after layoffs of more than a year.

Fabian Guzman Decisions Aaron Coley

Middleweight Fabian Guzman (11-0, 8 KOs) earned an eight-round unanimous decision over southpaw Aaron Coley (17-6-2, 7 KOs).

Coley found success countering early, but Guzman consistently outworked him and landed the cleaner punches. Guzman increased his output during the seventh, forcing Coley onto the defensive.

Knowing he needed something dramatic, Coley pressed forward in the final round, but Guzman boxed well enough to close out the victory.

Scores: 78-74 twice and 79-73.

Referee: Robert Hoyle.

Joel Iriarte Stops Jorge Lagunas

Joel Iriarte (11-0, 10 KOs) stopped Jorge “Piolas” Lagunas (19-10, 16 KOs) at 2:48 of the eighth and final round.

Iriarte controlled the bout from the outset with steady body work and physical strength. By the sixth and seventh rounds he repeatedly forced Lagunas to the ropes, where he unloaded combinations.

The eighth followed the same pattern before referee Tony Weeks halted the contest as Lagunas absorbed unanswered punishment.

Gael Cabrera Outpoints Francisco Portillo

Gael “El Terrorista” Cabrera (12-0, 7 KOs) won an eight-round unanimous decision over Francisco “Rayito” Portillo (20-15-2, 11 KOs).

Cabrera controlled the opening three rounds with accurate punching and sharp counters. Portillo pressed the action through the middle rounds, but Cabrera consistently answered with cleaner shots.

Cabrera closed the fight strongly to remain unbeaten.

Scores: 79-73 twice and 80-72.

Referee: Harvey Dock.

Dalis Kaleiopu Scores First-Round Knockout

Dalis Kaleiopu (9-0, 7 KOs) stopped Yeyery “La Buija” Castillo (14-3, 11 KOs) at 2:37 of the opening round.

Kaleiopu hurt Castillo with a right hand midway through the round before another right sent him crashing to the canvas. Castillo was unable to beat referee Robert Hoyle’s count.

Juan Carlos Becerril Upsets Dylan Capetillo

Juan Carlos Becerril (3-0, 2 KOs) stopped Dylan “La Amenaza” Capetillo (2-1, 1 KO) at 2:59 of the third round in a major upset.

Capetillo enjoyed success through the opening two rounds and appeared in control before Becerril turned the fight around in the third. A perfectly timed left hook landed flush on the chin, dropping Capetillo heavily.

Referee Thomas Taylor completed the count, giving Becerril the biggest victory of his young career.

Ring Announcer: Mark Fratto.

Sports.title: William Zepeda Overwhelms Lamont Roach Jr. To Capture WBC Lightweight Title
Sports.content:
Coming off back-to-back majority draws against Gervonta Davis and Isaac Cruz, Roach (25-2-3, 10 KOs) hoped to become a two-division world champion. Instead, he spent much of the evening trying to slow one of boxing’s busiest offensive fighters.

Zepeda (34-1, 27 KOs) established the pace almost immediately, cutting off the ring with intelligent footwork and forcing Roach backward behind a nonstop attack. The Mexican southpaw mixed head and body shots while maintaining the high punch output that has become his trademark, rarely allowing Roach enough time to set his feet for counters.

“Shakur gave me a great test. I think he gave me a great exam. During the year I was out of the ring, we worked on what we were missing,” said Zepeda to DAZN after the fight. “We implemented some new things tonight, but we still have to keep growing to stay among the elite.”

Single counters produced Roach’s best moments, but the openings disappeared quickly. Zepeda stepped back inside after nearly every exchange, keeping the pressure on before Roach could put together extended combinations.

Clean counters continued to land in spots, yet Zepeda answered by pushing the action and backing Roach toward the ropes. There were no knockdowns, though the pattern changed little over the second half of the fight as Roach searched for openings while moving backward.

“We thought he was a one-trick pony. He actually used his feet. He was stepping back and not allowing me to get my counters off,” said Roach on what went wrong against Zepeda. “He did it the whole fight. I had to switch a couple things up, but I just didn’t succeed.”

Repeated body shots gradually slowed Roach’s movement, allowing Zepeda to remain in punching range for much of the fight.

Sports.title: Raymond Muratalla Eyes 140 After Dominant Win Over Robson Conceição
Sports.content:
Despite the lopsided scorecards, Muratalla did not believe he performed at his highest level.

“I felt good. I don’t think I gave my best performance. I think making 135 is a little hard for me. I’m going to feel a lot better at 140,” Muratalla said after the fight. “Yes, this will be my last fight at 135. It’s tough making this weight and I’m looking forward to moving up.”

The comments immediately raise questions about how much longer Muratalla plans to remain at lightweight. He captured the vacant IBF title earlier this year and successfully defended it against Conceição, but his postfight remarks indicate the strain of making weight is becoming a significant factor.

Conceição, a former Olympic champion who previously campaigned at 130 pounds, showed toughness by lasting the distance but spent much of the fight trying to solve Muratalla’s jab and body attack. The challenger remained competitive in spots, yet he struggled to slow the champion’s pace or force exchanges on his terms.

If Muratalla decides to move to junior welterweight, he would enter one of boxing’s deepest divisions with his unbeaten record intact and a world title already on his resume. His performance against Conceição confirmed he remains one of the sport’s most technically polished young champions, even if he believes his best boxing will come five pounds heavier.

Sports.title: Richardson Hitchins Sees Opening As Devin Haney Needs Opponent
Sports.content:
That left an opening for another welterweight contender, and Hitchins immediately stepped forward.

Hitchins is coming off a 10-round unanimous decision over Ricardo Salas in his first fight at 147 pounds for Zuffa Boxing. He has publicly pursued a fight with Haney for years, but the circumstances are different now because Haney no longer has an opponent lined up.

The biggest question is not whether Haney notices the challenge. It’s whether fans want the matchup. Both fighters are known for their technical styles, leaving many observers uncertain about the bout’s commercial appeal compared with other names Haney has been linked to.

Hitchins recognized an opportunity and acted on it. With Haney searching for his next opponent, the former IBF light welterweight champion has inserted himself into the conversation at a time when the door may finally be open.

Sports.title: Juan Carlos Becerril Stuns Dylan Capetillo With Third Round TKO
Sports.content:
Becerril (3-0, 2 KOs) stayed composed and waited for his opening. Late in the third round, he landed a crushing left hook that caught Capetillo flush and sent him crashing to the canvas. Capetillo beat the count, but his legs were unsteady, and he struggled to convince referee Thomas Taylor that he was ready to continue.

Taylor halted the contest at 2:59 of the third round, awarding Becerril a technical knockout after deciding Capetillo was no longer able to defend himself. The dramatic finish silenced the crowd and instantly changed the direction of the fight.

Capetillo entered the bout as one of Golden Boy’s youngest professional prospects after turning pro earlier this year. The setback serves as an early reminder of the risks young fighters face against opponents with confidence and punching power, even in the opening stages of their careers.

Becerril, meanwhile, leaves Las Vegas with the biggest victory of his career. After recovering from an early knockdown, the unbeaten Mexican prospect showed composure under pressure and seized his opportunity when it arrived, handing Capetillo the first defeat of his professional career.

Ghana News.title: KNUST calls for collective action to tackle student mental health, financial pressures
Ghana News.content:
The Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Kumasi (KNUST) has called for a collective approach to addressing growing challenges facing students, including mental health concerns, financial pressures, loneliness and career uncertainty, saying student well-being is a shared responsibility essential to producing resilient and socially responsible graduates.

The call was made during the second edition of the Directorate of Student Affairs (DoSA) Day, held on the theme, "Promoting a Collective Stakeholder Commitment to Student Affairs."

Speaking at the event, KNUST Pro Vice-Chancellor, Professor David Asamoah, said universities must go beyond academic instruction to create environments that enable students to thrive intentionally.

He noted that while academic excellence remains central to the University's mission, producing ethically grounded, emotionally resilient and socially responsible graduates is equally important.

"It reminds us that student affairs is everyone's responsibility. A great university is not measured solely by its infrastructure, research output or global rankings, but by the quality of graduates it produces," he said.

According to him, today's students face unprecedented challenges, including mental health concerns, financial pressures, loneliness, career uncertainty and the distractions of an increasingly digital world.

Professor Asamoah urged students to make use of the support systems available through the Directorate of Student Affairs.

"Seek help whenever you need it. Do not suffer in silence. Participate actively in leadership programmes, student organisations, volunteer activities and mentorship opportunities," he advised.

Director of Student Affairs, Professor Marian Asantewah Nkansah, said the Directorate exists to support students throughout their university journey to ensure they enjoy a fulfilling and rewarding campus experience.

"Our goal is to help students become not just graduates, but well-rounded personalities who will carry our institution's name forward and contribute meaningfully to nation building," she said.

She explained that DoSA Day was introduced to highlight the Directorate's interventions and deepen appreciation of its role in promoting students' welfare.

"The DoSA Day initiative was instituted to showcase to the entire university community, especially to our students and stakeholders, the initiatives and interventions that we have put in place for our students' well-being," Professor Nkansah said.

Chairman of the DoSA Day Planning Committee, Professor Samuel Asamoah Sakyi, described the celebration as an opportunity to strengthen collaboration among stakeholders while recognising excellence in student support.

He encouraged participants to actively engage in the day's activities, build partnerships and familiarise themselves with the range of support services available to students.

"Student affairs is not the responsibility of one directorate alone, but the shared responsibility of the entire university community and its stakeholders," he said.

As part of the celebration, the Directorate honoured 40 former and current staff members for their outstanding contributions to student affairs at KNUST.

The awardees included former directors, deans, vice deans, administrative heads, hall masters, senior tutors and other staff whose dedication has helped shape student life and welfare at the University.

Ghana News.title: Two sets of laws for two sets of people in Ghana – Godfred Dame on Sedina Tamakloe case
Ghana News.content:
Attorney General and Minister of Justice, Godfred Dame

Former Attorney-General and Minister for Justice, Godfred Yeboah Dame, has criticised what he describes as the growing perception that Ghana’s justice system operates “two sets of laws for two sets of people” following the acquittal and discharge of former MASLOC Chief Executive, Sedina Tamakloe Attionu.

In a press release issued on Friday July 31, 2026, the former Attorney-General argued that the Court of Appeal’s decision has deepened public concerns over whether political affiliation now influences accountability within Ghana’s criminal justice system.

Beyond the acquittal itself, Dame contended that the development fits what he described as a broader pattern in the conduct of criminal prosecutions.

He alleged that the current Attorney-General has shown a tendency to discontinue cases involving leading members and affiliates of the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC), while opposition figures continue to face prosecution in corruption-related cases.

Referring to the public reaction to the Court of Appeal’s decision, Godfred Dame maintained that the criticism surrounding Sedina Attionu’s acquittal was understandable.

He argued that the prosecution had led cogent evidence during the trial, evidence which, according to him, had been widely reported by the media and was therefore well known to the public.

The former Attorney-General further asserted that the Sedina case has reinforced the perception that equality before the law is no longer applied evenly.

In his view, the principle now exists “only in theory”, warning that confidence in the justice system suffers when citizens believe justice is administered differently depending on political affiliation.

Dame also took aim at what he described as the government’s prosecutorial priorities. He argued that Ghanaians should expect higher standards from an administration which, according to him, discontinued criminal cases involving some of its leading members upon assuming office, while subsequently embarking on prosecutions of leading opposition figures under what he characterised as difficult trial conditions.

While expressing those concerns, Dame rejected attempts by NDC communicators to attribute Sedina Attionu’s acquittal to the previous Akufo-Addo administration.

He maintained that neither he nor the Office of the Attorney-General was served with any notice of appeal during his tenure and insisted that the appeal only became active after the change of government.

To support that position, Dame recounted that his principal focus as Attorney-General was not an appeal but the enforcement of the High Court’s judgment.

He disclosed that his office successfully pursued Attionu’s extradition from the United States, noting that a United States District Court upheld Ghana’s extradition request in April 2026.

Concluding his statement, Mr Dame cautioned that a justice system in which political allies allegedly avoid accountability while political opponents struggle to have their rights respected reflects poorly on the State.

He stressed that public confidence in the administration of justice can only be preserved if the law is applied fairly, consistently and without regard to political affiliation.

Ghana News.title: Joy and pain – celebrating Nubuke Foundation at 20
Ghana News.content:
In today’s world where we are incessantly bombarded with visual imagery wherever we go, one tends to overlook the power of sound. Audio experiences have been overshadowed, yet we shouldn’t forget their ability to subtly transport a listener into another person’s world- while they share stories and memories of joy, pain, events and many more.

In the past couple of months, I have had the honour of sharing my thoughts, vision and memories of the journey as a co-founder of Nubuke Foundation.

The first steps of this journey actually began almost 25 years ago.

I had the pleasure of speaking with Florence Amerley Adu on her Glocal podcast on a rainy morning in Accra, recalling who, why, how, and where Nubuke Foundation?

I was reminded of the days when we kept diaries. A peek into your diaries vividly brought the past back, and you disappeared into another world of memories, laughing at things long forgotten or saddened by losses along the way.

Listen to my conversation with Florence here: https://lnkd.in/exgPugvA

My second conversation with Michelle Renee Jackson (https://lnkd.in/exSkGDBQ ), however, turned out to be a pleasant surprise. It was again an honour to be the first guest from Africa to be interviewed on the Black Philanthropy podcast.

Even though I don't usually refer to myself as a philanthropist, what stood out for me as we began to delve and share stories is how much humankind has in common. I came away from this conversation feeling closer to the African American community - who always seem so far away across the Atlantic - than ever before.

Michelle’s thoughtful questions highlighted and opened up into the world of philanthropy, stressing why it mattered. As we are all connected to the bigger picture, we must recognise that every action we take will always have an impact on the community in which we belong and even beyond.

What impact or legacy do you choose to leave in your society?

My conversation with Michelle can be listened to here: https://lnkd.in/e-A2M7pV

Nubuke Foundation’s 20-year legacy is visible in the visual arts and culture of Ghana and worldwide.

Happy listening.

If you are moved by our story, do get in touch, because our work is not yet done.

Philanthropists need philanthropists too!

About Nubuke Foundation

Nubuke Foundation is a prominent visual art and cultural institution located at 7 Lome Close in East Legon, Accra, Ghana. Established in April 2006 by Odile Tevie, Kofi Tutu Agyare, and Kofi Setordji, it serves as a dynamic creative hub dedicated to preserving, recording, and promoting contemporary art, heritage, and culture in Ghana.

For more information about our anniversary programme in October, follow our socials:

Instagram: nubuke_foundation | Facebook: Nubuke Foundation | LinkedIn: Nubuke Foundation

-

The author is Odile Tevie, Co-Founder and Director of Nubuke Foundation.

Ghana News.title: WestJet flight attendants go on strike after talks fall through, grounding flights
Ghana News.content:
Flight attendants at Canada's WestJet went on strike on Sunday ‌after failing to reach a deal with the country's second-largest carrier, grounding flights during the busy summer travel season.

The Canadian Union of Public Employees, which represents 4,400 flight attendants at the carrier, majority-owned by Onex Corp, is seeking pay ​for its members from the time they check in until they clock out, which is ​not currently the case.

The strike follows a four-day work stoppage by flight attendants last August ⁠at larger rival Air Canada, highlighting broader efforts by flight attendants in Canada and the U.S. ​to challenge a compensation structure that mostly pays cabin crew when an aircraft is in motion.

The union ​had given 72 hours' notice on Thursday to the airline signaling that a strike could come if talks failed to produce an agreement, following which WestJet issued a lock-out notice.

The union on Sunday said it had tried until the last minute ​to reach a deal but that “WestJet's offer did not go far enough.”

"We are on strike because ​we believe we deserve better. We are ready to go back to the table to settle," said Alia Hussain, president ‌of ⁠the union's WestJet component.

The airline, which has a domestic market share of about 30%, confirmed the work stoppage and said it would refund or reaccommodate affected passengers.

"We presented a proposal... to offer an hourly rate covering all time before and after flights, plus a double-digit wage increase in year one among other priorities the ​union raised. Unfortunately, it ​wasn't accepted," WestJet CEO ⁠Alexis von Hoensbroech said.

Patty Hajdu, Canada's jobs minister, described the development as disappointing. "A strike or lockout does not mean an agreement can't be reached; the ​expectation is that parties can and should come to an agreement at the ​bargaining table," she ⁠added.

The airline canceled 309 flights through Sunday night in anticipation of the strike. It did so to "minimize the risk of stranding guests and aircraft."

The Canadian government intervened to stop the Air Canada strike last year, which was ⁠later defied ​by flight attendants. The union's WestJet division said it hoped ​the Canadian government would not interfere in the bargaining process.

Ghana News.title: Five dead, 41 missing, after Indonesia ferry catches fire
Ghana News.content:
Five people have been found dead and 41 are missing after an Indonesian ferry carrying at least 250 people caught fire while at sea, officials say.

The captain of the ship reported the fire - off Madura island - as the vessel sailed from the country's second-largest city, Surabaya in East Java, to Makassar in South Sulawesi, according to Basarnas, the National Search and Rescue Agency.

Footage played by local Indonesian news outlet iNews shows large numbers of people in life jackets on what appears to be a lifeboat.

Other clips show people climbing down from the ferry that has flames and plumes of smoke coming from the top of the vessel.

Basarnas posted a video to its TikTok, with a statement saying at 08:24 (02:24 GMT) the Surabaya Search and Rescue office received information that passenger ship KMP Mutiara Sentosa 2 was on fire.

"Based on information from the shipping company, the fire occurred at around 06:00-07:00 (00:00-01:00 GMT)."

Later, Basarnas said it got confirmation the ferry "was almost entirely engulfed in flames" as "passengers held on in the ship's bridge and bow while awaiting rescue".

In some of the footage, can be seen jumping into the sea, with crowds of people in life jackets gathering and lifebuoys being thrown to some before they are carried into a rescue ship.

Ghana News.title: Mahama concerned over unhygienic fish drying video at Tema Newtown
Ghana News.content:
President John Dramani Mahama has expressed concern over a video recorded by the Buzstop Boys, showing fish being dried in what he described as unhygienic conditions at Tema Newtown.

Speaking at Ringway Gospel Centre Assemblies of God, Mahama said the video, which captured the sanitation situation at the fishing community, revealed the poor environmental conditions under which fish meant for the market was being processed.

"The fish is supposed to come into the market. These Buzstop Boys went to Tema Newtown, and if you see the rubbish there, they were drying fish. And that fish is supposed to come into the market," he said.

He said the footage highlights the urgent need for improved sanitation and better management of food processing areas to protect public health.

Mahama also commended the work of the Buzstop Boys, a group known for drawing public attention to sanitation challenges through their environmental advocacy activities.

The President further urged Ghanaians to adopt responsible waste disposal habits, warning that throwing sachet water wrappers, Styrofoam containers, food packaging and other refuse into drains contributes to flooding.

Quoting James 2:17, which states that "faith without works is dead," Mahama said environmental cleanliness requires action and must be reflected in the behaviour and character of citizens.

Ghana News.title: Okyeame Kwame: A true example of a national asset
Ghana News.content:
In an era where celebrity influence is often measured by social media clout, viral trends, or fleeting moments of fame, few public figures manage to transcend entertainment to become permanent fixtures of national progress.

In Ghana, one name stands out as the gold standard of purposeful celebrity: Kwame Nsiah-Apau, universally known as Okyeame Kwame. Earning the title of a "national asset" is no small feat. It requires consistency, unmatched patriotism, intellectual depth, and a career devoid of toxic controversies.

With his latest appointment as the Ghana Health Service’s National Hepatitis Ambassador, Okyeame Kwame has once again cemented his place not just as the "Rap Doctor," but as Ghana’s ultimate civic champion.

The Evolution of a Civic Icon

For over two decades, Okyeame Kwame has redefined what it means to be a musician in Africa. While his lyrical prowess and timeless discography earned him legendary status in the highlife and hiplife genres, his dedication to social impact has truly set him apart.

Governments change, political tides shift, and ministerial portfolios rotate, but Okyeame Kwame remains a constant pillar of trust for state institutions. His journey through various high-profile national portfolios tells the story of a citizen deeply invested in every facet of Ghana's development:

The National Hepatitis Ambassador: In his latest monumental national role, Okyeame Kwame was officially designated by the Ghana Health Service to lead the charge against viral hepatitis. This is far from a ceremonial title; it is a continuation of over 18 years of personal dedication, massive free public screenings, and advocacy that he spearheaded long before official state instruments caught up with his vision.

The Made in Ghana Ambassador: Appointed by the Ministry of Trade and Industry, Okyeame Kwame took patriotism to the studio and the streets. Through his critically acclaimed Made in Ghana album, his deliberate projection of local fashion, and his relentless advocacy for patronizing local goods and services, he became the face of economic nationalism.

Tourism Ambassador: Under the Ministry of Culture and Tourism, he leveraged his global appeal and deep understanding of Ghanaian heritage to market the country's rich cultural tapestry to the rest of the world, championing arts as a vehicle for national identity.

Climate Change & Agricultural Advocates: Beyond culture and health, his footprint stretches into environmental sustainability as a former Climate Change Ambassador, alongside his voluntary patriotic efforts supporting agricultural initiatives like Feed Ghana.

Why Okyeame Kwame is a National Asset

What transforms a talented artist into a national treasure? For Okyeame Kwame, it boils down to three core pillars:

Institution Building Over Personal Glory: Many celebrities lend their faces to brands for quick financial gains. Okyeame Kwame often marries his commercial art with national policy, aligning his private initiatives with state goals—frequently offering his time and platform voluntarily out of pure civic duty.

Intellectual and Moral Consistency: Popularly known for his articulate delivery, sharp intellect, and gentlemanly demeanor, Okyeame Kwame provides a blueprint for youth mentorship. Whether he is speaking on dyslexia awareness (drawing from his own childhood experiences) or financial literacy for creatives, he projects a polished, progressive image of the Ghanaian intellect. His willingness to go back to school, during the peak of his career encouraged many creatives to also seek higher education. Co-authoring the book Love Locked Down with his wife Annica Nsiah-Apau created an example and a guide for young families seeking stability in their relationships.

Longevity and Relevance: Staying relevant in the entertainment industry for five years is hard; staying culturally and socially vital for almost thirty years is a masterpiece of personal branding. He has smoothly transitioned from a youthful rap icon into an elder statesman of Ghanaian creative arts.

A Blueprint for the Future

As Ghana continues its march toward achieving major health targets - such as the elimination of viral hepatitis - and bolstering local industries, the value of trusted intermediaries between the state and the masses cannot be overstated.

Okyeame Kwame represents the ideal synergy between state vision and citizen execution.

He proves that true influence is measured by how many lives you can uplift, how many diseases you can help eradicate, and how deeply you can make your people fall in love with their own identity.

From the stages of Kumasi and Accra to the high offices of ministries, Okyeame Kwame is not merely an entertainer. He is a national treasure, a living testament to purposeful patriotism, and a true Ghanaian asset.

Ghana News.title: Trump says he will hold off on fresh Iran attack in hope of quick deal
Ghana News.content:
President Donald Trump has said the U.S. will hold off on a fresh attack on Iran as long as a ​deal can be reached quickly to halt Iran's nuclear ambitions and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

Trump said late on Saturday on his Truth Social ‌platform that Iran and other Middle Eastern countries had asked for time to complete a deal that would lead to "the Immediate, Complete and Total" reopening of the vital strait and "an end to Iran's nuclear threat"

He did not name the countries in the post, which followed a call with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman of Saudi Arabia, a U.S. ally.

"Based on this request, I have agreed, ​for the future benefit of the WORLD and, likewise, the survival of a successful and prosperous Iran, to cancel the attack, subject to being able ​to rapidly make a DEAL," Trump wrote.

Israel "joins me in this commitment", he said.

IRAN SAYS IT IS BOOSTING DETERRENCE

Trump's apparent de-escalation after ⁠days of threats of new attacks from each side was the latest twist in the war the U.S. and Israel launched five months ago. Attacks have spread ​across the Gulf to the Red Sea and even a Mediterranean facility in Egypt.

Iran has largely closed the Strait of Hormuz, a conduit for 20% of the world's oil and LNG ​before the war, causing energy prices to rise and stoking broader inflation.

Eli Cohen, Israel's energy minister and a member of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s security cabinet, said there was close security and intelligence coordination between Israel and the U.S. on everything happening in the region.

But he added: "With or without an agreement, and regardless of any external commitments, if Iran attempts to renew ​its nuclear programme or advance its ballistic missile industries, we will be there. We will take action, and we will strike."

Trump and Netanyahu met on Tuesday in ​Washington, with an Israeli official saying they had explored all possible paths to curb Iran's nuclear programme, including diplomacy, economic pressure and force. Tehran denies seeking a nuclear weapon.

Iran’s acting defence ‌minister, Brigadier ⁠General Majid Ebn Al-Reza, said Tehran viewed recent U.S. threats as “psychological and cognitive warfare” but was treating them seriously, adding that Iran would boost preparedness and deterrence rather than be caught off guard or remain passive, Press TV reported.

In his call with Trump, the Saudi crown prince stressed the "necessity of prioritising dialogue to de-escalate tensions" in the Middle East, according to Saudi Arabia's state news agency.

A White House official told Reuters that the two had spoken but did not provide details.

OIL PRICE SURGED LAST MONTH

At a cabinet ​meeting on Friday, Trump said he believed ​U.S. negotiators, including his son-in-law Jared ⁠Kushner, special envoy Steve Witkoff and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, could reach a deal with Iran.

As an April ceasefire in the war unravelled last month, benchmark Brent crude futures jumped 24%, and analysts polled by Reuters expect prices to rise further this ​year.

Trump has argued that his stated goal of keeping Iran from gaining nuclear weapons justifies higher fuel costs in the ​near term, but the ⁠economic pain has put political pressure on him to find a way to end the war.

Adding to the energy industry's concerns, Iran's Houthi allies in Yemen in recent days began threatening the Bab el-Mandeb, the strait at the other end of the Red Sea from the Suez Canal, another export route for Saudi crude.

The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said ⁠on Saturday ​it had received reports of two maritime incidents off Oman. In one, an unknown projectile struck a tanker, ​damaging the engine room. In the other, the master of a tanker reported seeing a large splash and an explosion close to the vessel, though no damage was reported.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: From Sudan to Spain: Between war and home | Al Jazeera Originals
World.content:
Aboubaker was 23 when he left Sudan in 2022, hoping for a better future.

This short documentary follows his journey across five countries and the Sahara Desert before he finally reaches Europe. Today, he is rebuilding his life in Madrid through football, work, and a close-knit Sudanese community.

But in April 2023, war broke out in Sudan. As violence continues to engulf his homeland, Aboubaker watches from thousands of kilometres away, desperately awaiting news from the family he left behind in Darfur.

A story about leaving home, finding belonging, and living with the uncertainty of watching a war unfold from afar.

Directed and produced by Chiara Brambilla for Al Jazeera Originals.

World.title: FIFA boss Infantino’s position looks unacceptable: European Leagues head
World.content:
Claudius Schafer says there can be ‘only one consequence’ to Infantino’s actions over his World Cup privatisation plan.

Gianni Infantino’s ‌position as FIFA president looks untenable following his ⁠failed plan to ⁠sell a stake in the World Cup’s commercial rights, the head of Europe’s professional football leagues has said.

Claudius Schafer, whose organisation represents 53 professional men’s and women’s football leagues, said ⁠on Sunday there could be “only one consequence” for ⁠Infantino after his plan triggered a storm of protest from regional associations.

“When I saw how this whole thing unfolded and that FIFA’s key bodies weren’t involved, then there’s essentially only one consequence ‌in any company or association,” he told Swiss newspaper SonntagsZeitung.

Asked if this meant that Infantino was now unacceptable as FIFA president, Schafer said: “This is usually the consequence when someone in a company pushes such a business deal forward without anyone knowing about it.”

Infantino said on Friday FIFA ⁠had scrapped the plan after a widespread ⁠backlash.

Regional confederations UEFA and CONCACAF said on Saturday they had lost confidence in his leadership.

Schafer, also chief executive of the Swiss Football League, said the proposal ⁠suggested that FIFA’s main goal was to maximise profits for third parties by having ⁠more and bigger competitions in future.

“It’s solely ⁠about the financial advantages; everything else is completely ignored,” he said.

The European Leagues opposed this because it would add more matches to an already packed ‌international calendar to the detriment of national championships, Schafer said.



“Nobody knew about the plans, not even the FIFA Council, the governing ‌body ‌of FIFA. I was very surprised that the president was acting completely alone in this matter.”
