World.title: Chiefs and Pirates raise hopes of epic league title talk
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs and Orlando Pirates have wasted no time making a statement in the new Betway Premiership season, with both Soweto giants opening their campaigns with convincing victories.

The two teams occupy the top two spots on the table after the opening weekend.

Amakhosi produced an impressive attacking display to beat promoted Kruger United 3-1 in Mbombela, while defending champions Orlando Pirates overcame a stubborn Milford side 2-0 at Orlando Stadium.



Pirates will naturally start the season with confidence after ending Mamelodi Sundowns’ eight-year dominance by lifting the league title last season.

Defensively, Abdeslam Ouaddou’s side already look well organised, but their lack of cutting edge in front of goal could become a concern if they fail to create more chances.

Chiefs and Pirates make statement

Chiefs, meanwhile, looked sharp in attack. They were clinical with their opportunities and deserved all three points against league newcomers Kruger United.

The performance has given supporters fresh hope that Fernando Da Cruz’s side could finally mount a genuine title challenge.

It is, of course, far too early to draw firm conclusions after just one league match. However, the early signs suggest the gap between the Soweto rivals may be much closer than in recent seasons, raising the possibility of an exciting title battle.

Mamelodi Sundowns should not be overlooked. The Brazilians, who won eight consecutive league titles before Pirates dethroned them last season, were not in league action this weekend but are expected to be firmly in the championship race once their campaign gets underway.



Attention now turns to the MTN8 next weekend, where Chiefs, Pirates and Sundowns will all be in action.

Pirates head into the competition as favourites after winning the last four editions, but Chiefs will be eager to build on their impressive league start and show they are ready to compete for major honours once again.

Who will win the league?

World.title: KiSwahili unites the continent
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - With more than 200 million speakers, Kiswahili has grown far beyond East Africa.

For centuries, it has served as a vital official language and cultural bridge in various African countries.

The language even has its official day, which is 7 July.

Fay Shao, Swahili Africa director, said the Miriam Makeba Foundation and Swahili Africa have partnered to celebrate that legacy, particularly at a time when migration and identity have become increasingly contested.

“KiSwahili is the one true heritage of the continent because when it started, it started as the language for trade when people were trading among themselves, people from the central part of the continent to the eastern part of the continent.

“Then they came up with this dialect, which later became like a common language that can be used. And it was formalised.

“Now that you have this language that everyone can understand, then let's make it official. And that's when it started. Someone somewhere - there's someone from the Zulu tribe or Hausa tribe contributed to the building up of Kiswahili.

“In South Africa, I always refer to it as the "Fana Kalo" because it's just that a language that develops in a specific community where they want to trade, they want to do things together, but they don't wanna lose their culture or lose their language, but they want to communicate.”

World.title: Experts call for greater investment in assistive technology
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Around 15% of Africans are living with disabilities.

Technology is constantly evolving and improving the lives of some people, but millions with special needs continue to face barriers.

Access to education, employment, entrepreneurship and digital participation is limited.

According to a Stellenbosch University report, this is caused by a lack of access to the latest technologies.

Quinette Louw, a Professor of Physiotherapy at Stellenbosch University, said more needs to be done.

“We have to invest in assistive technology to strengthen the entire ecosystem. We need to invest in local innovators, in local manufacturing, but ensure quality standards, of course.

“We also have to advocate for the inclusion of people with impairments and disability, not because it enriches the lives of those individuals, but also because if people can play, learn and work, they participate in society. And of course, as I said before, they contribute to our economy," Louw said.

World.title: Four killed in Nyanga shooting
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - Police are investigating the killing of four men in Nyanga, Cape Town, on Saturday night.

They were ambushed by gunmen on Old Klipfontein Road while fixing a flat tyre.

Emergency services declared the victims dead at the scene and the suspects are yet to be arrested after fleeing.

A preliminary police investigation shows the motive for the killings could be taxi-related.

Police spokesperson Colonel Andrè Traut has urged anyone with information to come forward.

“Anyone with information that could assist the investigation is urged to contact the investigating team via the SAPS Crime Stop number on 08600 10111 or submit information anonymously through the MySAPS mobile application. All information received will be treated with the strictest confidentiality,” Traut said.

Four counts of murder have been registered for investigation by the Serious Violent Crime Unit.

World.title: SALGA backs Coalition Bill to stabilise local municipalities
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The South African Local Government Association (SALGA) believes the Coalition Bill will play a major role in stabilising governing agreements.

Cabinet has approved the Municipal Structures Amendment Bill for submission to Parliament.

It aims to regulate coalition governments in municipalities and reduce political instability.

SALGA’s Lance Joel said residents across the country's major municipalities have been robbed of basic services because of persistent coalition chaos since the 2016 elections.

“It starts with the formation of coalitions. The formation itself is a narrow majority. The idea is to try to minimise those instabilities. It's a step in the right direction, but it will require political maturity,” Joel said.

World.title: Police seize over 90kg of cocaine at airport
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG – Police are investigating the smuggling of over 90kg of cocaine discovered at OR Tambo International Airport.

The cocaine, with an estimated value of R28million, was found during an intelligence-driven operation that was executed following information received from SAPS Crime Intelligence's Border Integrity Unit.

Police spokesperson Brigadier Athlenda Mathe said the drug consignment was intercepted in a joint operation.

“The information was operationalised by members of the SAPS Visible Policing Unit at OR Tambo International Airport, in collaboration with Customs officials and Menzies Aviation operational members.

“The cargo, which had arrived on a flight from São Paulo, Brazil, was intercepted immediately upon arrival at approximately 13:00. The 95 kilograms of cocaine were seized at the cargo section of OR Tambo International Airport,” she said.

No arrests have been made.

“Investigations are ongoing to identify and apprehend those involved in the attempted smuggling operation.

“The SAPS remains committed to disrupting organised criminal networks involved in the illicit drug trade and will continue working with its law enforcement partners to ensure that South Africa's borders and ports of entry are protected from criminal exploitation,” Mathe added.

World.title: Rise Mzansi believes it can take Joburg back to its glory days
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG – Rise Mzansi, like several others, is out drumming up support on the last day of voter registration.

It hopes to convince potential voters to give it a chance to lead the Johannesburg metro.

The country's richest city is a shadow of its former self and is set to be a major battleground in the November polls.

The party’s Joburg mayoral candidate, Lukhona Mnguni, said a lot needs to be done

“As Rise Mzansi, we are clear what we want to achieve this election. The power lies with the voter to get amasela out. We will launch a plan for Joburg... The campaign cannot end there,” he said.

World.title: Expropriation Act case back in court
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - The Western Cape High Court will hear an application to challenge parts of the Expropriation Act on Monday.

AfriForum, the DA, and the Institute of Race Relations want certain provisions of the Act struck down.

President Cyril Ramaphosa, Minister of Public Works, the National Assembly, the Speaker and NCOP chairperson are respondents in the matter.

AfriForum said its fight against expropriation of land without compensation

is in the interest of everyone in the country.

AfriForum’s Kallie Kriel said the case was important.

“AfriForum cannot and will not stand by and watch. That is why we have appointed a top legal team. We will not let that happen in South Africa,” Kriel said.

World.title: Standing Committee dismisses claims of irregularities in Parliament rebuild
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - Parliament's Joint Standing Committee on the Financial Management has dismissed claims of governance issues in the rebuilding of the National Assembly.

It comes after the DA called for an urgent investigation into the handling of the project.

The party claimed there has been no proof of a lawful transfer of the allocated billions of rands.

It said there is no record of Parliament taking over the project following 2022 fire.

But the Standing Committee has hit back, saying it's public knowledge that the project had to be transferred from Public Works to Parliament.

World.content:
Shocking revelations by MPs and senators that they received bribes to impeach former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua have brought to the fore the alarming level of corruption that has permeated the 13th Parliament.

World.title: CS sued in bid to kick out Railways boss, audit SGR contracts
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

A court battle is brewing over Kenya Railways operations and the corporation’s Managing Director Phillip Mainga's reign.

A petitioner is now seeking to push the KR boss out, claiming he is employed on permanent terms.

In the case against KR board, the Attorney General and Transport Cabinet Secretary, the complainant alleges that Mainga was appointed in 2018, noting that State corporations hire their bosses on short-term contracts.

Mainga has been named as an interested party.

“Under the prevailing governance principles applicable to the state corporations, the office of the Managing Director is not meant to be occupied indefinitely,” argues Wahome Mucunu, adding that Mainga’s tenure in office ought to have allegedly lapsed in 2024.

Mucunu claims that the corporation has been at the heart of numerous concerns over procurement and transparency.

He states that among the projects that have raised concerns are the Standard Gauge Railway (SGR project).

According to him, Transparency International this year in March this year allegedly indicated that SGR was a high-risk project, with a 4.9 out of 5 corruption risk score.

“The project has equally generated sustained public debate concerning transparency, accountability, value for money, public participation, procurement practices and debt sustainability. The Petitioner states that the people of Kenya, being the ultimate financiers of the project through taxation and public borrowing, possess a legitimate constitutional interest in the manner in which the project was conceived, procured, financed and implemented,” says Muchunu.

He further claims that Transparency International indicated that public institutions, among them KR, allegedly repeatedly failed to provide information requested by accountability actors and researchers. Muchunu alleged that the assessment concluded that the responses received were insufficient to facilitate effective public oversight.

“All material times relevant to this Petition, the first interested party, Mr. Phillip Mainga, has served as the Managing Director of Kenya Railways Corporation. The office of Managing Director constitutes the highest executive office within the Corporation and carries overall responsibility for the administration, management and operational control of the affairs of the Corporation,” he argues.

He also claims that many questions have been raised by members of the public, civil society organisations, governance experts and accountability institutions regarding the management of major projects undertaken by the corporation.

According to him, the answers given do not allegedly exude confidence as they are not allegedly fully addressed.

“Such concerns have centered on the adequacy of procurement procedures, transparency of contractual arrangements, disclosure of project costs and effectiveness of oversight mechanisms. The Petitioner states that these concerns have never been adequately addressed in a manner capable of restoring public confidence,” he continues.

In his case before Justice David Mburu, the petitioner urges the court to find that failure to disclose details about the SGR contract was a violation of the Constitution. He also seeks for a finding that Mainga ought to have left office by last year.

At the same time, he is urging the court to rule that the parastatal’s board had violated the Constitution and to compel it to find his successor.

Muchunu also wants to have the SGR project contracts audited.

World.title: Tiktoker Mauti changes plea, freed on bail in case involving Ruto's children
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

TikToker Hesbon Mauti was charged for posting a video threatening to kill and defile President William Ruto's children. [Nancy Gitonga, Standard]

TikToker Hesbon Mauti Thomas, accused of posting a video containing remarks threatening President William Ruto’s son George Ruto and daughter, has been released on a Sh5,000 cash bail after changing his plea to not guilty.

Mauti appeared before Milimani Principal Magistrate Geoffrey Onsarigo on Friday, July 31, 2026, where the charge of offensive conduct conducive to breaches of the peace was read afresh to him.

The accused, who had initially pleaded guilty to the charge on Thursday, changed his plea after his lawyer Cliff Ombeta applied for the matter to be reopened and for the charge to be read again.

The court allowed the application, after which Mauti denied the charge and pleaded not guilty.

According to the charge sheet, Mauti is accused of posting a video on June 25, 2026, through his TikTok account PROVIDENT@bonifaceaminga, containing remarks that prosecutors say were likely to cause a breach of the peace.

The charge sheet alleges that Mauti altered words in the video to make remarks targeting President Ruto’s son George Ruto and his daughter, while demanding that their parents be paid Sh2 million.

Mauti is charged with offensive conduct conducive to breaches of the peace contrary to Section 94(1) of the Penal Code, Chapter 63 of the Laws of Kenya.

After denying the charges, his defence team told the court that Mauti is a young man and a law student at Chuka University whose fees are paid by a church.

The lawyers further informed the court that Mauti is an orphan and has no parents to assist him in securing his release, asking the court to grant him a lenient cash bail.

“We are looking at the charges and when we look at it and the consequences that come from that, and if it goes on this particular way we know what the sentence is and what the consequences are. The court has got the right before passing the sentence to be able to reconsider when he changes his plea,” his lawyers told the court.

The defence also told the court that they had advised Mauti that the earlier position he had taken by pleading guilty carried serious consequences and offered to represent him in the matter.

The prosecution did not oppose his release on bail.

Magistrate Onsarigo granted Mauti a cash bail of Sh5,000 and directed him to provide one contact person.

The matter will be mentioned on August 18, 2026, for pre-trial directions.

World.title: Ruto calls for national dialogue to shape Kenya's vision
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Ruto said recent economic reforms had laid a stronger foundation for future growth. [File, Standard]

President William Ruto has invited Kenyans to take part in what he described as the country's most significant national conversation since the adoption of the 2010 Constitution, saying the discussions will help chart Kenya's next long-term development agenda.

Speaking on the country's development trajectory, the President said the conversation should move beyond partisan politics and election cycles to focus on a shared national vision.

"I invite every Kenyan to what I believe will become the most consequential national conversation since the adoption of our Constitution in 2010," Ruto said.

"A national conversation about Kenya's development. This conversation must rise above politics, transcend electoral cycles and unite us around a shared destiny."

The President acknowledged that while Vision 2030 had set an ambitious goal of transforming Kenya into an upper-middle-income country by 2030, the country remains off course to achieve that target.

"Vision 2030 set a target of Kenya becoming an upper-middle-income country by 2030. So far, we are off target. This is not a criticism of Vision 2030, nor is it a reason for disappointment; rather, it is an opportunity to learn from our successes proudly, reflect with honesty on where we have fallen short, and define together Kenya's next long-term vision," he said.

At the same time, Ruto announced that the government will formally launch a nationwide conversation on August 12 to develop Kenya's next long-term development blueprint as Vision 2030 nears its end.

"Accordingly, on Wednesday, August 12, 2026, we shall formally launch the National Conversation on Kenya's Future Beyond Vision 2030; the most consequential exercise in national reflection and public participation since the promulgation of our Constitution in 2010," he stated.

Ruto said recent economic reforms had laid a stronger foundation for future growth, citing improvements in key macroeconomic indicators.

"We have stabilized our currency, inflation has fallen, borrowing costs have declined, and investor confidence has returned," he said. "Last year Kenya attracted a record $3.2 billion in foreign direct investment, more than double the amount recorded in 2022."

He added that Kenya's improving investment climate had earned international recognition.

"The 2025 IMD World Competitiveness Ranking placed Kenya as the most competitive economy in Africa, reflecting the confidence our reforms have restored," Ruto said.

At the same time, Ruto also highlighted the establishment of the National Infrastructure Fund and the Sovereign Wealth Fund, saying the two institutions would help finance strategic investments while safeguarding the country's wealth for future generations.

According to Ruto, Kenya must now confront difficult questions about its development path to unlock its full potential.

"The question we must ask ourselves candidly and honestly is why other nations have fulfilled so much of their potential while we have repeatedly fallen short. What must we now do differently to ensure that the next chapter of Kenya's development story is fundamentally different from the last?" he posed.

He urged all Kenyans to help shape a new long-term national vision, saying the country's future depends on collective commitment rather than political divisions.

World.title: Lawyer seeks orders to suspend court boycott
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Advocate Adrian Kamotho argues that LSK's actions create the impression that court orders can be overturned through a boycott. [File, Standard]

A city lawyer has moved to the High Court seeking conservatory orders to suspend the Law Society of Kenya's (LSK) ongoing targeted boycott of judges and judicial officers.

In a petition filed under a certificate of urgency, Advocate Adrian Kamotho has sued LSK led by President Charles Kanjama, over its nationwide and targeted court boycott of Chief Justice Martha Koome, Deputy Chief Justice Philomena Mwilu and other judges, arguing that the action is unconstitutional, undermines judicial independence and denies litigants access to justice.

"The LSK's actions create the impression that lawful court orders can be overturned through a boycott, setting a dangerous precedent to the rule of law and thereby undermining the proper administration of justice," Kamotho states in the petition.

The lawyer has named the Judicial Service Commission (JSC), Chief Justice Martha Koome, Deputy Chief Justice Mwilu, several Supreme Court, High Court and Environment and Land Court judges, Court of Appeal Judge Sankale Ole Kantai, Kibera Chief Magistrate Stella Atambo and the Kenya Magistrates and Judges Association as interested parties in the case.

He is seeking orders to immediately suspend the implementation of the LSK's targeted boycott announced through statements and operational guidelines issued on July 17, July 20 and July 22, 2026, pending the hearing and determination of the petition.

"Pending the hearing and determination of this Petition, the court be pleased to issue a conservatory order restraining the LSK, whether by itself, its Council, officers, agents or any person acting under its authority, from implementing, enforcing or giving effect to the targeted boycott," Kamotho seeks.

According to the petition, the targeted boycott, which commenced on July 23, directs advocates not to participate in fresh hearings, part-heard matters or new applications before judges listed by the LSK.

East Africa Law Society president Ramadhan Abubakar Mukira addresses the media on the court boycott outside the Supreme Court of Kenya in Nairobi on July 22, 2026. [Benard Orwongo, Standard]

Lawyers are also required to seek adjournments, transfers or recusals of matters regardless of their clients' instructions.

"The Respondent has directed advocates not to participate in fresh hearings, part-heard matters or new applications before the listed judges and judicial officers," Kamotho states.

He adds: "Advocates appearing before the targeted judges and judicial officers have been directed to seek the transfer, recusal or adjournment of pending proceedings, irrespective of their clients' instructions, the circumstances of the individual case or the applicable legal principles."

Kamotho further claims the society has threatened disciplinary action against judges, judicial officers and advocates who decline to implement the boycott.

"The LSK has further directed that any judge, judicial officer or advocate who declines to facilitate the boycott be reported to it for 'appropriate action,' including possible complaints before the Judicial Service Commission and such further action as its Council may deem necessary," he says.

According to the petition, every day the boycott remains in force exposes court users to delayed justice and unnecessary hardship.

"Every day that the targeted boycott remains operative exposes litigants and court users to adjournments, disruption of part-heard proceedings, expiry of interim protection measures, prolonged detention, additional expense and denial or delay of access to justice," Kamotho argues.

He also faults the LSK for allegedly including the late Supreme Court Judge Mohammed Ibrahim in its list of judges affected by the boycott.

"The targeted list of judges includes Hon. Justice Mohammed Ibrahim (deceased), demonstrating unconscionable casualness on the part of the LSK and apparent failure to verify elementary material facts before imposing measures of such gravity," the petition states.

Kamotho contends that the boycott creates an unlawful mechanism for exerting pressure on judges outside the constitutional framework.

He argues that the dispute raises fundamental constitutional questions, including whether the LSK has the legal authority to organise an indefinite boycott, compel advocates to withhold legal services from clients and determine which judicial functions judges may perform.

He maintains that the boycott threatens litigants' constitutional rights to equality before the law, access to justice, legal representation and a fair hearing, particularly in urgent and criminal matters.

In his supporting affidavit, Kamotho says advocates have been placed in an impossible position by the LSK's directives.

"The directions therefore place advocates in an immediate and irreconcilable conflict between their lawful professional duties and the Respondent's threatened enforcement measures," he says.

He further says litigants are innocent parties caught in an institutional dispute.

"The practical burden of the boycott consequently falls upon litigants and court users who are strangers to the institutional dispute forming the alleged basis of the boycott," he states.

Kamotho insists the conservatory orders sought are intended only to preserve uninterrupted court operations and judicial independence pending determination of the constitutional petition, arguing that the public interest favours continued access to courts and legal representation rather than disruption of judicial proceedings.

The petition is pending directions and hearing.

World.title: Ruto: Government will deal firmly with criminals
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto arrive for the consecration of Rev. Vitalis Job Ekuru as the fourth Bishop of the ACK Diocese of Katakwa in Busia County on July 26, 2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto has declared war on individuals who involve in violence, destruction of property and political intimidation.

He said people initially participated in anti-government demonstrations have "graduated from protesters to goons."

Speaking on Sunday during the consecration of Rev. Vitalis Job Ekuru as the fourth Bishop of the ACK Diocese of Katakwa in Busia County, the President said the government would no longer tolerate criminality disguised as peaceful protests.

"They have now graduated from protesters to goons. They are bringing chaos everywhere," Ruto said.

President Ruto maintained that safeguarding peace remains the government's top priority while ensuring all leaders have the freedom to campaign without fear of violence or intimidation.

He argued that Kenya had previously experienced a rise in criminal activities, but efforts to deal with those responsible had been complicated by differing opinions over how security agencies should respond.

"We had a small problem earlier when crime issues increased and we did not agree on how to tackle the crime as a nation because sometimes we used to defend those who were hurting people and destroying property. We could say that they should not be touched because they are our children," he said.

"But now we have seen the repercussions because they have now graduated from protesters to goons. They are bringing chaos everywhere."

Ruto said the government had resolved to restore law and order, insisting that criminal gangs would not be allowed to disrupt peace under the cover of political demonstrations.

"We have agreed to discipline all the goons, and no one will be allowed to propagate crime and disrupt peace in our country," he said.

The President also sought to reassure Kenyans that the country would remain peaceful as preparations begin for the 2027 General Election, saying his administration would do everything possible to safeguard stability before, during and after the polls.

"I agree that peace is not negotiable. All of us, irrespective of who we are, our persuasion, our political leaning and whatever it is that we believe in, we must have a peaceful nation," Ruto said.

"I want to assure you as the people of Kenya that we will have peaceful elections next year because elections come and go, but this nation must remain firm, united and stable. We shall do everything possible to ensure that this nation is stable."

At the same time, the Head of State emphasized that every political leader should be free to campaign and present their agenda without intimidation, provided they conduct their activities peacefully.

"Every leader should be given a chance to give their opinion. Those who have an agenda or plan should be given an opportunity to explain it to Kenyans. Even those who have nothing should be given a chance to speak, but all of us must ensure that we are peaceful," he said.

The President's remarks come against the backdrop of heightened political tensions and growing concerns over violent disruptions at political gatherings.

Recent incidents, including the Ol Kalou by-election in Nyandarua County, saw armed gangs disrupt voting and terrorize residents, prompting renewed debate over the role of criminal groups in Kenya's political landscape.

The government has faced criticism from sections of the opposition, who have accused state agencies of sponsoring the gangs.

However, Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen has rejected the claims, instead alleging that the groups were mobilized by allies of former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua. Murkomen has pledged decisive action against those behind the violence, regardless of their political affiliation.

World.title: Ruiru 'Vampire' arrested after lodging incident with woman
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The suspect was arrested after an angry mob cornered and assaulted him near the Powerstar area in Ruiru town following weeks of attacks that had spread fear among residents. [Courtesy, X]

Police in Ruiru have arrested a 35-year-old man believed to be behind a series of bizarre and violent attacks in which residents were robbed and bitten, leaving several victims nursing serious injuries.

The suspect, identified as Githaiga from Mugutha, was arrested on Saturday afternoon after an angry mob cornered and assaulted him near the Powerstar area in Ruiru town following weeks of attacks that had spread fear among residents.

Ruiru Sub-County Police Commander Charles Kibathi confirmed the arrest, saying the suspect was heavily intoxicated at the time and had allegedly bitten a woman who was with him, tearing part of her lower lip.

"The suspect and the female victim were taken to hospital for treatment as investigations continue," Kibathi said.

He added that detectives are investigating whether the suspect is linked to the earlier attacks reported in Ruiru and neighbouring Gitothua Ward.

However, some residents defended the suspect, claiming the altercation that led to the woman being bitten stemmed from a disagreement after the two emerged from a room where they had spent the night.

Kibathi assured residents that police are pursuing all leads to establish whether other people may have been involved in the attacks and pledged to intensify security operations in the area.

The arrest follows weeks of panic after several residents reported being attacked by a man who allegedly robbed victims before violently biting them.

Among the latest victims was Daniel Ndegwa, who was attacked on July 11 at about 9 p.m. while walking to a nearby shopping centre. Ndegwa told police he was confronted by a man demanding his mobile phone before a struggle ensued. During the confrontation, the attacker bit his finger and injured his left hand. A friend who was accompanying him was also reportedly bitten.

Residents said the attacks had become increasingly frequent throughout July, forcing many people to avoid walking outside after dark.

In one of the most shocking incidents, another victim reportedly suffered severe facial injuries after the attacker allegedly bit off part of his cheek.

The incidents have disrupted normal life in Ruiru town and Gitothua Ward, with many residents opting to remain indoors in the evenings for fear of being attacked.

Residents, led by Severino Githinji, criticized the security situation, saying families have been living in constant fear and called for increased police patrols and swift action against those responsible.

Police said the first official report of the attacks was made on July 11, and investigations are ongoing to establish whether the arrested suspect is responsible for all the reported incidents.

Kibathi urged members of the public to continue cooperating with investigators as detectives work to unravel the full circumstances surrounding the attacks.

World.title: Murkomen: Police no longer rely on Gachagua's 'gossip'
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Interior CS Kipchumba Murkomen during the official launch of the Multi-biometric Identification System (MBIS) and handover ceremony of ANSI National Accreditation Board Certificate at DCI Headquarters on July 23, 2026. [NPS]

Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen has accused former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua of spreading falsehoods, saying technology-driven policing has replaced "gossip-based" investigations.

Speaking during the handover of the ANSI National Accreditation Board certification to the Forensic Evidence Management Unit and the launch of the Multi-Biometric Identification System at the Directorate of Criminal Investigations headquarters on Thursday, Murkomen said the country has shifted from outdated investigative methods to science-based policing.

"We are moving away from gossip-based collection of evidence to science. I saw an impeached former leader claiming he is well connected to police officers and receives gossip every day because he is not busy unlike the President," said Murkomen.

He said the biometric system will strengthen investigations through science and technology, making unofficial information unnecessary.

"That is an old style of collecting evidence. We now have a modern police service driven by science and technology. We do not need his gossip to run the National Police Service," he observed.

Murkomen claimed the technology would make it harder for unsuitable individuals to rise through public office.

"If these systems had been in place many years ago, people like Gachagua would not have survived the system as habitual offenders until he slipped through to become Deputy President. Such things will never happen again with this technological advancement," said Murkomen.

The Interior CS defended Inspector General of Police Douglas Kanja, saying he has the government's confidence and has discharged his duties professionally.

"I have full support and faith in the leadership of the Inspector General. He has carried out his duties with dignity, honour and respect for the citizens of Kenya and his office," noted Murkomen.

Murkomen also rejected Gachagua's criticism of police leadership, arguing that Kenya is recording fewer cases of terrorism, banditry, robbery and other crimes.

"There has never been a period when Kenya has recorded fewer incidents of terrorism, banditry, robberies and other crimes. Our security agencies are working together and have improved security," he said.

He also criticised remarks attributed to Gachagua warning tourists against visiting Kenya, saying they damage the country's reputation.

"For anyone to stand out there and say Kenya is not safe and tourists should not come to our country is very embarrassing," explained Murkomen.

Murkomen dismissed claims that 68 women were raped by police officers during the Ol Kalou parliamentary by-election, urging anyone with evidence to report the matter to the Directorate of Criminal Investigations, the Independent Policing Oversight Authority or the Kenya National Commission on Human Rights.

"If those incidents occurred, they should be reported so those responsible can be held accountable. If not, those making such reckless statements must also be held accountable," said Murkomen.

He accused Gachagua of making the allegations out of political desperation.

"I know why Gachagua speaks the way he does. It is because of desperation. Knowing that he cannot hold any office again in Kenya and can never be President of this republic, he wants to take the entire nation, including the economy, down the drain with himself. We will not allow that," he said.

Murkomen also urged media organisations to challenge politicians they host instead of allowing false claims to go unchecked.

"We should not feed Kenyans with lies. I want to tell media houses that when you invite such reckless human beings, please carry with you a lie detector. Otherwise you are going to mislead the people of Kenya and drive bad behaviour in our country," said Murkomen.

He maintained that intelligence gathering within the National Police Service follows lawful procedures and dismissed claims that private individuals receive confidential police briefings outside official channels

World.title: FEDCOC Head urges businesses to join new licensing system
World.content:
Chairman of the Federation of Egyptian Chambers of Commerce (FEDCOC) Ahmed al-Wakil described the new public shop licensing system as a “historic opportunity” to integrate informal businesses into the formal economy, urging traders and business owners to take advantage of government incentives to regularize their operations.

al-Wakil praised the government’s efforts to simplify licensing procedures through the Digital Egypt platform, highlighting reduced fees, streamlined services and discounts of up to 50% during the initial implementation phase.

He said the system would improve the business environment by expanding the formal economy, enhancing transparency by publishing all official fees online, and preventing unauthorized charges.

al-Wakil also called for expanding the platform’s services to cover sole proprietorships, partnerships, and small businesses across the Suez Canal and Sinai regions, pledging that local chambers of commerce would provide technical support, awareness campaigns, and digital assistance to help businesses transition to the new system.

World.title: Damietta Port receives 13 vessels in 24 hours
World.content:
“Damietta Port received 13 vessels and recorded the departure of nine ships over the past 24 hours, bringing the total number of vessels at the port to 32,” according to the Damietta Port Authority.

The port handled 15,217 tons of export cargo, including beet pulp feed, gypsum, bagged cement, urea and other goods. Imports reached 20,515 tons, consisting of scrap metal, beech wood, steel, rice and plywood.

Container traffic included 550 export containers, 242 import containers and 3,912 transit containers.

The port’s public grain silos contained 84,641 tons of wheat, while private storage facilities held 44,430 tons. Truck traffic totaled 2,798 movements during the reporting period.

Meanwhile, the GALLIPOLI SEAWAYS Ro-Ro vessel departed for Trieste, Italy, carrying 3,704 tons of cargo, including agricultural products, textiles, garments, electrical cables, automotive parts, buses, machinery and industrial equipment.

The cargo was bound for several European destinations, including Italy, Germany, the Netherlands, the United Kingdom, France, Austria, Sweden, Poland, Slovenia, Slovakia and Hungary, while transit shipments were destined for the United Arab Emirates, Oman, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Bahrain.

World.title: Abdelatty congratulates Yemen’s new FM, reaffirms Egypt’s backing
World.content:
Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation, and Egyptian Expatriates Badr Abdelatty has congratulated Yemen’s newly appointed Foreign Minister Afrah Abdulaziz Al-Zouba during a phone call on Saturday, August 1, 2026.

Abdelatty reaffirmed Egypt’s commitment to strengthening bilateral ties and supporting Yemen’s stability, lauding longstanding fraternal relations between the two countries and underscoring Cairo’s keenness to deepen cooperation and coordination across various fields.

The talks focused on the latest developments in Yemen, as Abdelatty reiterated Egypt’s unwavering support for the Arab country’s unity, territorial integrity and legitimate government, in line with relevant international resolutions.

He stressed the importance of supporting Yemen’s national institutions to help restore security and stability and meet the aspirations of the Yemeni people.

The two ministers also exchanged views on regional developments and emphasized the need to continue efforts toward a comprehensive political settlement that preserves Yemen’s unity and contributes to broader regional stability.

World.title: Cairo to host international textile machinery Exhibition in September
World.content:
Cairo will host the 24th Exhibition for Textile & Carpet Machineries, Printing Technologies and Accessories (Egypt Stitch & Tex Expo) from September 24 to 27, 2026, bringing together 425 Egyptian and international exhibitors.

The exhibition, to be held at the Cairo International Convention Center under the theme “The Textile Experts Show”, will showcase the latest technologies and solutions for the textile, garment and printing industries across 40,000 square meters.

The event is expected to bring together machinery manufacturers, investors, suppliers and textile producers, offering opportunities for business partnerships, export expansion and technology transfer.

The exhibition comes as Egypt’s textile industry accelerates factory modernization and investment in advanced manufacturing technologies to improve productivity and strengthen global competitiveness.

Chairman of the Ready-Made Garments Chamber at the Federation of Egyptian Industries

Mohamed Abdel Salam said that the exhibition would help Egyptian manufacturers access the latest textile technologies, modernize production lines and enhance product quality while reducing operating costs.

A conference will also be held alongside the exhibition, bringing together government officials, industry representatives and business leaders to discuss the future of Egypt’s textile and garment industry.

World.title: Govt remote work continues on Sundays in Egypt during August
World.content:
The Egyptian Cabinet on Thursday approved a draft resolution to continue remote work on Sundays for all employees in establishments subject to the Labor Law during August.

The government began implementing a remote work system on Sundays in April as part of a package of measures aimed at strengthening the resilience of the national economy in the face of the repercussions of the Iran war.

Its goal was rationalizing energy consumption and reducing government spending in light of regional economic developments.

The decision to work remotely on Sundays of each week was extended during May, June and July, with the exception of some vital sectors such as public services and the health sector, transportation, industrial and production facilities, in addition to educational institutions.

The decision is being implemented flexibly within organizations, with specific tasks being identified that can be performed remotely, while maintaining a minimum number of employees on-site when necessary.

World.title: Trabzonspor president reveals truth about signing Mohamed Salah
World.content:
The president of the board of directors of Turkish club Trabzonspor, Ertuğrul Doğan, on Saturday evening revealed the truth behind reports of it about signing Egyptian star Mohamed Salah during the current summer transfer window.

The French website Foot Mercato had confirmed that Trabzonspor was close to signing Salah in the current summer transfer window.

Doğan told Turkish channel Aspor, “There are many reports confirming our agreement with Mohamed Salah, but that hasn’t happened. If anything does, I will announce it to the fans and all media outlets.”

He added, “I hope to sign Salah, and I am committed to the interests of Trabzonspor.”

The Egyptian star left Liverpool FC at the end of last season after spending nine seasons with the Reds.

World.title: US issues urgent warning for American citizens in the Middle East
World.content:
The US State Department has issued an urgent warning to its citizens in the Middle East on Saturday, warning them to prepare immediately for the possibility of widespread disruptions to air traffic, including flight cancellations and airspace closures in several countries in the region.

This high-level diplomatic warning comes amid escalating military tensions and exchange of fire in the Middle East, increasing the risk to civil aviation and prompting US embassies to take precautionary measures to protect citizens.

In an exclusive interview with Axios, US President Donald Trump revealed decisive escalatory moves and positions regarding Iran.

He confirmed that he previously considered launching a military attack larger than ever before against Iran, and that US forces are fully prepared to carry it out.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Searing heatwave across Egypt to break by Wednesday: EMA
World.content:
The Egyptian Meteorological Authority (EMA) forecasts that the intense heatwave will continue across most of the country on Sunday, with high humidity levels increasing the perceived temperature by up to four degrees Celsius.

A meteorologist at the Forecasting and Early Warning Center of the EMA, Manar Ghanem, said that the heatwave is expected to break on Wednesday and Thursday, with temperatures across the country dropping slightly to between 35C and 36C.

In statements to Al-Masry Al-Youm Ghanem added that despite this decrease, the drop in temperatures will not be very noticeable due to the continued high humidity levels impacting the weather – but the overall conditions will be better.

The EMA explained that the expected maximum temperatures on Sunday will reach 40C in Greater Cairo and Upper Egypt, 43C in southern Upper Egypt, 39C in Lower Egypt, 35C on the northeastern coast, and 31C on the northwestern coast.

The perceived temperature across the country will range between 41 and 44 degrees Celsius.

The EMA advised avoiding direct sun exposure, drinking plenty of fluids, and wearing loose-fitting, light-colored cotton clothing.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Chief Mumena Ordered To Pay K600,000 To Torture Victims
World.content:
The Lusaka High Court has ordered Chief Mumena and the Attorney General to jointly pay more than K600,000 to three members of one family after finding the traditional leader unlawfully detained, tortured and forced them into labour over accusations that they held court documents challenging his authority.

Judge Geoffrey Mulenga ruled that Chief Mumena, whose real name is Jonathan Eshron Mumena, must personally pay K5,000 to each petitioner and publish a public apology in a newspaper of nationwide circulation within 30 days.

The ordeal began in January 2024, when Loveness Mwanza, Lawrence Kamasanyi and Salon Kalusa, all of Kananga area in North-Western Province, were forcibly taken from their homes on the chief’s orders. They were held in a metal container without basic sanitation or ventilation, assaulted, forced to perform labour and denied adequate food, water and medical care.

For Kalusa, who depends on antiretroviral medication, the consequences proved especially severe. He was cut off from his treatment during the detention, causing his health to deteriorate seriously. The family later filed a petition against the chief and the Attorney General in November 2024, arguing that their constitutional rights had been violated and that the State had failed in its duty to intervene once it became aware of the abuse.

Chief Mumena never appeared in court to answer the allegations. In his judgment, Mulenga noted that although duly served with court process, the chief neither entered an appearance nor led evidence in rebuttal, leaving the petitioners’ account of events entirely unchallenged.

The court found that the petitioners’ rights under Articles 11, 13, 14, 15, 17 and 22 of the Constitution had been violated. Mulenga further held the Attorney General jointly and severally liable, ruling that the State had failed to prevent or stop the abuses despite being aware of the petitioners’ unlawful confinement and mistreatment.

The judge described Chief Mumena’s conduct as displaying “contumelious disregard” for both the petitioners’ constitutional rights and the authority of the court, noting that he had ignored court summons and shown no remorse throughout the proceedings.

Mwanza was awarded K175,000 in damages for unlawful detention, battery, torture, forced labour and inhuman treatment, plus K30,000 in exemplary damages, bringing her total award to K205,000.

Kamasanyi, who suffered permanent injuries including swelling and tenderness to his right scrotum, was awarded K185,000 in compensatory damages and K30,000 in exemplary damages, for a total of K210,000.

Kalusa was awarded K185,000 in compensatory damages and K35,000 in exemplary damages for the deterioration in his health, giving him a total of K220,000.

Beyond the compensation, Chief Mumena must personally pay K5,000 to each petitioner, while the petitioners were also awarded legal costs to be agreed or taxed.

World.title: EIZ optimistic on new fees regulation
World.content:
EIZ is optimistic new fees regulation will align engineering sector and protect consumers

By David Kamungu

Like lawyers, accountants and other professionals that have gazetted guidelines on fees that they are required to charge for their services, the government has approved new regulation regulating pricing engineering professional services in Zambia.

Until now, the engineering sector in Zambia has existed without a framework that regulates the minimum chargeable fees by engineers due to lack of enabling legislation to ensure total professionalism in pricing by eliminating unhealthy competition such as undercutting in pricing during bidding processes.

The unregulated pricing of engineering services has had many pitfalls.

In some cases, some providers of engineering services, in desperate bids to win certain tenders, have resorted to undercutting rivals with dire consequences on both the engineering service providers and the consumers as the quality of the final product tends to be below prescribed and acceptable standards.

And this is why the recently government approved Engineering Institution of Zambia (Professional Service Fees) Regulations, 2026 also referred to as S.I No. 34 of 2026 is being held as a “significant milestone” for the local engineering sector.

So, S.I No. 34 of 2026 is essentially aimed at streamlining and aligning the engineering sector and professional practice by providing guidelines for professional fees to be charged for services rendered by engineering professionals.

“The whole purpose is not merely to prescribe fees but to promote professionalism and generally, the quality service of work. And therefore, by providing this transparency fees structure, our members are better positioned to dictate the necessary expertise, time and resources required to deliver engineering services,” Engineering Institution of Zambia (EIZ) Chief Executive Officer and Registrar Eng. David Kamungu said in an interview.

“In terms of what these fees mean to EIZ members like other regulated professions such as law, architecture here in Zambia, engineering now has an approved framework that recognizes the value of the professional services.”

Eng. Kamungu emphasized that the prescribed fees to apply to professional engineering services rendered by qualified practitioners should not be misinterpreted as employment remuneration.

According to Zambian labour laws which are also consistent with international best practices, employment remuneration is compensated through a salary – a fixed amount paid by an employer to an employee as compensation for ongoing employment, usually on a monthly basis and determined by employment contracts, organisational salary structures, and collective agreements among other considerations.

On the other hand professional service fee is the amount charged for specialised professional services provided by an independent, qualified and licensed practitioner or professional firm for a specific assignment, project or consultancy.

These fees are charged only when professional services are engaged and are intended to compensate the professional for the expertise, responsibility, time, skill and experience required to perform the work.

For a long time in Zambia, the engineering profession has not been able to regulate the minimum chargeable by engineers due to a lack of enabling legislation.

This absence of legislation to regulate the minimum chargeable fees by engineers has exposed consumers of engineering services to unhealthy competition such as undercutting as there has been no adequate buffer against harmful practices.

“For our members, this provides clarity and they also provide consistency and fairness in the pricing of engineering services. They also help eliminate unfair price competition but also protect the integrity of the profession in ensuring that only experts are approved to perform these jobs,” Eng. Kamungu said.

In the build-up to the formulation of S.I No. 34 of 2026 Regulations, some stakeholders expressed reservation that the standardizing of minimum Professional Service Fees could lead to an increase in cost of accessing engineering services in the country.

But with any functioning legislation, the formulation of new law regulating the minimum Professional Service Fees for engineering services was done with a specific focus on consumer protection which is at the core of any rational and ethical business practice.

The focus of S.I No. 34 of 2026 is to ensure consumer protection is implemented and enforced through minimum fees that are considered fair, consistent with required quality and meet minimum professional standards.

“Regarding the concerns, it is important to appreciate that quality Engineering is an investment rather than a cost. The objective of these regulations is not to make Engineering services expensive, but to ensure the delivery of professionally and sustainably but also equally by the service providers,” Eng. Kamungu explained. `

Who Is Eligible to charge Professional Fees?

The approved professional services fees only apply to members that hold valid EIZ practicing certificates such registered Professional Engineers, Engineering Technologists, Engineering technicians and registered engineering Craftspersons among others.

“So, those are members that have our registration certificates that are issued in accordance with the Engineering Registration Board,” says Eng. Kamungu.

How are the Professional fees going to be charged?

Typical of any assignment where professional services are billed according to the time spent on the work, the Regulations prescribe hourly fee rates expressed in fee units varied through the practitioner’s professional classification, years of relevant experience and the category of engineering professional among other considerations.

To determine the actual monetary amount chargeable per hour, the prescribed fee units are multiplied by the current Fee Unit Value established under Statutory Instrument No. 25 of 2024, which is presently K0.40 (40 Ngwee) per fee unit.

World.title: Cancer Diseases Hospital reopens after US$31 million upgrade
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema has commissioned the refurbished radiotherapy and imaging section at Cancer Diseases Hospital in Lusaka, restoring specialised cancer treatment services that had been suspended for six years.

The US$31 million facility, fully funded by the Zambian Government, makes Zambia one of only three African countries with advanced dedicated cancer care capacity, alongside South Africa and Egypt.

Hichilema described the commissioning as a prayer answered for hundreds of cancer patients across the country. “All of you cancer patients out there, your prayers have been answered. I am talking about over 800 cancer patients who have been waiting in the queue to go for treatment in India and other countries,” he said.

The radiotherapy and imaging services were suspended in 2020 to allow for the transformation of the hospital into what the President described as a world-class cancer treatment centre. The reopening was achieved without external funding.

The first patient to receive treatment at the upgraded facility was Maureya Zimba, 62, a cervical cancer patient whose testimony visibly moved the President.

“How satisfying it is to hear Madam Maureya Zimba, a 62-year-old cervical cancer patient, being the first patient to undergo treatment here. Her treatment was more than a medical procedure; it is a mark of hope for many cancer patients among the 21 million Zambians,” Hichilema said.

Zimba expressed gratitude to the President and urged him to continue the development agenda his administration has pursued.

Hichilema announced that the Ndola Cancer Treatment Centre, now 85 percent complete, will be commissioned before the end of the year. He also directed Ministry of Health permanent secretary for technical services Kennedy Lishimpi to expedite construction of the Livingstone Cancer Centre, which will serve the southern and western parts of the country.

The President further revealed plans are under way to build a medical city near Kenneth Kaunda International Airport to promote health tourism.

He disclosed that his administration had cleared a legacy debt owed to Indian hospitals for the treatment of Zambian cancer patients, debt that had accumulated under the previous government.

“We had to clear it because Indian hospitals started refusing to treat cancer patients, so we cleared it and said bye, bye,” he said.

Hichilema cautioned health workers against spending excessive time on their mobile phones while on duty, saying the facility’s network access would be restricted except for digital consultation purposes.

“I do not expect phones here. The system should ensure that everyone who works here does not come in with a phone. We will even obliterate the network here unless you want to deal with digital consultations,” he said.

Secretary to Cabinet Patrick Kangwa, speaking through remarks read on his behalf by Presidential Delivery Unit head Kusobile Kamwambi, said the President’s priority directive was to ensure quality healthcare, resulting in an 80 percent availability of medicines in health facilities across the country.

Kangwa said the expansion of digital hospitals, recruitment of health workers and construction of maternity annexes stand as evidence of the President’s commitment to improving healthcare.

German Ambassador to Zambia Sonke Siemon welcomed the selection of a German company to undertake the refurbishment of the centre, saying Germany remains committed to partnering with Zambia to strengthen the country’s healthcare system.

Lishimpi said in his opening remarks that the hospital had accumulated a backlog of 1,600 patients following the suspension of radiotherapy services in 2020.

Siemens Healthineers Southern Africa chief executive officer Ayanda Swana said the newly installed equipment has the capacity to treat up to 3,000 patients annually.

Cancer Diseases Hospital senior medical superintendent Dr Susan Msadabwe said the reopening of the radiotherapy unit would significantly improve access to treatment, allowing more patients to receive specialised cancer care within the country.

The hospital has also installed a new CT simulator to enhance the precision of radiotherapy planning, with a second CT simulator already being installed to expand capacity further. Chief radiation therapist Dr Ncheebe Sidaza said the simulator serves as the initial stage of treatment planning, allowing clinicians to map tumours accurately before patients begin therapy on the hospital’s linear accelerators

World.title: Mundubile launches public campaign funding appeal
World.content:
Opposition presidential candidate Brian Mundubile has launched a public fundraising drive for his campaign, inviting ordinary Zambians to bankroll his bid for the presidency with the national vote fast approaching.

The National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity leader announced the initiative in a Facebook post on Saturday, describing it as a “people-driven campaign” and urging citizens to make voluntary contributions towards party activities.

The move places Mundubile’s financing strategy in the same category as that once associated with constitutional lawyer John Sangwa, who built his Movement for National Renewal candidacy around the same citizen-funded model before withdrawing from the race earlier this year, citing registration delays and fears among supporters over the traceability of contributions.

Mundubile disclosed no fundraising target and gave no indication of how contributions would be collected or accounted for. The post directed supporters to a newly launched campaign support platform.

The NRPUP candidate paired the appeal with a policy pledge, promising to revise school grants upwards once he forms government. He offered no detail on the scale of the proposed increase or its funding source.

UPND supporters have moved swiftly to criticise the fundraising appeal on social media, framing it as evidence of a struggling campaign. The mockery, however, sits awkwardly against President Hakainde Hichilema’s own fundraising history. In September 2015, ahead of the 2016 election, Hichilema publicly promoted a donation platform, HH-Zambia.com, urging supporters to “spread the word” that his campaign could now receive donations. He renewed the approach in 2021, running a GoFundMe page titled “Hakainde Hichilema-2021 Presidential Fundraiser,” which accepted small individual donations processed through the platform.

Both fundraising drives were run openly and publicly, mirroring the model Mundubile has now adopted.

The announcement lands at a sensitive point in the campaign calendar. With voters set to head to the polls within days, presidential candidates typically shift from broad policy messaging to logistics-heavy final pushes covering transport, rally costs and get-out-the-vote operations, all of which require sustained cash flow.

The NRPUP has campaigned on a platform of national reconciliation and unity, with Mundubile and running mate Makebi Zulu positioning themselves as the primary challenge to Hichilema.

The party has in recent days gained momentum from defections, including former Ngambela Clement Sinyinda, who publicly endorsed the Mundubile-Zulu ticket after withdrawing his support for Hichilema.

Presidential campaigns in Zambia require substantial resources for provincial travel, rally logistics, campaign materials and volunteer coordination, particularly given the country’s geographic spread and infrastructure challenges.

Crowdfunding as a campaign financing model carries both advantages and risks. Supporters argue it strengthens grassroots ownership and reduces dependence on a small number of wealthy backers who might expect political favours in return. Sangwa’s own experience with the model illustrates the risks, as his campaign ultimately stalled partly over difficulties raising funds through the same approach.

Whether Mundubile’s version can generate sufficient resources to compete with better-resourced rivals in the campaign’s closing days remains an open question, particularly in a race already shaping up to be tightly contested.

The NRPUP has not indicated whether it will publish regular updates on funds raised, or whether the platform will remain open through to polling day.

World.title: Copper Queens’ quarterfinal hopes dented after loss to Nigeria
World.content:
The Copper Queens have complicated their chances of advancing to the quarterfinals of the 2026 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) after suffering a 1-0 defeat to defending champions Nigeria on Saturday night.

A win for Zambia at Al Madina Stadium would have seen them progress to the last eight with a game to spare.

Instead, Asisat Oshoala’s early strike condemned Bruce Mwape’s former side to their first loss of the tournament.

Oshoala scored in the 8th minute to give the Super Falcons the lead.

Nigeria, who had lost their opener to debutants Malawi, held on until the final whistle to revive their own qualification hopes.

It was a disappointing display for Zambia, who had kicked off the tournament with a dominant 6-0 win over Egypt last Tuesday.

The result has seen the Copper Queens drop from top of Group C to third, remaining on three points.

In the other Group C match played earlier on Saturday, Malawi secured a 3-1 victory over Egypt to book their place in the quarterfinals.

Zambia now face a must-win final group game against Malawi next Wednesday at Al Madina Stadium in Rabat to keep their knockout stage ambitions alive.

The top four semi-finalists at WAFCON will earn automatic qualification to the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup in Brazil.

The Copper Queens are aiming to better their bronze medal finish at the 2022 WAFCON, won under the late coach Bruce Mwape.

World.title: Inclusive electoral process, flourishes democracy-ECZ
World.content:
The Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) says it recognises that an inclusive electoral process is the cornerstone of a thriving democracy.

Speaking during the ECZ Women’s Conference held at Ndola Skills Training Centre in Ndola today, Copperbelt Provincial Electoral Officer, Shaft Musaka, said women are not just participants in elections, but decision-makers, advocates and architects of a brighter future.

Mr Musaka said the Commission has deliberately implemented policies aimed at empowering women at every stage of the electoral process.

“We have strengthened voter education programmes specifically tailored to address barriers that hinder women’s full participation in elections,” he said.

Mr Musaka said the Commission is also actively promoting women’s representation in electoral administration to ensure their voices are heard, valued and integrated into decision-making structures.

He added that the ECZ continues to champion safe, peaceful and fair elections that are free from intimidation and discrimination, enabling women to vote and contest leadership positions with confidence.

Mr Musaka explained that empowering women requires collective action and collaboration, adding that the Commission is working with communities, organisations and other stakeholders to amplify women’s voices, promote civic engagement, and encourage more women to stand as candidates, election observers and advocates for peaceful and credible elections.

“As we embrace this commitment, let us remind ourselves that peace is not just the absence of conflict; it is the presence of justice, equity and opportunity,” he said.

Mr Musaka urged women in Ndola and across the country to actively participate in shaping Zambia’s democratic future.

“Let this Women’s Conference be a call to action for every woman in Ndola and beyond to rise, participate and shape the future of Zambia’s democracy,” he said.

World.title: Hichilema completes ten-province tour amid Kaingu row
World.content:
Hichilema completes ten-province tour with Western Province pledges as independent candidate Kaingu accuses him of overreach

President Hakainde Hichilema has concluded a nationwide community outreach campaign by pledging a sweep of infrastructure and economic projects for Western Province, becoming the first presidential candidate in the 2026 general election to campaign in all ten provinces. But the closing leg of his tour has also drawn sharp criticism after he urged voters in Mwandi not to support independent parliamentary candidate Iris Kaingu, prompting accusations that he overstepped his role as head of state.

Speaking during engagements in Shang’ombo, Nalolo, Limulunga and Senanga, President Hichilema said his government’s focus for Western Province would be on infrastructure and economic projects that create jobs, improve livelihoods and strengthen cross-border trade with Angola. He told supporters in Shang’ombo that the district’s strategic location and natural resources gave it the potential to become one of Zambia’s most prosperous border towns.

“I see the potential of developing Shang’ombo into a very successful town. We are going to improve the border post so that people trade well with Angola and some of you will be employed there,” he said.

He announced plans to establish an abattoir in the district to allow livestock farmers to process beef locally for export, expand agricultural production to boost food security, improve telecommunications through additional mobile towers, modernise the Shang’ombo airstrip, construct a new market with reliable water supply, establish more boarding secondary schools and build a skills training centre for young people. He also pledged to rehabilitate the Shang’ombo-Rivungo canal through construction of a harbour and related facilities.

The President said the creation of a second constituency in Shang’ombo had already increased Constituency Development Fund allocations from K40 million to K80 million, allowing for faster investment in schools, health facilities, feeder roads and water projects. He said upgrading the Sioma-Shang’ombo road remained a priority.

In Nalolo, he said economic growth would be driven by expanded agricultural productivity, timely Farmer Input Support Programme payments through mobile money platforms, and improved road networks. He pledged to improve mobile network coverage, construct a district hospital, complete government offices and staff houses, and recruit more teachers and health workers.

In Limulunga, President Hichilema said Western Province had enormous untapped potential and announced plans to establish a milk-processing plant, expand fisheries into a commercial enterprise, complete Lewanika University, upgrade Mongu Airport into an international facility, and advance plans for the proposed Sioma Hydro-power Station.

“The upgrading of the Mongu airport is starting soon and we will continue to develop for our people. Running a country is not a joke, one must have the love for the people,” he said.

UPND Liuwa parliamentary candidate and former Finance and National Planning Minister Situmbeko Musokotwane said President Hichilema had demonstrated commitment to Western Province through continued investment in infrastructure and social programmes, and urged residents to support UPND to ensure development programmes continue.

In Senanga, the President apologised for arriving late due to a demanding schedule and appealed to voters to support UPND, saying this would ensure continuity of programmes including free education. He said upgrading the Senanga-Maata road remained a key priority.

The engagements marked the conclusion of the President’s nationwide community outreach programme, which he began earlier in the campaign season and which took him to all ten provinces ahead of the 13 August vote.

However, the tour’s final stretch has been overshadowed by controversy following remarks President Hichilema made in Mwandi on Thursday, where he urged residents not to vote for Iris Kaingu, an aspiring independent parliamentary candidate, because she defied his advice not to contest outside the UPND.

Kaingu, reacting to the remarks, said Zambians have the right to choose the person they want to vote for and should not be forced to support a candidate they do not want. She said she was shocked that the Head of State would attack her in such a manner when she was merely exercising her democratic right to contest as an independent.

“I cannot believe the president came all the way to de-campaign me even when the people of Mwandi have clearly indicated that they do not want the UPND candidate,” she said.

Kaingu also pushed back on the suggestion that Western Province remains loyal UPND territory, arguing that the party’s traditional support base in the province has been eroded by continued underdevelopment.

“If Western Province is UPND’s bedroom, then it is a dirty bedroom, because the people in the province are now suffering, as infrastructure is in a deplorable state,” she said.

Movement for Multi-Party Democracy national secretary Lumba Kalumba condemned the President’s remarks as an affront to democracy, saying that calling an adult woman a “difficult child” and labelling her difficult for refusing to obey was not mere rhetoric but language of subordination.

“It frames her as disrespectful for making independent choices. It reinforces the idea that women in politics must be compliant, not assertive; obedient, not ambitious. A democratic President does not dictate who may or may not stand. He does not use state and party platforms to bully opponents, especially women. He competes on issues, not on intimidation,” Kalumba said in a statement.

She said labelling a woman a “difficult child” set a dangerous precedent for Zambian democracy. “This is not strong leadership. It is an infringement on women’s rights, democratic rights, and the basic principles of a free and fair election,” Kalumba said.

The controversy has also drawn editorial criticism. An opinion piece published this week argued that the remarks in Mwandi sit uneasily alongside the President’s repeated declarations of commitment to increasing women’s participation in leadership, noting that the Constitution expressly recognises independent candidates as a legitimate category of contestant, not a violation of party loyalty.

President Hichilema‘s tour of Western Province, and the broader ten-province outreach it capped, has been framed by his campaign as evidence of a leader personally engaged with every corner of the country ahead of polling day. But the Mwandi remarks have instead become the dominant talking point in the campaign’s closing fortnight, with critics arguing that a sitting president using his platform to campaign against an independent candidate raises questions about the boundaries between incumbency and electoral fairness that voters will now weigh alongside the infrastructure pledges themselves
