World.title: Delhi HC transfers special judge assigned to paper leak cases a week after taking charge
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The

has transferred Special Judge Anu Grover Baliga, who was appointed last month to head the designated fast-track court for paper leak cases, as part of a reshuffle involving 138 judicial officers.

Judge Baliga was appointed after the Delhi High Court, on July 23, designated a special court to hear criminal cases related to paper leaks and other unfair practices in public examinations, as cited by PTI.

Baliga had spent just over a week at the designated paper leak court after assuming charge on July 25. Special Judge Ajay Gupta, who had earlier been hearing paper leak cases, including the NEET matter, will replace her.

The High Court also appointed Special Judges Vikas Dhull, Prashant Sharma, Pulastya Pramachala, Kiran Bansal and Amit Bansal to NIA courts dealing with terror cases.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi had announced the setting up of fast-track courts to ensure the swift disposal of cases related to paper leaks.

World.title: 'Drugs part of enemy nations' terror plan to hurt India': PM Modi during 'Nasha Mukt Yuva' launch - top quotes
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday launched the 'Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan', calling on the country's youth to stay physically and mentally fit and remain away from drug abuse.

He said achieving the goal of a developed India requires a healthy, confident and drug-free younger generation. During his address, PM Modi also highlighed how the drugs affect one's family and career.

Launching the campaign through video conferencing, PM Modi said the initiative is not only for individuals, families and society but also for the nation. He added that the next 100 Sundays would represent 100 strong steps towards a drug-free India.

"Next 100 Sundays will mark 100 strong steps towards drug-free India," he said.

PM Modi also warned that drug trafficking was part of a larger strategy by hostile forces to weaken India and called for greater public vigilance. "Hurting India's interests by supplying drugs part of enemy nations' terror plan," he said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Here are the top quotes from his address:

Youth must stay fit for developed India

"Today, all countrymen have come together for a great and important resolve. The campaign we are witnessing is meant for individuals, families and society, but above all, it is for the nation. The campaign, 'Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat', clearly reflects this resolve. As the country moves towards the goal of a developed India, it is essential that our youth remain physically and mentally healthy and stay away from drugs and other such harmful substances."

"The campaign we are witnessing today is for the individual, the family, and society; above all, it is for the nation. The very name of this movementâthe 'Drug-Free Youth' initiative under the Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan â clarifies its resolve. As the nation sets its sights on becoming a Viksit Bharat, it is essential that our youth be healthy in body and mind, brimming with self-confidence, and forever free from the deadly habit of drugs. This is the objective of the campaign... This campaign was launched last year as a pilot project from Kashi... Over 125 spiritual organizations have joined us today for the welfare of crores of our fellow citizens."

"By being addiction-free, you need to protect your potential. You need to be aware that drugs get you high for a short time, but take your career and family to a new low/bottom.

From Varanasi to nationwide campaign

"As the MP from Kashi, I am happy that this campaign was launched last year from the sacred land of Kashi as a pilot project. Along with scientific clarity, it also carries spiritual energy. Social organisations and NGOs have joined this initiative for the welfare of crores of Indians. Together, they have prepared a roadmap through the Kashi Declaration. Today, we are witnessing how the welfare-oriented idea that emerged from Kashi has become a national project. From today, the Nasha Mukt Yuva campaign is being launched across the country."

"The 'Nasha Mukta Yuva Abhiyaan' is launching across the country today... There is immense power in collective action, and today, driven by that very strength, this campaign is set to touch the heart of every young person. Lakhs of youths across the nation took a pledge to stay free from drugs... The pledge taken today will continue to move forward steadily over the next hundred weeks."

"Drug use disturbs focus, takes you away from dreams. If a youth gets addicted to drugs, his aspirations take a hit, family gets shattered."

Govt's anti-drug drive and national campaign

Strict action is being taken in the country against drug traffickers and drug abuse; there have been many times more arrests compared to before, and drugs worth thousands of crores of rupees have been seized. "Today, thousands of students from schools, colleges and universities are connected online to this programme. Even lakhs of volunteers of MY Bharat are also connected. The NSS jawans too have joined us. People from different sectors, institutions and backgrounds--more than 1 crore youths are together today. I congratulate all of you for this big movement."

Youth key to Viksit Bharat, drugs part of enemy agenda

"You are India's Amrit Peedhi. You will shape your lives over the next 20-25 years, and you will lead the country to the goal of a Viksit Bharat in 2047, and you will be at the helm. You will be the ones to reap its full benefits."

"The country needs your energy, your imagination, and your talent, so staying drug-free is crucial for the country and for your own lives."

Profiting from the supply of drugs while aiming to destroy a country like ours is part of their terror-driven agenda."

Parents, teachers and society must lead the fight

"Make efforts to free your child from addiction with medical help."

World.title: 'Dismantle terror infrastructure first': India's US envoy hits out at Pakistan over Indus Waters Treaty
World.content:
Indiaâs envoy to the US, Vinay Mohan Kwatra said Pakistan had eroded the foundation of the

over the past five decades. He added that Islamabad had âdismantledâ the goodwill and friendship that underpinned the 1960 agreement, and that New Delhiâs decision to keep the treaty in abeyance merely acknowledged that reality.

As reported by US' Newsweek magazine, Kwatra said the treatyâs preamble reflected a commitment made 'in a spirit of goodwill and friendship', but Pakistanâs conduct had weakened that foundation over half a century.

âIt is worth remembering that the treaty's preamble declares it was concluded âin a spirit of goodwill and friendshipâ. Pakistan spent half a century dismantling that goodwill and friendship. The abeyance merely acknowledges what Pakistan's conduct had already destroyed,â Kwatra said.

His remarks came after Pakistan recently hosted a conference protesting Indiaâs decision to keep the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) in abeyance on April 23 last year, a day after Pakistan-trained terrorists killed 26 people in Pahalgam, Jammu and Kashmir.

The IWT, signed by India and Pakistan in 1960, divided the waters of the six rivers of the Indus basin between the two countries. India was given control over the eastern rivers, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej which account for about 20 per cent of the basinâs water, while Pakistan received rights over the western rivers Indus, Jhelum and Chenab carrying around 80 per cent.





âThat asymmetry stifled development for decades in Indian regions that could have benefited from better water rights. India honoured the treaty anyway,â Kwatra said according to Newsweek.

The envoy said Pakistanâs approach towards India had been marked by wars, hostility and cross-border terrorism, citing the 1965, 1971 and 1999 conflicts along with major terror attacks, including the 2001 Parliament attack, the 2008 Mumbai attacks, the 2016 Uri and Pathankot attacks, the 2019 Pulwama attack and the 2025 Pahalgam attack.

Kwatra also said that if Pakistan sincerely wanted Indiaâs cooperation on bilateral issues, it must first dismantle the terror infrastructure it has built over the years.

On implementation of the treaty, Kwatra alleged that Pakistan had repeatedly delayed Indian projects and opposed efforts to revisit the agreement in view of changing technology and requirements.

âPakistan also consistently blocked India's initiatives to renegotiate the treaty in light of six decades of technological change, which would have let India develop its hydropower potential,â Kwatra added.

âBit by bit, Pakistan eroded India's faith that it could exercise its rights under the treaty, or hope for a better one suited to today's realities,â he said.

Responding to calls for India and Pakistan to resume talks, Kwatra said past initiatives had failed to address core concerns.

Water and blood cannot flow together',â Kwatra said.

Kwatra also said Pakistan should focus on improving its own water management instead of blaming India for its challenges.

"The Government of Pakistan would do better to fix its dismal water productivity, than to stage conferences blaming India and issuing threats,â he said, adding, âThe habit of pinning every domestic failure on India has grown old."

World.title: Culture can slow ageing, says study
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Want to age more slowly? The answer may lie not just in exercise and diet, but also in a trip to the theatre, museum or even the cinema.

A new study by Japanese researchers has found that older adults who engage more frequently in cultural activities tend to have a lower physiological ageâa measure of how well the body's organs and systems are functioningâthan their actual age, suggesting cultural engagement may be an overlooked tool for healthy ageing.

Researchers from the Institute of Science Tokyo analysed 4,207 observations from 1,899 adults aged 50 years and above in the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing. Participants who more frequently visited cinemas, museums, art galleries, theatres, concerts or the opera had lower physiological age. Every one-point increase in cultural engagement score was associated with a 0.085-year reduction in physiological age, even after adjusting for income, health status, employment, smoking, physical activity and other factors.

The association persisted in a four-year follow-up analysis. Physiological age, estimated using 10 markers including blood pressure, lung function, grip strength, walking speed, BMI, haemoglobin, cholesterol and blood sugar, is considered a better predictor of disease and mortality than chronological age.

The researchers said cultural engagement may promote healthy ageing by strengthening social connections, reducing loneliness and stress, improving mental well-being and encouraging healthier lifestyles.





Indian experts said the findings reinforce the importance of staying socially engaged as people age.

Dr Prasun Chatterjee, Group Clinical Lead, Department of Geriatric Medicine and Longevity Sciences, Apollo Hospitals, and former professor at AIIMS, said the findings reinforce that healthy ageing depends not only on diet and exercise but also on social and cultural engagement. Social interaction improves memory and mood by boosting serotonin and dopamine, enhancing emotional well-being, memory and a sense of purpose, which encourage healthier lifestyles.

In the Indian context, he said, activities such as visiting parks, cinemas, theatres or places of worship can provide similar benefits by promoting happiness, social connection and purpose.

Prof Rajesh Sagar, psychiatrist at AIIMS, New Delhi, said social and cultural engagement promotes healthy ageing by strengthening emotional support networks, improving cognitive function and reducing chronic stress.

World.title: Veteran mountaineer Purja’s body found three days after avalanche on Broad Peak in PoK
World.content:
The body of veteran Nepalese-British mountaineer Nirmal Purja was found on Sunday (August 2, 2026), three days after he and nine fellow climbers were swept away in an avalanche on Broad Peak, located in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir’s Gilgit-Baltistan.

Also read | Who is Nirmal Purja, renowned Nepalese climber killed in Pakistan avalanche?

The Alpine Club of Pakistan (ACP) said the 43-year-old mountaineer’s body was found at an altitude of around 5,700 metres.

So far, the bodies of five climbers have been recovered, and efforts are underway to locate the remaining five, it said.

"The ground rescue team has reached Nirmal Purja ‘Nims Dai’ at approximately 5,700m on Broad Peak, where three additional bodies have also been sighted, though their identities remain unconfirmed,” the ACP said.

The ground team will bring the bodies down to the Japanese camp, it said, adding that recovery efforts continue under extremely difficult terrain conditions.

The ACP said the mountain’s terrain, risk of avalanches and steep slopes are posing challenges in rescue efforts as helicopters could not be employed due to the weather conditions.

Purja and the other climbers — five from Nepal, one Pakistani, one Omani, one American and one Chinese — were on Thursday (July 30, 2026) swept away by the avalanche that struck Broad Peak, located in the Karakoram range near K2.

It is the world's 12th-highest mountain and is considered one of the most challenging peaks to climb.

On Saturday (August 1), Purja's expedition enterprise — Elite Exped — announced that all members of the group had died.

Four of the ten bodies were recovered on Friday (July 31), three of them identified as Oman's Nadhira Ahmed Abdullah Al Harthy, Nepal's Pur Bahadur Gurung and American Mallory Geis, according to ACP President Major General Irfan Arshad. The bodies were airlifted to Skardu, a city in Gilgit-Baltistan.

Purja had an illustrious mountaineering career. He had successfully climbed all 14 peaks above 8,000 metres around the world in just six months and six days, setting a new record in 2019. He was about to complete his mission of climbing all 14 eight-thousanders twice after completing Broad Peak.

World.title: Israeli strikes kill nine in Gaza, Israeli Minister says no deal to halt attacks
World.content:
Israeli airstrikes continued in Gaza for a second straight day on Sunday (August 2, 2026), killing at ‌least nine Palestinians, despite U.S. President Donald Trump’s announcement of a breakthrough in ​efforts to implement last year’s Gaza ceasefire agreement.

Israeli Energy Minister Eli Cohen ⁠said on Sunday (August 2, 2026) that there was no deal to halt attacks on Gaza and that he saw a need for Israel, which already controls 70% of the Strip, to take full control of it.

Mr. Cohen is a ‌member of Prime Minister Netanyahu’s security cabinet, a small circle of Ministers that oversees security and diplomatic policy.

Palestinian health officials said Israeli warplanes carried out separate strikes ‌across the enclave in the northern Gaza City, the central city of Deir al-Balah, and ‌the ⁠southern area of Khan Younis.

A man and his wife were killed and four ⁠people were wounded in an airstrike on an apartment in Deir al-Balah, while two more people, including a child, were killed in a strike on an apartment in Gaza City, medics said.

A father, mother, and their 9-year-old son ​were killed around dawn after a strike ‌on a house in the Mawasi area of Khan Younis. Another person was killed near Jabalia in northern Gaza.

The Israeli military said the strikes in Deir al-Balah were targeting two commanders of Hamas’ elite “Nukhba” force. The Gaza City and Jabalia strikes also targeted “military operatives” but ‌the military was still reviewing the situation, it said.

At least 1,230 Palestinians have been ​killed in Israeli strikes since a ceasefire was reached in October.

Mr. Trump said on Thursday (July 30, 2026) there had been a breakthrough after Hamas agreed to disarm under ⁠a U.S.-backed initiative to implement the ceasefire agreement reached last year in Egypt.

Mr. Trump’s Board of Peace, the U.S.-led body overseeing the ceasefire, published on Friday (July 31, 2026) a 15-point roadmap setting out the final steps ‌for implementing the agreement.

Roadmap yet to be implemented

The roadmap has yet to be implemented. Hamas has said it will hand over its weapons for storage only after Israel halts military operations and withdraws its forces in line with last year’s agreement. An Israeli official told Reuters there would be no withdrawal from the military’s current positions unless Hamas undergoes “genuine disarmament”.

Mr. Cohen told Army Radio he did not believe Hamas would disarm, but that it would rather play games ‌and try to hide its weaponry.

Mr. Netanyahu has not commented publicly on the initiative, while National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir ​has called it unacceptable and said Israel should continue assassinating Hamas leaders. Former senior Fatah official Mohammed Dahlan, who is based in the United Arab Emirates, said in ⁠a Facebook post that Jared Kushner, Trump’s son-in-law and a senior adviser involved in the U.S. initiative, ⁠had told him he was working with the Israeli side to stop attacks on Gaza.

Mr. Dahlan said contacts with the U.S. were continuing to ensure the agreement was fully ‌implemented, adding that its success now depended on Israel fully ending its daily attacks on Gaza.

Reuters has reached out to the U.S. State Department for comment on Mr. Dahlan’s remarks. ​There was no immediate comment from Israel.

World.title: YouTube terminates Delhi slum-dweller’s page following overnight success, social media protests
World.content:
Social media has erupted with pleas from users asking YouTube India to restore the account of Mohammad Irfan, a resident of a Delhi slum, whose channel gained a substantial following overnight before being taken down by the video-hosting platform.

While YouTube has not yet issued any official clarification, attempts to access Mr. Irfan’s page, Main Irfan, display a message stating that “this account has been terminated for violating Google’s Terms of Service”.

Mr. Irfan also took to X, saying the termination was “some kind of mistake” and urging the platform to to rectify it.

“My channel was completely new, and I have honestly followed all of YouTube’s guidelines,” Mr. Irfan said in his post on X. “People really liked my content, which is why my subscribers increased. It seems like there was a mistake by your automatic system. Please review my channel again and restore it.”

Mr. Irfan’s channel found a vocal supporter in veteran journalist Ajit Anjum, who posted several times on X in support of the page while it was active, and after it was taken down.

“A young man named Mohammad Irfan, who lives in a slum in Delhi, started his YouTube channel just yesterday with our support,” Mr. Anjum posted on X on Sunday (August 2, 2026). “From yesterday evening until this morning, his channel gained more than 70,000 subscribers.”

“Suddenly this morning, his YouTube channel was terminated,” he added. “How did a working-class young man manage to gain so many subscribers in such a short time? That in itself is an extraordinary achievement. So why did YouTube terminate his channel so abruptly?,” the post said.

A young man named Mohammad Irfan, who lives in a slum in Delhi, started his YouTube channel just yesterday with our support. From yesterday evening until this morning, his channel gained more than 70,000 subscribers.

suddenly this morning, his YouTube channel was terminated.

How… https://t.co/AoQeeMKEog — Ajit Anjum (@ajitanjum) August 2, 2026

Several other social media users also posted in support of Mr. Irfan’s page, saying that the content and the channel were genuine, and that its termination was the result of a mistake by Google-owned YouTube’s automated systems. They urged the platform to rectify the issue.

World.title: Lt. Governor urges students to become ‘watchdogs’ of campuses in fight against drug abuse
World.content:
Puducherry Lieutenant Governor K. Kailashnathan on Sunday (August 2, 2026) urged students and youth volunteers to become “watchdogs and moral guardians” of their campuses in the fight against drug abuse, describing the menace as a “silent pandemic” that threatens India’s national security and its goal of becoming a developed nation by 2047.

Addressing students, faculty and My Bharat volunteers at the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan programme held at Pondicherry University, Mr. Kailashnathan said the campaign launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi was not a routine government scheme but a solemn national pledge and a mass people’s movement that required participation from every citizen.

A developed nation cannot be built on infrastructure and economic growth alone. He noted that roughly 40% of India’s population is aged between 15 and 35, calling this demographic the “engine” that will drive the country’s development.

“A Viksit Bharat is absolutely impossible without a Nasha Mukt Bharat,” he said, adding youth can contribute to nation-building only if they remain physically strong, mentally sound and emotionally resilient.

The Lt. Governor cautioned drug abuse was not merely a personal or family tragedy but a broader threat to India’s economic and security interests. He said resources meant for education, healthcare and infrastructure were increasingly being diverted to manage addiction-related crises, undermining the country’s ambition to become the world’s third-largest economy by 2030.

He further warned illicit proceeds from narcotics trafficking were being used to fund organised crime, anti-national activities and narco-terrorism, calling the issue a “direct and critical threat to national security.”

“The prevailing drug abuse in our country is tearing at the very fabric of our society. It almost always begins with a seemingly harmless experiment - a single instance of giving in to peer pressure or seeking a temporary escape from academic or personal stress. But this experiment transforms into a habit. Before the individual even realizes it, it degrades into a severe addiction,” he said.

He also spoke of the toll on families - citing parents who sacrifice their comforts to educate their children, only to see those dreams destroyed by addiction.

Mr. Kailashnathan appealed to the students to pledge to stay away from drugs and to intervene when they notice friends or roommates withdrawing or falling into bad company, urging them to use social media, debates and youth festivals to spread the anti-drug message

“Let Puducherry emerge as a shining beacon in this national campaign,” he said

Mr. Kailashnathan also administered the Nasha Mukt Yuva Pledge to the students.

Chief Minister N. Rangasamy, Pondicherry University Vice-Chancellor Prof. P. Prakash Babu, Chief Secretary Sharat Chauhan and officials participated.

World.title: Rain fury: 157 families shifted to 26 relief camps in Kozhikode
World.content:
As part of mitigating rain-related calamities, the District Disaster Management Authority (DDMA) has opened 26 relief camps in Kozhikode district. There are now 563 persons belonging to 157 families, including women and children, staying in these camps as part of the relief measures initiated with the support of the local administrators and the Revenue Department.

Also read | Kerala heavy rains updates on August 2, 2026

According to Revenue Department officials, the families have been temporarily shifted to the relief shelters opened in Vadakara, Thamarassery, Koyilandy and Kozhikode taluks, they said.

Arrangements are also in place to ensure emergency medical care for the camp members. The support of various voluntary organisations has also been ensured to meet the needs of the camp members.

“Though rainfall was moderate in the urban and rural areas on Sunday, the vigil would be continued in the wake of the rough weather alert. All taluk-level and village-level rescue squads were given instructions to stay alert,” said a senior Revenue Department official from Vadakara taluk. He said more families would be evacuated from various landslide-prone zones in the upland areas following the instructions of the DDMA.

Malabar River Festival cancelled

In view of the inclement weather conditions, organisers have cancelled all the events related to Malabar River Festival, the annual white-water kayaking competition held in the Iruvazhinji river in Kozhikode.

Earlier in the morning, district administration had put off the events for Sunday (August 2, 2026).

Water levels in the Iruvazhinji and Chali rivers have gone up considerably. Local residents have been barred from venturing to the banks of these rivers. Police, Fire and Rescue Services, have been deployed there. In an order, District Collector M.S. Madhavikutty has asked all the government departments to be on high alert.
